## RETRO-164 — FOLLOW-473 (fail-closed two-step auth on GET /api/adapt + /api/adapt/description — closes the highest-blast-radius fail-open + spoofable-`x-tenant-id` pair; recovered from an interrupted session with TWO divergent uncommitted worktree attempts) — 2026-07-08

### 1. Summary of change

- **PR:** #475 (merged 2026-07-08T19:03:53Z, commit `511fbbe`). Title: `fix(control-plane): fail-closed two-step auth on GET /api/adapt + description [FOLLOW-473]`. Coordination/QUEUE bookkeeping merged separately as PR #476 (commit `95c4b02`, 2026-07-08T19:04:20Z — QUEUE.md only, +44/-2, no code).
- **Files changed:** #475 = 21 files (+883 / -63). NEW shared helper `apps/control-plane/src/lib/adapt-get-auth.ts` (+92: `resolveAdaptGetAuth`, `AdaptGetAuthResult`). Both call sites `app/api/adapt/route.ts` (+32/-12: drop `getAuthClaims` import + presence-only `ADAPT_API_KEY` compare + `x-tenant-id ?? 'unknown'` fallback; add try/catch→Sentry→401 + `authResult` branch) and `app/api/adapt/description/route.ts` (+30/-12: same shape). NEW `route.follow473.test.ts` in both dirs (+263 / +258; 17 dedicated auth cases total) + updated `route.test.ts` in both (resolved-tenant behavior) + 8 sibling adapt suites touched (+7/+8 each: mock the new resolver). #476 = QUEUE.md only.
- **Modules touched:** control-plane ONLY (1 new lib + 2 API routes + tests). No SDK / ingest / decision-api / shared / Modal / db-migration / docs-of-record change. The helper mirrors the two-step auth already live on `POST /api/adapt/feedback` (ADR-0015 / FOLLOW-450), minus the HMAC body-signature step (GET has no body to sign).
- **Key contracts changed:** **No SDK↔API wire contract changed.** Real per-tenant SDK traffic sends `Authorization: Bearer ${config.apiKey}` (a real `api_keys` row) → resolves identically pre/post. Server-internal deltas only: (a) `x-tenant-id` is NO LONGER a tenant authority on either route (F-05 invariant now holds); (b) an unset `ADAPT_API_KEY` no longer fails OPEN (any non-empty bearer previously accepted → now 401 unless it matches a real key); (c) `ADAPT_API_KEY` set without `OPS_TENANT_ID` → 500 (parity with feedback). `AdaptGetAuthResult` is a control-plane-internal type, not exported cross-package.
- **Session provenance (process signal):** recovered from an interrupted session — the dispatched backend-engineer completed the full implementation but the terminal closed with the work UNCOMMITTED (nothing on origin, no PR). On recovery the coordinator found TWO divergent uncommitted FOLLOW-473 attempts in parallel worktrees (official: 325 adapt tests / 17 follow473 cases / thinner helper; fork: 309 tests / 14 cases / fatter self-contained helper), adjudicated by running both suites + verifying symmetric DB-throw handling, landed the more-covered official branch, discarded the fork, cleaned up both stranded worktrees.

### 2. Verification done in PR

- Test files changed: 2 new `route.follow473.test.ts` (+263/+258) + 2 updated `route.test.ts` + 8 sibling adapt suites (resolver-mock plumbing). · Assertions added: 17 dedicated auth cases — fail-closed 401 (missing/empty/unmatched bearer), ops-bypass 200 (ADAPT_API_KEY→OPS_TENANT_ID), misconfig 500 (ADAPT_API_KEY without OPS_TENANT_ID), spoofed `x-tenant-id` proven ignored (tenant taken from the KEY), DB-throw → 401 (Rule K.2 fail-loud). · Coverage delta: unknown (est. positive — two previously fail-open branches now asserted). Notably present: an explicit "resolver resolves a tenant → 200 with NO reliance on x-tenant-id / ADAPT_API_KEY presence" case in both `route.test.ts`.
- CI checks: real gates green per QUEUE #475 (typecheck + eslint + prettier + adapt suite 325 tests); standing `Rule I` baseline red is pre-existing/non-blocking (new symbols confirmed absent from `--log-failed` per PR #476 notes). This read-only retro did not re-watch CI — PM-attested per QUEUE.

### 3. Wiring Audit

`Wiring Audit — clean ✅` (for the PR's own surface).

- **CHECK A (dead code):** `resolveAdaptGetAuth` + `AdaptGetAuthResult` (`adapt-get-auth.ts`) each have ≥1 non-test importer — `app/api/adapt/route.ts:75` and `app/api/adapt/description/route.ts:58`. Not dead. The helper's own docstring carries the Rule-S call-site inventory (both siblings enumerated + "a third consumer MUST be appended here"), satisfying the RETRO-112 Rule-S amendment. Clean.
- **CHECK B (half-wire):** no NEW event / env-var / column / topic / SDK-signal introduced. The helper CONSUMES pre-existing env vars `ADAPT_API_KEY` + `OPS_TENANT_ID` — both already had producers (ops Doppler provisioning) and a prior consumer (`feedback/route.ts`). No new producer/consumer pair created here. Clean.
- **Cross-consumer grep (step 2) surfaced a PRE-EXISTING sibling dead-config in ANOTHER app** — `apps/decision-api/src/index.ts:35` declares `ADAPT_API_KEY` (docstring: "every request's Bearer token must match this value exactly … presence-only when absent") but NO code in the decision-api request path consumes it. Not introduced by this PR (control-plane-only diff); recorded in §4a LG-1 / §7 → FOLLOW-531. Flagged here because it is the direct sibling of the exact symbol this PR hardened.

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P2 — SIBLING-NOT-SWEPT, cross-app; the load-bearing correctness finding) — the `estalara-decision-api` Cloudflare Worker `POST /api/adapt` (`apps/decision-api/src/index.ts:84` → `handleAdaptRequest`) enforces NO bearer auth at all, and its declared `ADAPT_API_KEY` env var is a phantom (declared + documented, never consumed anywhere in `apps/decision-api/src`).** Grep: `grep -rn "ADAPT_API_KEY\|Authorization\|Bearer\|401" apps/decision-api/src --include=*.ts | grep -v test` returns only the Env-type declaration + outbound Bearers (llm-gateway, Upstash, schema-API) — zero inbound auth check. So this sibling of the two routes FOLLOW-473 just hardened is strictly WORSE (no gate, not merely fail-open). **Blast-radius bound:** deploy-staging.yml deploys decision-api only `--env staging` (`api-staging.estalara.io`); there is NO production deploy step, and the live SDK targets the control-plane (`admin.estalara.com/api`, per `packages/sdk/src/core/endpoint.ts`), NOT this Worker — so it is a staging-only, off-prod-path unauthenticated decision endpoint, hence P2 not P0. Its index.ts docstring ("presence-only auth is used" when absent) is stale/aspirational — no auth exists. → **FOLLOW-531** (enforce Rule-S two-step OR confirm CF-Access gating / decommission + remove the phantom env + fix the docstring).
- **LG-2 (P3 — ops-tenant env-var fragmentation across the auth family) — the "ops tenant" concept is spelled TWO different ways.** `resolveAdaptGetAuth` + `feedback/route.ts` read `OPS_TENANT_ID`; `crm/outcome/route.ts:172` + `quiz/completion/route.ts:120` read `ADAPT_TENANT_ID` for the identical ADAPT_API_KEY ops-bypass. An operator provisioning one name silently leaves the other family mis-scoped (500 on the ops path). Not a bug in THIS PR (it correctly matched feedback's `OPS_TENANT_ID`), but a real config-drift hazard the consumer map exposed. → **FOLLOW-533** (consolidate to one name or document the split as intentional in `.env.example`).

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught (P0/P1/P2)

- **None introduced.** N/A for defects. One INVERSION worth recording (not a bug): the new helper hardens the ops-key compare to constant-time `secretEquals(adaptApiKey, bearerToken)` (`adapt-get-auth.ts:72`), whereas the pattern it claims to "mirror" — `feedback/route.ts:305`, plus `crm/outcome:173` and `quiz/completion:121` — still uses a plain timing-unsafe `bearerToken === adaptApiKey`. The new code is BETTER than its own stated template; the consequence is that those three ops-bypass compares are now the stragglers on the timing-unsafe-secret-compare surface (RETRO-161 class). This folds into the EXISTING FOLLOW-522 (broaden the FOLLOW-484 grep-lint) — recommend its lint also flag `bearerToken === adaptApiKey`. No new number (would be ledger noise).

#### 4c. Test coverage gaps

- **TG-1 (P2 — the thinner-helper drift risk; the design-choice finding) — the fail-loud DB-throw contract lives OUTSIDE the shared helper as an unenforced caller obligation.** `resolveAdaptGetAuth` deliberately does NOT catch the `resolveApiKey` throw (Rule K.2) — its docstring says the caller "MUST wrap the call in try/catch, capture to Sentry, and fail loud (401)." Both routes currently do this identically, but each has its OWN try/catch + `Sentry.captureException(..., tags:{area:'adapt'|'description'})` + 401 construction, and NOTHING pins the two together. Each route's follow473 suite tests its own DB-throw→401 in isolation; there is no SHARED parity assertion. If a future edit drops or alters the try/catch on ONE route, `resolveApiKey`'s throw would surface as an unhandled 500 on that route only — a silent asymmetry the green CI on the untouched route would not reveal. The discarded fork (fatter, self-contained helper that owned the try/catch internally) would have made this drift structurally impossible; the adjudication correctly chose the more-tested branch but inherited this seam. → **FOLLOW-532** (add a shared symmetry test OR move the throw→Sentry→401 handling into the helper as a third `AdaptGetAuthResult` disposition).

#### 4d. Documentation gaps

- Folded into LG-1: `apps/decision-api/src/index.ts:32-33` docstring ("every request's Bearer token must match this value exactly … presence-only auth is used" when absent) describes auth that no longer (or never did) exist in the request path. → FOLLOW-531.

### 5. Cascading impact

#### 5a. Current sprint tickets affected

- **Sprint 22b hardening epic (the FOLLOW-449.. audit-remediation series this ticket belongs to):** FOLLOW-473 discharges the two highest-blast-radius fail-open routes. **FOLLOW-484 / FOLLOW-522 (fail-open + timing-unsafe grep-lint):** the decision-api LG-1 gap would NOT be caught by that lint (it is ABSENCE of a check, not a fail-open `if (secret && x !== secret)` shape) — a lint blind spot worth noting; the LG-2/§4b straggler compares WOULD be in FOLLOW-522's broadened scope.

#### 5b. Future sprint tickets affected

- **FOLLOW-510 (the source stub, DONE-folded):** its two ACs — "elevate FOLLOW-473 P2→P1" and "ADAPT_API_KEY provisioning preflight/confirmation" — are satisfied on the primary path (elevated; preflight noted: `OPS_TENANT_ID` absent in prod ⇒ ops branch 500s exactly as feedback already does, real api_keys traffic unaffected). Residual operator hop: provision `OPS_TENANT_ID` if the ops-bypass path is ever needed in prod.
- **FOLLOW-508 / FOLLOW-511 (existing decision-api two-plane stubs):** FOLLOW-531 (decision-api adapt-route auth) is adjacent to these — co-schedule so the Worker's whole auth posture (schema-API token + adapt-route bearer) is settled in one pass.

#### 5c. Contracts changed others rely on

- **None external.** SDK wire (`Bearer apiKey`) byte-identical; `AdaptGetAuthResult` control-plane-internal; no shared schema / `docs/INTERFACES.md` entry warranted. Verified the SDK targets control-plane, not the decision-api Worker (`packages/sdk/src/core/endpoint.ts` example `https://admin.estalara.com/api`), so the LG-1 sibling is genuinely off the live contract surface.

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

- **F-05 invariant (tenant is ALWAYS server-derived, never from a caller header) now holds on the two highest-traffic routes** — a meaningful hardening of the decision plane. The residual smell is the ops-tenant env-var fragmentation (LG-2): the "one ops tenant" architectural concept is realized under two names (`OPS_TENANT_ID` / `ADAPT_TENANT_ID`) across five auth surfaces, which will keep generating provisioning-drift findings until consolidated.

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern (SIBLING-NOT-SWEPT — a decision-grade auth surface is hardened on some siblings while an off-primary-path sibling in ANOTHER app is left un-hardened):** seen in — **RETRO-153** (fixed the copied fail-open route, left the ORIGINAL `/api/internal/schema` fail-open; HELD count 1) and **RETRO-164** (this — hardened the two control-plane GET adapt routes, left the `decision-api` Worker `/api/adapt` sibling with NO auth + phantom env). promote-threshold 2, **current count 2-across but only 1 PRIOR retro (RETRO-153).** **HELD — NO promotion.** The algorithm requires the pattern in ≥2 PRIOR retros; RETRO-153 is the sole prior and itself explicitly held SIBLING-NOT-SWEPT at count 1. Watch: a THIRD instance where a hardening leaves a same-class sibling unswept is the trigger. The actionable residual is already ticketed (FOLLOW-531) and partly covered by the Rule-K/Rule-J duplicate-surface family + the FOLLOW-522 lint.
- **Process pattern (STALLED-WORKER STRANDED-BUT-COMPLETE WORK — the RETRO-146/150/162/163 family, now 5th sighting):** FOLLOW-473's interrupted session left complete-but-uncommitted work in worktrees. The family has DELIBERATELY and repeatedly chosen the executable-checklist vehicle (`docs/AGENT_WORKFLOW.md` "Recovered-work re-verification", born of FOLLOW-448) + FOLLOW-527 (WIP auto-commit) + FOLLOW-530 (cache-bust) OVER a CONVENTIONS_PATCH prose rule ("a guard that executes beats a prose rule" — RETRO-146/150; restated RETRO-163 §6). **NO new prose rule** — promoting now would duplicate a working checklist and contradict accumulated reasoning. BUT this instance carries a GENUINELY NEW sub-shape the checklist does not cover (see §7/§9): **TWO divergent uncommitted attempts for the SAME ticket — a silent duplicate that the recovering coordinator had to adjudicate ad hoc.** The increment is a checklist AMENDMENT (like FOLLOW-530), not a prose rule → **FOLLOW-534.**

### 7. Prior-follow-up closure check (step 7)

- **FOLLOW-473 claims to close RETRO-158 / FOLLOW-510 (the reassess-and-fix stub).** End-to-end trace on the PRIMARY (live) path — CONNECTED, not moved one hop: SDK sends `Bearer ${config.apiKey}` (`packages/sdk/src/core/adapt.ts` → `admin.estalara.com/api/adapt`) → `resolveAdaptGetAuth(req, token)` → Step-2 `resolveApiKey(req)` → SHA-256(bearer) → `api_keys` row → real `tenantId` → threaded into the decision tree + attribution (`const tenantId = authResult.tenantId`). The two former gaps are eliminated AT the route boundary in code (proven by the two follow473 suites: unset-`ADAPT_API_KEY`+random-bearer → 401, and spoofed-`x-tenant-id` → tenant taken from the key), not relocated downstream WITHIN control-plane. Sweep confirms zero remaining `!== ADAPT_API_KEY` fail-open shapes and zero `x-tenant-id ?? …` fallback-authority shapes in non-test control-plane code; the `audit`/`config` routes that still read `x-tenant-id` are middleware-injected (`middleware.ts:311/336` `.set()` OVERWRITES any inbound value → not spoofable, FOLLOW-454 pattern).
- **BUT the CLASS closure is one-hop-incomplete at the CROSS-APP level:** the "close the fail-open ADAPT_API_KEY decision-route class" objective moved the gap from "two control-plane GET routes" to "one staging decision-api Worker route" (LG-1). This is exactly the fail mode step 7 exists to catch — the gap did not vanish, it hopped to a sibling app. Off the live path (staging-only, SDK doesn't target it) so P2, but recorded so a future retro doesn't read "ADAPT_API_KEY fail-open class fully closed" and stop. → FOLLOW-531.

### 8. Multi-axis / contradiction reconciliation (step 8)

- **Auth-branch axis (ops-bypass AND primary):** BOTH analyzed. Ops-bypass (Step 1): constant-time, scoped to `OPS_TENANT_ID`, misconfig→500 — cannot select a caller-supplied tenant. Primary (Step 2): SHA-256→api_keys→real tenant, 404-normalized-to-401 (no key-existence oracle). Fail-closed on both.
- **Route axis (adapt AND description):** BOTH call sites verified identical two-step + identical try/catch→Sentry→401 shape — currently symmetric; the residual is that symmetry is UNENFORCED (TG-1), not that it is presently broken.
- **Env-state axis (`ADAPT_API_KEY` set/unset × `OPS_TENANT_ID` set/unset):** all four combinations covered — unset key + real bearer → 401 (was fail-open); set key matching → ops tenant or 500; set key not-matching → falls to Step 2. Prod reality (key present, `OPS_TENANT_ID` absent) → ops path 500s exactly as feedback already does; real traffic uses Step 2, unaffected → no outage (reconciles the FAIL-CLOSED-HARDENING-IS-FAIL-DANGEROUS watch from RETRO-153 §6: here the primary path does NOT depend on the newly-required secret, so no live 401 regression).
- **Cross-app sibling axis:** analyzed — surfaced LG-1 (decision-api Worker). This is the axis the PR's own scope did not cover.
- **Contradiction with prior retros:** NONE. This EXTENDS RETRO-153's SIBLING-NOT-SWEPT (held count 1) with a second-app instance and RETRO-161's timing-unsafe-compare sweep (the ops `===` stragglers fold into FOLLOW-522). No prior "clean" verdict is overturned.

### 9. Follow-ups

- **FOLLOW-531 (P2, backend-engineer, ~2–3h)** — Sweep the SIBLING: the `estalara-decision-api` Worker `POST /api/adapt` (`apps/decision-api/src/index.ts` → `handleAdaptRequest`) enforces NO inbound bearer auth and its `ADAPT_API_KEY` env var is declared+documented but never consumed. Either (a) enforce the Rule-S two-step (or at minimum a constant-time `ADAPT_API_KEY` gate) so it matches the now-hardened control-plane GET routes, OR (b) confirm it is decommissioned / Cloudflare-Access-gated and remove the phantom `ADAPT_API_KEY` env + fix the stale "presence-only auth is used" docstring. Staging-only + off the live SDK path (SDK → control-plane), hence P2. Co-schedule with the existing decision-api two-plane stubs FOLLOW-508 / FOLLOW-511. Source: §3 / §4a LG-1 / §7.
- **FOLLOW-532 (P2, backend-engineer + qa-engineer, ~2h)** — Pin the two GET call sites against future drift (the thinner-helper seam): the fail-loud DB-throw contract (try/catch → `Sentry.captureException` → 401) lives OUTSIDE `resolveAdaptGetAuth` as an unenforced caller obligation, so an edit to one route's catch would silently 500 that route only. Either add a SHARED parity test asserting both `GET /api/adapt` and `GET /api/adapt/description` map a `resolveApiKey` throw to 401 + a Sentry capture identically, OR fold the throw-handling into the helper as a third `AdaptGetAuthResult` disposition (`{ok:false,status:401,dbError:true}`). Source: §4c TG-1.
- **FOLLOW-533 (P3, backend-engineer, ~1–2h)** — Consolidate the ops-tenant env var: `OPS_TENANT_ID` (adapt GET routes + feedback) vs `ADAPT_TENANT_ID` (crm/outcome + quiz/completion) name the SAME "ops tenant" concept, so provisioning one silently mis-scopes the other family. Pick one canonical name (alias the other for back-compat) OR document the split as intentional in `.env.example` with the exact route list under each. Source: §4a LG-2 / §5d.
- **FOLLOW-534 (P3, devops-engineer + pm-orchestrator, ~1h)** — Amend the `docs/AGENT_WORKFLOW.md` "Recovered-work re-verification" checklist to add a "scan-for-and-adjudicate-divergent-duplicate-worktrees" step: on resume, enumerate ALL worktrees/branches carrying uncommitted work for the ticket (not just the first found), and if >1 diverge, adjudicate by comparing test coverage + behavioral parity BEFORE landing one and discarding the rest. FOLLOW-473's recovery did exactly this ad hoc (325 vs 309 tests, symmetric-DB-throw check) but the checklist does not mandate it, so the next recovery could silently land the wrong fork or leave a diverged sibling worktree lurking. Same executable-checklist vehicle as FOLLOW-530 (NOT a prose rule), consistent with the RETRO-146/150 family reasoning. Source: §6 / §7 / retro provenance.

### 10. Cross-references

- **Related to RETRO-158 (FOLLOW-490) — the direct source.** FOLLOW-473 was surfaced by RETRO-158's F-13 sweep + FOLLOW-510's reassessment; this retro is its closure check — the primary path is closed end-to-end (§7), the cross-app sibling (decision-api) is the residual hop → FOLLOW-531.
- **Related to RETRO-153 (SIBLING-NOT-SWEPT, HELD count 1) — the governing pattern for §4a LG-1.** This is the second-app instance; still HELD (only 1 prior retro; ≥2-PRIOR bar unmet). Also inherits RETRO-153's FAIL-CLOSED-HARDENING-IS-FAIL-DANGEROUS watch — discharged here because the primary path doesn't depend on the newly-required secret (§8).
- **Related to RETRO-161 (FOLLOW-466) — the timing-unsafe-secret-compare sweep.** The new helper's constant-time ops compare leaves `feedback`/`crm/outcome`/`quiz/completion`'s plain `===` ops compares as the stragglers; folded into the existing FOLLOW-522 lint broadening (§4b), not a new number.
- **Related to ADR-0015 / FOLLOW-450 (feedback route two-step auth) — the reference pattern.** FOLLOW-473 mirrors it (minus HMAC); the mirror is imperfect in a GOOD direction (constant-time ops compare) — noted so a future retro reads the divergence as intentional hardening, not drift.
- **Related to RETRO-146 / RETRO-150 / RETRO-162 / RETRO-163 — the stalled-worker recovered-work family (now 5th sighting).** The family's executable-checklist vehicle held again; FOLLOW-534 extends it with the NEW divergent-duplicate-worktree adjudication sub-shape (first seen here), keeping the checklist-not-prose choice. FOLLOW-527 (WIP auto-commit) remains the residual crash-loss vehicle that would have prevented the strand entirely.

### 3. Wiring Audit

- **CHECK A (dead code):** clean. The one new symbol, `writeDescriptionGenerationAudit`, is module-private and called at `route.ts:198`. The new Zod field is consumed at `route.ts:203-205`. No new export, no orphan.
- **CHECK B (half-wire):** **HALF_WIRE_P (P1 classification) — `description_generations` now has a PRODUCER but NO in-repo CONSUMER.** File: `apps/control-plane/src/app/api/internal/description-cache/route.ts:325` (`INSERT INTO description_generations`). Grep evidence: `grep -rn "description_generations" --include=*.ts --include=*.py` → the ONLY code touch-points are this writer, the DSR module (which explicitly EXCLUDES it from erasure), and their tests. No reader endpoint, no provisioned Grafana dashboard (only a commented example query in migration 0007), no K.3 Internal Ops UI (MASTER_DESIGN §K.3/§2588 states the table "should be available in Internal Ops for per-tenant hallucination audit" — that surface does not exist in-repo). The audit trail is therefore **write-only** even once the grant lands: nothing reads the facts back. → **FOLLOW-536.** (Softened, not spurious: the design intent is a human-via-Grafana/Internal-Ops read, analogous to the write-mostly `dsr_audit_log`; hence the follow-up is filed P2, not P1 — but the wire is genuinely open and must be tracked.)
- **Half-wire (producer side) — the prod reachability leg:** the producer itself does NOT reach prod today (grant blocker, §4b BUG-1). Recorded here as the primary CHECK-B concern and correctly filed as an OPEN escalation.

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P2, NEW — the load-bearing new finding): `description_generations` has NO TTL / retention policy and now grows unbounded.** `infra/clickhouse/migrations/0007_description_generations_verified_facts.sql:20-22` — `ENGINE = MergeTree() PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(created_at) ORDER BY (tenant_id, listing_id, archetype, locale, created_at)` with **no `TTL` clause**. Before this PR the missing TTL was inert (zero writers). This PR makes it matter: every non-NEUTRAL generation appends a row, and rows are never deduped. Compare siblings — `events` has `TTL toDateTime(ts) + INTERVAL 13 MONTH` (0001:46), `intent_events` has a documented 90-day TTL (0014:34-37). `description_generations` has neither. **Compounding factor:** RETRO-163 §4a LG-1's model-toggle mutual-invalidation ping-pong (FOLLOW-528) re-dispatches a fresh Sonnet generation on every effective-model toggle — each of which now appends another audit row, so DEMO/model-switching traffic inflates this table fast. → **FOLLOW-535** (add a TTL migration, e.g. 13 months to match `events`, or a compliance-set window).
- **LG-2 (P3, NEW): pre-grant Sentry flood.** Because the write is fail-loud-but-non-blocking, EVERY successful FIT generation in prod will 403/497 `ACCESS_DENIED` and emit a `description_generations_write_failed` Sentry event until the grant lands (§4b BUG-1) — potentially one per generation, indefinitely. That is alert-fatigue on a P2 finding whose failure is expected-and-known. → **FOLLOW-538** (gate the CH write behind a flag until the grant lands, OR add a Sentry fingerprint/rate-limit so the known pre-grant window doesn't drown real signal).
- **LG-3 (P3, minor — noted, not filed): `generated_at` imprecision.** `writeDescriptionGenerationAudit` sets BOTH `generated_at` and `created_at` to callback-receipt time (`route.ts:308`), not the actual Modal generation time. For a hallucination audit trail the seconds-scale skew is acceptable; the Python job holds the true timestamp but does not forward it. Surgical-scope: left as a note, foldable into FOLLOW-535 if a schema touch happens anyway.

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught (P0/P1/P2)

- **BUG-1 (P1, prod-correctness, already-escalated — the go-live blocker): the prod `ingest_worker` CH grant was deliberately narrowed on 2026-06-29 to EXCLUDE `description_generations`, which this PR's writer re-requires.** `docs/runbooks/clickhouse-ingest-worker-grant-narrowing.md` (ESC-032/FOLLOW-424) lists the table as "none (no writer) — intentionally dropped" and the prod attestation confirmed `SELECT … FROM default.description_generations` → `ACCESS_DENIED` (497). The route writes with `CLICKHOUSE_USER`/`CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` (= `ingest_worker` in prod, same creds every control-plane CH sink uses — `route.ts:319-320`). Net: in prod, every insert 403s and the table stays EMPTY — F-17's actual goal (a durable audit trail) is silently NOT achieved, while CI/local are green. This is the RETRO-021 measured-in-fixture / not-reachable-in-prod shape, one hop further out (a permission grant, not a missing seed). **Correctly filed** as an OPEN escalation with the exact `GRANT INSERT ON default.description_generations TO ingest_worker;`. Verdict on the escalation: **accurate and sufficient** (names the grant, the runbook row to update, the Step-3 smoke re-run, and the impact). One addition folded into LG-2: it should also address the Sentry noise during the pre-grant window.

#### 4c. Test coverage gaps

- **TG-1 (P3): no test asserts the exact JSONEachRow ROW SHAPE matches migration-0007 column names/order end-to-end against a real (or ephemeral) ClickHouse.** The tests mock `fetch` and assert the JS object's keys; a drift between the object keys and the CH column set (e.g. a renamed column) would pass the mock but fail the real insert (Rule Z class — the assertion validates the shape THIS runtime emits, not the other side's contract). Low risk here (schema is stable, JSONEachRow tolerates key order), so noted, not filed; covered indirectly if FOLLOW-535's TTL migration adds an apply-time smoke.

#### 4d. Documentation gaps

- **DG-1 (P3, NEW — a live contradiction the writer activates): the audit inventory disagrees on whether `description_generations` is a DSR-erase target.** `apps/control-plane/src/lib/clickhouse-dsr.ts:44` lists it under "Tables intentionally NOT erased — listing-scoped, no session_id column." But `AUDIT_RISK_MATRIX.md:21` (risk #3, FOLLOW-039) and `AUDIT_TEST_GAPS.md:251` name `description_generations_verified_facts` as a table the erase route SHOULD hard-delete for Art.17. With zero writers this contradiction was moot; the new writer makes it live. Reconciliation + follow-up in §5d / FOLLOW-537.

### 5. Cascading impact

#### 5a. Current sprint tickets affected

- **ESC-032 / FOLLOW-424 (grant-narrowing runbook) — its premise is now FALSE.** The runbook's "Confirmed Table Access" row for `description_generations` ("none — no writer — intentionally dropped") must be corrected; the negative-control assertion (`SELECT` → `ACCESS_DENIED`) that the runbook treats as a health signal is now a false-positive-for-health. Tracked by the grant escalation; §7 keeps it OPEN.
- **RETRO-163 / FOLLOW-528 (model-toggle re-dispatch ping-pong)** — directly amplifies LG-1's row-growth; cross-referenced, no new dependency created.

#### 5b. Future sprint tickets affected

- **K.3 Internal Ops hallucination-audit UI (unbuilt, MASTER_DESIGN §K.3/§2588)** — this PR provides the write half; the read half (the whole point of the audit trail) is still unbuilt → FOLLOW-536. Any future K.3 ticket now has a populated source to read FROM (once the grant lands).

#### 5c. Contracts changed others rely on

- `POST /api/internal/description-cache` gained optional `verified_facts_used`. Only consumer is `generate_description.py` (grepped — no other caller). Additive + defaulted ⇒ no downstream breakage. Cross-runtime (Py producer → TS Zod consumer) tested on both sides on the shared `verified_facts_used` key; acceptable (Rule Z — neither side tests against the OTHER's canonical fixture, but the payload key + array-of-strings shape are mutually asserted; low risk, not flagged for remediation).

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

- **The "`description_generations` is non-PII, therefore DSR-exempt" assumption is CORRECT AS SHIPPED — but is a design tripwire.** Multi-axis check (the parent flagged a possible DSR/erasure obligation): the new row carries `tenant_id, listing_id, archetype, locale, tier, model, source, description_chars, verified_facts_used, {generated,created}_at`. There is **NO `session_id` / user / device identifier** and no way to single out a data subject — `verified_facts_used` are facts about the *property*, `archetype` is a listing-generation label, not a person. So the writer creates **NO new Art.17 erasure obligation**, and `clickhouse-dsr.ts:44`'s exclusion is right. **This RECONCILES the parent's hypothesis: the DSR axis was analyzed and is CLEAN, with evidence — no DSR gap.** The tripwire (→ §5d architectural note, tracked by FOLLOW-537): the moment anyone adds a `session_id`/buyer key to this table for *per-buyer* hallucination audit, it INSTANTLY becomes an Art.17 erase target AND must be appended to `DSR_CLICKHOUSE_TABLES` — and the stale `AUDIT_RISK_MATRIX.md#3` line that already (wrongly, today) lists it would then become right. That coupling must be documented so a future per-buyer-audit ticket doesn't silently ship a compliance hole.

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern (GRANT-NARROWED-THEN-REWIDENED): "a later PR adds a writer/reader to a resource whose prod access was DELIBERATELY narrowed/removed by an earlier scope-reduction on a 'no consumer exists' premise; CI/tests are green because they never exercise the narrowed prod grant, so the feature is dead-on-arrival in prod with zero local signal until an operator re-widens the grant."** — seen in: RETRO-165 (this, FOLLOW-463 / the CH grant). **Count 1 (fresh) — HELD, NO PROMOTION.** This is a cousin of, but distinct from: RETRO-021 (measured-in-fixture / missing-seed, not a deliberate prior narrowing) and the Modal-secret-never-provisioned cases (RETRO-152/156, FOLLOW-436/460 — a secret that NEVER existed, not one deliberately removed). No prior NUMBERED retro exhibits the "prior deliberate narrowing re-invalidated" shape, so the ≥2-prior bar is unmet. **Also — the broader operator-pending class is ALREADY codified as Rule AA**, which this ticket already honors (status `CODE_COMPLETE_OPERATOR_PENDING`, grant leg OPEN with a fail-loud proof step). So even the parent-class need is met; only this narrower sub-shape is new, and it is held at 1. Watch: a 2nd instance of "a prior deliberate access-narrowing invalidated by a later writer/reader" is count 2 → promote (candidate letter after AA).

- **FOLLOW-536** (backend/ml-engineer, P2, 3h): wire a reader for the audit trail (K.3 Internal Ops endpoint or provisioned Grafana dashboard) — close the HALF_WIRE_P.
- **FOLLOW-537** (compliance-engineer, P3, 2h): reconcile the DSR/audit-inventory contradiction — confirm `description_generations` non-PII, correct `AUDIT_RISK_MATRIX.md#3` / `AUDIT_TEST_GAPS.md`, and document the "add `session_id` ⇒ Art.17 erase target + append to `DSR_CLICKHOUSE_TABLES`" tripwire.
- **FOLLOW-538** (ml-engineer, P3, 1.5h): suppress the pre-grant Sentry flood (flag-gate the CH write until the grant lands, or fingerprint/rate-limit `description_generations_write_failed`).
- (Grant itself: already filed as the OPEN escalation in `backlog/ESCALATIONS.md` — no new FOLLOW; it is the operator leg, not a code follow-up.)

Rule AA already covers the status discipline, so no new rule is owed for the operator-pending aspect.

### 2. Verification done in PR

Assertions added: ~15. Coverage delta: unknown (net-positive; the round-trip is the load-bearing new coverage).

This is the in-repo (TS↔TS) analogue of a Rule-Z cross-runtime round-trip, and it closes the exact "the schema mirrors what the author THINKS the SDK emits" seam that would otherwise be the risk here. Belt-and-suspenders with the shared-side fixture test. **Strong.**
- CI checks: per QUEUE, merged green. This read-only retro did not re-watch CI; PM-attested per the CI-gate-landscape precedent (Rule I / Vercel / Python-test pre-existing-red non-blocking). Note the "Cross-language event contract" gate (RETRO-165 §2) is on the same `EVENT_TYPES` surface this PR grows — additive, so expected green (§5c).

### 3. Wiring Audit

**Not a strict half-wire — the wire connects END-TO-END to a generically-consumed sink; the residual is an observability-goal-not-fully-REALIZED gap (softer than RETRO-165), filed P3.**

- **CHECK A (dead code):** clean. The new file's 6 `*EventSchema` exports each have a non-test importer — `index.ts:97` `export *` + composition into the `EventSchema` union (`index.ts:191-196`). The 6 `*PayloadSchema` exports are consumed compositionally by their own event schemas. The inferred `type` exports are type-only ⇒ CHECK-A exempt. No orphan export, no dead file (the module is a schema-registration file wired into the canonical union).
- **CHECK B (half-wire — every new event has BOTH a producer AND a consumer):** all 6 new event types have a PRODUCER (SDK `adapt-description.ts`, all emit sites verified §4/§8) AND a CONSUMER: `apps/ingest/src/handlers/events.ts:210` now `safeParse`-ACCEPTS them (previously → `rejected[]`, the F-04 drop) → `validated[]` → `pushToClickHouse` (`events.ts:354`) → the canonical ClickHouse `events` table. That table is GENERICALLY consumed: `session_summary_mv` fires on every INSERT (`0002_create_session_summary_mv.sql:50`, `argMax(type,ts)` last-event + session bounds include these rows), `clickhouse-dsr.ts:317` erases them by `session_id`, and they are ad-hoc / Grafana queryable. So the producer→consumer wire is CONNECTED — **NOT HALF_WIRE_P.**
- **Residual (the real, softer finding):** NO purpose-built reader surfaces the F-04 GOAL — applied/skipped/error/reapply RATES. The type-filtered readers (`pilot/cta-lift`, `dashboard/analytics/lift`) whitelist `cta.clicked`/funnel types and do NOT read `adapt.description.*`; `session_summary_mv` counts `page.view`/`chat`/`inquiry` explicitly but folds these only into generic `last_event_type`/bounds. So description-adaptation observability is now QUERYABLE (ad-hoc SQL / Grafana) but not DASHBOARDED/aggregated. This is the same SHAPE as RETRO-165 §3 / FOLLOW-536 (accepted/written but no purpose-built reader) — **but materially softer** (the sink here is the heavily-read canonical `events` store, not a dedicated zero-reader table). → **FOLLOW-539** (P3). Reconciliation with RETRO-165's HALF_WIRE_P verdict is in §8.

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P3, the reconciliation-rot finding — the parent's Rule-H tension, assessed): the 23 producer-less "reserved" event types are correct to retain, but the "reserved (no producer yet)" category is NOT formalized anywhere a future audit/sweep will trust — so this exact reconciliation can silently rot.** `index.ts:124-197` annotates the union by category with ticket provenance (Master Design §C.1, TICKET-DQS-001, TICKET-AB-001, TICKET-041, TICKET-RUNTIME-FIX-003, FOLLOW-195, FOLLOW-266), which is good, but there is no single tracked list of "these N types intentionally have no SDK producer and WHY," and no Rule-H carve-out documenting the legitimacy of a registered-type-without-producer. Rule I (wired-or-dead) does NOT flag them (the schemas ARE imported into the union, so they have a non-test importer). But this PR itself is evidence the reconciliation rots: F-04 was a DIFFERENT rot on the SAME axis (a produced type with no registration → silent ingest reject), rediscovered by a manual audit, not a gate. The inverse (a registered type with no producer) is equally invisible to CI and equally re-litigable by the next audit or a cleanup that "removes unused schemas." The in-PR matrix is an ephemeral PR artifact; it does not survive into the repo. → **FOLLOW-540** (P3): enumerate the reserved/no-producer types with provenance in a tracked location (an `ADR-0003` amendment or a `RESERVED_EVENT_TYPES` doc-block) + a Rule-H carve-out note so audits/sweeps treat them as intentional.
- **LG-2 (P3, minor — volume, noted not separately filed): the two empty-payload convergence events `adapt.description.re` / `adapt.description.headline.re` fire once per framework-revert burst and are now durably stored raw with no aggregation.** On flicker-prone SvelteKit/React pages these are the highest-cardinality of the 6 (the `re`-apply loop, `adapt-description.ts:146` / `:194`); the `rafPending`/flag dedup caps them to one-per-burst but bursts recur per reconciliation. They ride the `events` table's 13-month TTL so growth is BOUNDED (§5d), but a raw-store-every-`re` posture inflates the table with a low-information signal. Fold the "sample/aggregate vs store-raw `re` events" decision into FOLLOW-539's scope. Low severity.

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern (ACCEPTED/STORED-BUT-NO-PURPOSE-BUILT-READER — the observability-goal-not-fully-realized shape): "a fix restores a produced signal to its store (un-drops it at the boundary) so it becomes QUERYABLE, but ships no aggregation/panel/materialized-view that surfaces the RATE the ticket's observability goal implied — the wire connects to a generic sink, the *insight* does not."** — seen in: **RETRO-165 §3 / FOLLOW-536** (`description_generations` write-only, a DEDICATED zero-reader table, count 1 PRIOR) + **RETRO-166** (this — `adapt.description.*` accepted+stored into the canonical `events` table, SOFTER, generically read). **Current = 2nd sighting, but only 1 PRIOR numbered retro exhibits it → ≥2-PRIOR bar UNMET. HELD, NO PROMOTION.** Two independent reasons to HOLD, named distinctly (per my own RETRO-165 lesson to name WHICH hold applies): (a) count — 1 prior, not 2; and (b) VEHICLE — the observability-family (RETRO-156/159/160/161/162 §6) has REPEATEDLY and deliberately ruled the correct vehicle is a per-surface follow-up, NOT a prose rule, because the family is heterogeneous; promoting now would contradict that accumulated reasoning. AND the two instances are non-identical in severity (dedicated-table-zero-readers is a genuine HALF_WIRE_P; canonical-table-no-panel is a P3 enhancement), so even the count is generous. Vehicle = FOLLOW-539. **Watch: a 3rd sighting where an "un-dropped/registered signal reaches a store but no reader realizes the stated observability" is the promotion trigger** — and note it may fold into the existing Rule-H half-wire family rather than warrant a new letter.

It cannot mask a real Cloudflare token (which is random and would never begin with the literal `AdaptDescriptionHeadline` prefix). No gap.

### 7. Prior-follow-up closure check (step 7)

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P2, NEW — the load-bearing finding): the two PROD operator legs are COUPLED, and applying them in the wrong order REOPENS the exact gap FOLLOW-535 closes in code.** FOLLOW-535's TTL takes effect in prod only when a CH admin applies migration 0020 (`infra/clickhouse/migrations/0020_...sql`). FOLLOW-463's writer takes effect in prod only when the same admin runs `GRANT INSERT ON default.description_generations TO ingest_worker;` (the OPEN escalation, `backlog/ESCALATIONS.md:24-58`). **If the operator lands the GRANT before/without 0020, the table resumes exactly the unbounded growth RETRO-165 §4a LG-1 flagged** (every non-NEUTRAL generation appends a never-expiring row, amplified by the FOLLOW-528 model-toggle re-dispatch). The PR body + `QUEUE.md:20-21,28` both correctly recommend BUNDLING the two legs (TTL before/with the grant), but that mitigation lives ONLY in ephemeral PR prose + the transient QUEUE start-here — it is NOT in the durable grant-narrowing runbook the operator will actually follow (`docs/runbooks/clickhouse-ingest-worker-grant-narrowing.md`, which still lists the table as "none — no writer — intentionally dropped"). The grant escalation is the OLDER, more-tracked item, so a grant-first application is the plausible default. → **FOLLOW-542** (durable runbook/migration-header sequencing note) + surfaced to the PM in §5a.
- **LG-2 (P2, NEW — a prod-precondition the local golden test masks): migration 0020 (`ALTER TABLE … MODIFY TTL`) requires the table to already EXIST in prod, i.e. migration 0007 to have been applied there.** ClickHouse does NOT auto-apply migrations, so unlike CI (where `ttl-golden-test.sh` and `migrate.sh` apply 0007 THEN 0020 to a throwaway container), the prod apply is a manual Cloud-console action against whatever DDL history the prod cluster actually has. If 0007 was never applied in prod, `ALTER TABLE description_generations MODIFY TTL …` fails with `Code 60 UNKNOWN_TABLE`. Weak positive evidence the table DOES exist in prod: the FOLLOW-424 grant-narrowing attestation's negative-control `SELECT … FROM default.description_generations` returned `ACCESS_DENIED` (Code 497) rather than `UNKNOWN_TABLE` (`ESCALATIONS.md:37`), and the runbook lists it as a known table row — but access-denied is not conclusive proof of existence, and I have no prod read access to confirm. The operator session must confirm 0007's table is present (or apply it first) before 0020. → folded into **FOLLOW-542** AC + surfaced in §5a.
- **LG-3 (P3, minor — noted, not filed): the 13-month value is a reasoned default, not a compliance round-trip, and that is CORRECT here.** The migration matches the `events` audit horizon (`0001_create_events.sql:46`) rather than `intent_events`' 90 days. Per RETRO-165 §5d the table is session-LESS / non-PII (facts about the *property*, not a data subject), so there is no GDPR-mandated retention to honor and no escalation was owed — the default is legitimate. Recorded so a future compliance pass does not re-litigate it as an un-reviewed guess. If anyone later adds a `session_id`/buyer key (the RETRO-165 §5d tripwire → FOLLOW-537), the retention choice must be revisited alongside the Art.17 obligation.

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught (P0/P1/P2)

- **N/A — no shipped bug.** Adversarial DDL checks passed: (a) TTL keyed on `toDateTime(created_at)` casts `DateTime64(3,'UTC')` down to `DateTime` for the TTL expression, mirroring `events` (`0001:46`) — correct. (b) PARTITION is `toYYYYMM(created_at)` and TTL is also keyed on `created_at`, so ClickHouse drops WHOLE expired parts efficiently (no per-row partial-part scan) — a positive, not a gap. (c) `MODIFY TTL` is idempotent on re-apply (overwrites with an identical expression) — safe under `migrate.sh`'s re-apply-every-file model. (d) migration number 0020 is strictly sequential (0019 was the prior max; `ls infra/clickhouse/migrations/` confirms no collision), so the Migration-journal-monotonicity gate stays green. (e) the golden test's `_assert_absent` correctly inspects executable SQL only (strips `^\s*--` comments) so the rationale header — which legitimately names the sibling durations `90 DAY` / `13 months` — does not trip a false failure.

#### 4c. Test coverage gaps

- **TG-1 (P3, note — not filed): the golden test proves the TTL CLAUSE is present in the applied schema, not that expiry BEHAVIOR fires.** `ttl-golden-test.sh`'s live check asserts `SHOW CREATE TABLE` contains `TTL toDateTime(created_at) + toIntervalMonth(13)` — it does not insert a >13-month-old row and assert a merge drops it. That behavioral leg is native ClickHouse TTL semantics (not this ticket's code) and a merge-timing assertion would be flaky, so this is an acceptable residual, not a gap to file. The shape-level guard is the right coverage for a DDL-only ticket.

#### 4d. Documentation gaps

- **DG-1 (P3, NEW): `docs/DATA_DICTIONARY.md`'s new retention row marks `description_generations` Status = "Enforced (0020)" — but in PROD the TTL is NOT enforced (operator-pending) and the table is not even receiving writes yet (the FOLLOW-463 grant is still blocked).** Every sibling row in that table is honestly `Pending` / `See migration 0011`; "Enforced (0020)" overstates prod reality — it is code-defined / CI-verified but prod-unapplied. This is the same CI-green-but-prod-not-reached shape RETRO-165 §4b BUG-1 flagged, now leaking into a doc's status column, and it is a miniature of the Rule-AA code-vs-prod axis split the retro process mandates. Honest status would read e.g. "Enforced in code (0020); prod apply operator-pending (bundle with FOLLOW-463 grant)". → **FOLLOW-541** (P3, correct the status wording + add a code-vs-prod distinction to the retention table's Status column convention).

### 5. Cascading impact

#### 5a. Current sprint tickets affected

- **FOLLOW-463 grant escalation (`ESCALATIONS.md:24`, OPEN) — now COUPLED, not merely adjacent (§4a LG-1).** The TTL apply and the `GRANT INSERT` are two DDL actions in the SAME prod CH Cloud-admin session, and their ORDER matters: TTL must land before/with the grant, or the first prod writes accumulate un-bounded until 0020 lands. **Surfaced to the PM (I do not write ESCALATIONS/QUEUE):** the existing OPEN grant escalation should be annotated so the operator applies migration 0020 in the same session and BEFORE running `GRANT INSERT`, and confirms migration 0007's table exists first (§4a LG-2). Severity: P2 prod-regression-window risk, mitigated only by ephemeral prose today.
- **RETRO-165 / FOLLOW-463 (CODE_COMPLETE_OPERATOR_PENDING):** this ticket does NOT unblock FOLLOW-463 — the grant is still the go-live gate. It makes the eventual go-live SAFE (bounded growth) IFF applied in the right order. No status change to FOLLOW-463.
- **RETRO-163 / FOLLOW-528 (model-toggle re-dispatch ping-pong):** its row-amplification is now BOUNDED in code (13-month horizon) — a positive resolution of RETRO-165's "compounding factor," realized once 0020 applies in prod.

A forward-looking note for FOLLOW-536's scope; no change owed here.

#### 5c. Contracts changed others rely on

- **N/A — no read/write contract changed.** A `TTL` clause is a storage-retention policy; it alters neither the table's column set, the `INSERT INTO description_generations FORMAT JSONEachRow` writer shape (`route.ts:329`), nor any reader (there is none — FOLLOW-536). No SDK/ingest/decision-api/Postgres/env surface touched. Zero downstream code fan-out.

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

- **"CI-and-local-green ⇒ the retention gap is closed" is FALSE for ClickHouse (Rule M / MEMORY).** The golden test + `migrate.sh` prove the TTL applies to a throwaway container; prod requires a manual Cloud-console apply because `ingest_worker` lacks DDL grant. This ticket is a clean Rule-AA case: code axis closed, prod axis open. Contrast the Postgres siblings (RETRO-162 migration 0033, RETRO-163) which auto-apply via `db-migrate.yml` (FOLLOW-308) with no operator hop — the store determines whether "merged" means "live."
- **The parent's explicit question — "is there risk from the TTL being DEFINED but not yet ENFORCED in prod? does any consumer assume the TTL is active?" — ANSWERED, and the answer bounds the risk to OPERATIONAL, not CORRECTNESS.** There is **no in-repo consumer of `description_generations` at all** — it is write-only (grep `description_generations --include=*.ts/*.py` → the writer, the DSR module that EXCLUDES it, and tests; RETRO-165 §3 / FOLLOW-536). No query filters on or assumes the 13-month horizon; no code path breaks if the TTL is absent. Therefore the TTL-defined-but-not-enforced state carries **zero correctness risk** — the ONLY exposure is the retention/growth window in §4a LG-1 (unbounded rows if the grant lands before 0020). This RECONCILES the parent's hypothesis: no consumer assumes the TTL active; the risk is purely the operator-sequencing growth window, which §4a LG-1 / FOLLOW-542 addresses.

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern (COUPLED-OPERATOR-LEGS — wrong-order reopens a closed gap): "a code fix closes gap X, but takes effect in prod ONLY when its operator leg is applied together with — and in the correct order relative to — a SEPARATE, already-open operator leg on the same resource; applying the other leg first REOPENS gap X, and the ordering mitigation lives only in ephemeral PR/QUEUE prose, not the durable runbook the operator follows."** — seen in: **RETRO-167 (this — apply-0020-TTL must precede/accompany the FOLLOW-463 `GRANT INSERT`, else unbounded growth resumes).** Count 1 (fresh). **HELD — NO PROMOTION.** Distinct from Rule AA (which is the code-vs-prod STATUS discipline for a SINGLE operator leg — this is the ORDERING/COUPLING of two legs) and from the RETRO-165 §6 "grant-narrowed-then-rewidened" candidate (which is about a prior deliberate narrowing invalidated by a later writer — still count 1, and NOT re-triggered here, since FOLLOW-535 adds no writer/reader and re-widens no grant). The actionable vehicle is a runbook note (FOLLOW-542), not prose. **Watch: a 2nd instance of two coupled prod operator legs whose wrong order reopens a closed gap is the promotion trigger** (candidate letter after AA).
- **Rule AA (CODE-VS-PROD-AXIS / operator-pending) — CONFORMING instance, POSITIVE, no re-promotion.** FOLLOW-535 lands `CODE_COMPLETE`, the QUEUE marks it operator-pending (`QUEUE.md:20`), the PR names the CH-admin apply step and the fail-safe (no in-repo consumer ⇒ no correctness break), and this retro keeps the prod-enforcement axis OPEN with a proof step (SHOW CREATE / runbook Step-3 smoke). Textbook Rule-AA discipline honored. The DG-1 "Enforced (0020)" doc wording is the ONE spot that violates the axis-split; FOLLOW-541 corrects it.
- **Net: NO rule promoted this retro.** The single fresh candidate (COUPLED-OPERATOR-LEGS) is count-1 with a follow-up as its correct vehicle; promotion would be the premature codification the ≥2-prior threshold guards against.

### 7. Prior-follow-up closure check (step 7)

- **FOLLOW-535 (chartered target — closes RETRO-165 §4a LG-1, the unbounded-growth finding): CLOSED IN CODE END-TO-END, prod-enforcement OPERATOR-PENDING — NOT declared fully closed, and the residual is NAMED, not relocated one hop.**
  - **Chain traced:** RETRO-165 §4a LG-1 (no TTL on the 0007 table, now written by FOLLOW-463) → FOLLOW-535 migration 0020 DEFINES `TTL toDateTime(created_at) + INTERVAL 13 MONTH` → `migrate.sh` applies it + `ttl-golden-test.sh` PROVES the clause is present in the live `SHOW CREATE TABLE` (CI) → **prod NOT applied** (ClickHouse no auto-apply; the ClickHouse engine, the "consumer" of the TTL DDL, never receives it until a CH admin runs it via the Cloud console). So `migration(producer) → engine part-drop(consumer) → expiry(effect)` is CONNECTED and proven in CI, and **OPEN in prod**.
  - **Honest verdict:** the retention gap is closed on the CODE axis (the migration exists, is idempotent, is CI-verified, and is durably documented). It is **NOT closed on the PROD axis** — and this retro does NOT paper over that: §4a LG-1/LG-2 and §5a keep the operator legs (apply 0020, in the right order, after confirming 0007) OPEN with the exact actions. The gap has NOT been quietly moved one hop into obscurity (contrast the FOLLOW-097→114→127→141 `inquiry_submit_selector` chain) — it is the SAME operator-pending shape already tracked under Rule AA + the FOLLOW-463 escalation, made explicit and coupled.

RETRO-014's golden-query-comparison test is cited as the MODEL for `ttl-golden-test.sh` (a pattern reference), not a closure.

### 8. Multi-axis / contradiction reconciliation (step 8)

- **Code axis vs prod axis:** code CLOSED (migration + CI golden test), prod OPERATOR-PENDING (Rule AA). The load-bearing split.
- **Producer(migration) vs consumer(engine) axis:** both analyzed — the DDL producer ships and is CI-proven; the prod engine-consumer is unreached until the operator applies 0020 (§7).
- **Operator-sequencing axis (both legs):** analyzed — apply-0020 and `GRANT INSERT` are COUPLED and order-dependent (§4a LG-1); wrong order reopens the growth gap. This is the axis a single-leg analysis would miss.
- **Table-existence / migration-dependency axis:** analyzed — 0020 (ALTER) depends on 0007 (CREATE) being present in prod; CI masks this by applying both to a fresh container (§4a LG-2).
- **Retention-VALUE axis:** analyzed — 13 months matches `events`, is non-PII / no compliance mandate (RETRO-165 §5d), a legitimate reasoned default (§4a LG-3), not an un-reviewed guess.
- **TTL-EXPRESSION + partition-key axis:** analyzed — `toDateTime(created_at)` cast + `created_at`-keyed PARTITION ⇒ efficient whole-part drops; idempotent `MODIFY TTL`; sequential migration number (§4b).
- **Consumer-assumes-TTL axis (the parent's explicit question):** analyzed and RECONCILED — there is NO in-repo consumer of the table (write-only, FOLLOW-536), so no code assumes the TTL active ⇒ zero correctness risk from the defined-not-enforced state; the only exposure is operational growth (§5d / §4a LG-1).
- **Contradiction with a prior retro — NONE; two prior "unbounded" characterizations UPDATED, not overturned.** RETRO-165 §4a LG-1 and RETRO-166 §5d/§10 both characterized `description_generations` as "unbounded (no TTL) → FOLLOW-535." This retro does not contradict them — it records that FOLLOW-535 now bounds the table IN CODE, while noting the characterization is not fully reconciled in PROD until 0020 applies. An update along the code axis, consistent with both priors; RETRO-166's deliberate CONTRAST (events-has-a-TTL vs description_generations-had-none) remains valid history and is now converging.

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern (PARTIAL-SOT-RECONCILIATION / mixed-freshness): "a truth-reconciliation pass refreshes one axis of the SoT (the §Snapshot.1 table) accurately but leaves a sibling axis (the §Snapshot.2/.3/.5 narrative) stale inside the same document under one header date, producing a doc where a reader cannot tell which part is fresh — arguably more dangerous than uniform staleness."** — seen in: **RETRO-168 (this).** Count 1. **HELD — NO PROMOTION.** Watch: a 2nd partial-reconciliation that leaves undated mixed-freshness in a boot-critical doc is the promotion trigger (a rule "any SoT reconciliation must either refresh all cited axes or per-axis-date the stale ones").

- **Pattern (BASHLESS-AGENT-AUTHOR-BLUR): "delegating a PR-producing doc ticket to a shell-less agent (`architect`) forces the orchestrator to execute all mechanics and can silently make it a SECOND author whose executed edits diverge from the delegate's stated plan."** — seen in: **RETRO-168 (this).** Count 1 (first sighting of an agent-tooling-capability gap in the retro record — grep of prior retros for "no shell/bash tool" returned nothing). **HELD — NO PROMOTION.** Vehicle is the process stub FOLLOW-545.

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P2, NEW → FOLLOW-546 — the load-bearing finding; the async-interleave class FOLLOW-380 set out to close, relocated ONE HOP to the description path). FOLLOW-380's latest-wins guard is a SINGLE checkpoint (`index.ts:737`, `if (myRefreshId !== latestRefreshId) return;`) placed immediately after `fetchDirectives`. But the description adaptation is dispatched fire-and-forget AFTER that checkpoint — `void applyDescriptionAdaptation(config, resp.archetype)` at `index.ts:805` — and lives in a SEPARATE module (`packages/sdk/src/core/adapt-description.ts:265`) that has NO access to `myRefreshId`/`latestRefreshId`.** `applyDescriptionAdaptation` re-reads `listingId` FRESH from the DOM (`adapt-description.ts:279-283`) and then `await fetchDescription(...)` (`:285`) with the STALE `resp.archetype` captured from the superseded refresh. On rapid cross-listing nav where the new listing resolves a DIFFERENT archetype (neutral-fit → SoT restore, or FOLLOW-201 drift), a stale invocation paints the CORRECT (freshly-read) listing's description slot with the WRONG archetype's generated copy — the precise "stale async re-adaptation clobbers the newer listing's DOM" failure LG-1 targeted, surviving because the guard covers only the synchronous directive/headline path, not the fire-and-forget description tail. Same-archetype navs (the common SoT-stable case) are unaffected, which narrows the window but does not close it. → **FOLLOW-546**.
- **LG-2 (P3, NEW → FOLLOW-547 — forward-incompat on rollback / staggered-CDN, fails-safe-by-accident). The SoT JSON write is UNVERSIONED.** The legacy direction (an OLD plain-string entry read by the NEW bundle) is correctly handled: `readResolvedArchetype` (`session.ts:524-548`) tries `JSON.parse`, falls through to `{archetype: raw, confidence: 0.85}` for a bare string — and 0.85 > 0.6 (server gate) AND > 0.5 (DOM floor), so a restored legacy SoT is not suppressed. **The worker's 0.85-fallback reasoning HOLDS — verified against both gate constants (§3).** The RESIDUAL is the REVERSE direction: a NEW JSON entry read by an OLD (pre-FOLLOW-380) bundle after an SDK rollback or during a staggered-CDN redeploy, in a session that spans the flip in-tab. The old `readResolvedArchetype` returns the raw JSON string AS the archetype, setting `currentIntentState.archetype` to `'{"archetype":"family_buyer","confidence":0.85}'` — an invalid archetype. It fails SAFE, but by accident, on three independent legs: (1) the old bundle also lacks bug-(c)'s fix, so it leaves neutral-era low confidence in place → server gate `confidence <= 0.6` returns no directives → no adaptation; (2) `archetype_hint` is `z.string().optional()` in the adapt route (`route.ts:203`), NOT enum-validated, so the garbage string cannot crash the endpoint; (3) the old bundle self-heals on its next non-neutral persist (overwrites JSON with a plain string). Blast radius is bounded by sessionStorage ephemerality (per-tab, cleared on tab close) and only bites sessions live-across-the-flip in the same tab. Net severity LOW/P3 — but "safe by three coincidences on a rollback" is fragile and unmeasured. → **FOLLOW-547** (version + instrument the schema).

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern (ASYNC-READAPT-NO-INFLIGHT-GUARD): "an async re-adaptation triggered by a rapid-fire DOM/navigation event has no in-flight guard covering its FULL async tail, so a superseded invocation's later continuation (esp. a fire-and-forget sub-adaptation in a different module) interleaves on shared state / paints the newer listing's DOM."** — seen in: **RETRO-105 §6 LG-1 (count 1, `refreshDirectives` overlap on rapid SPA nav — explicitly "held, → FOLLOW-380") + RETRO-169 (this, count 2 — FOLLOW-380 guarded the directive path but left the fire-and-forget `applyDescriptionAdaptation` tail uncovered).** **HELD — NO PROMOTION.** Per this repo's consistent promotion adjudication (Rules AA/Q/V provenance comments: "the 2 banked occurrences are both PRIOR retros → ≥2-PRIOR threshold met; the promoting retro is the 3rd sighting"), promotion requires TWO PRIOR retros with the pattern. Here there is ONE prior (RETRO-105); this retro banks the 2nd sighting. **Pre-authorized promotion trigger:** the NEXT (3rd) sighting — or the discovery that FOLLOW-546's fix itself re-relocates the guard gap — promotes a rule of shape *"an in-flight/latest-wins guard on a rapid-nav re-adaptation MUST cover every async continuation that mutates host DOM, including fire-and-forget sub-adaptations in other modules — a single post-fetch checkpoint is insufficient."* Adjacent to Rule R (rehydrate-boundary idempotency) but a distinct axis (concurrency, not rehydration), exactly as RETRO-105 noted.
- **Pattern (UNVERSIONED-CLIENT-STORAGE-SCHEMA-EVOLUTION): "a client-side sessionStorage/localStorage payload gains a field with a read-time backward-compat fallback but NO forward-version marker, so a rolled-back / staggered-CDN old bundle mis-parses the new shape and survives only by coincidental fail-safe."** — seen in: **RETRO-169 (this), count 1.** **HELD — NO PROMOTION** (first sighting; grep of prior retros for a client-storage schema-version finding returned nothing — the closest, Rule W, is a ClickHouse DDL apply-time schema rule, a different runtime/axis). Vehicle is FOLLOW-547.
- **Meta (git-checkout self-inflicted loss vs RETRO-168 DG-2 bashless-blur — assessed for a ≥2 rhyme, REJECTED):** the sdk-engineer's `lessons.md` records losing unstaged `index.ts` edits via `git checkout <file>` during a non-vacuousness simulation (recovered). RETRO-168 DG-2 / FOLLOW-545 is the *bashless-architect author-blur* (a MISSING tool forcing the orchestrator into a 2nd-author workaround). These do NOT rhyme into one ≥2 pattern: DG-2 = missing-tool-forces-workaround (a routing/capability gap); this = present-tool-used-destructively-on-uncommitted-work (a git-hygiene self-inflicted loss). Distinct roots, distinct owners, distinct fixes. **No rule, no duplicate stub** — the sdk-engineer already self-recorded its own guardrail ("NEVER `git checkout <file>` to revert a simulation while unstaged ticket work lives in that file; use a `cp` scratchpad backup").
- **Net: NO rule promoted this retro.** All candidates below the ≥2-PRIOR threshold; the async-interleave pattern is banked at its 2nd sighting per Rules AA/Q/V adjudication.

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P3, NEW → FOLLOW-548 — the load-bearing finding; the SAME async-interleave class, re-relocated ONE MORE HOP from the fetch-in-flight window to the rAF-deferred write). FOLLOW-546's `isStale()` re-check at `adapt-description.ts:309` is SYNCHRONOUS and runs immediately after `await fetchDescription` — it correctly closes the hundreds-of-ms fetch-in-flight window RETRO-169 LG-1 targeted. BUT the actual DOM mutation is DEFERRED: `slots.forEach((slot) => requestAnimationFrame(applyAndObserveSlot(slot, paragraphs)))` (`:323`) and the headline rAF (`:333`).** The `isStale()` gate therefore guards the SCHEDULING of the rAF, not the write inside it. In the ~1-animation-frame gap between the `:309` check and the rAF firing, a superseding `listing.viewed` → `void refreshDirectives()` handler can run to completion synchronously (bump `latestRefreshId`, paint the new listing's directives/headline), after which the stale rAF still fires and calls `render(el, paragraphs)` + `obs.observe(...)` (`adapt-description.ts:161-163`) — painting the STALE archetype's description onto the newer listing. Worse, `applyAndObserveSlot` attaches a **self-reinforcing** `MutationObserver` that re-asserts the stale paragraphs on any host mutation. **Persistence path (not merely a transient flicker):** if the superseding nav's OWN description fetch returns null — an uncached listing, `source !== 'ai_cached'` → `fetchDescription` returns null → the newer `applyDescriptionAdaptation` bails at `if (!resp) return` (`:314`) BEFORE reaching its own rAF/observe — then it never overwrites the stale observer, and the stale description PERSISTS and is actively defended. This is the pattern definition verbatim ("a superseded invocation's later continuation paints the newer listing's DOM"), and it literally instantiates RETRO-169's pre-authorized rule text: *a single post-fetch checkpoint is insufficient — there is STILL an uncovered async continuation (the rAF) past it.* Smaller window than the fetch (~16ms vs hundreds), lower probability, but a real, citable residual with a persistent-stale leg. → **FOLLOW-548**. This is the THIRD relocation hop of the RETRO-105 async-interleave gap (sync-checkpoint → fire-and-forget tail → rAF-deferred write) — the serial-relocation shape (§6, §7).
- **LG-2 (P3, design note — the never-stale default is a latent footgun; NO current bug, folded into FOLLOW-548, no separate stub).** `isStale: () => boolean = () => false` defaults to never-stale so the ~30 test call sites compile unchanged. Verified SAFE TODAY: the ONLY non-test call site is `index.ts:809`, which passes the real predicate (grep `applyDescriptionAdaptation` non-test = `:65` import + `:809` call only). The residual is FORWARD: a FUTURE prod call site that forgets the 3rd arg silently reverts to never-stale with NO compile error and NO lint — re-opening exactly this gap. The JSDoc documents the default (`adapt-description.ts:264-272`) but nothing structurally enforces it at prod call sites. Low severity (latent, not live), folded into FOLLOW-548's AC as a guard/comment at the sole call site.

LG-1 (§4a) is an incomplete-scope concurrency gap on the rAF-deferred write (narrow ~1-frame window, persistent only when the superseding listing is uncached), classified P3 there — not a straightforward bug in the merged lines.

That is the residual, and its non-vacuousness proof requires manually draining the rAF queue between the `:309` check and the callback (jsdom `requestAnimationFrame` must be stubbed/stepped) — the harness the (d) test already stands up can be extended for it.

This is the leg that turns the rAF window from a self-healing flicker into a persistent stale-paint.

## RETRO-172 — FOLLOW-532 (fold the DB-throw fail-loud contract INTO `resolveAdaptGetAuth` — closes RETRO-164 §4c TG-1's unenforced-caller-obligation seam by making both GET adapt call sites share ONE branch; the fold genuinely CLOSES the seam end-to-end rather than relocating it, but the new `area` argument is itself an unpinned per-call-site obligation, and the `dbError` discriminant is a test-only shape Rule I structurally cannot police) — 2026-07-10

### 1. Summary of change

- **PR:** #502 (merged 2026-07-10T14:36:48Z, commit `a934adf`). Title: `fix(control-plane): fold DB-throw parity into resolveAdaptGetAuth [FOLLOW-532]`. RETRO/DONE bookkeeping bundles onto `pm-orchestrator/FOLLOW-532-close` → PR #503 (this retro).
- **Files changed:** 7 (+227 / -42). Code: `apps/control-plane/src/lib/adapt-get-auth.ts` (+42/-11: `resolveAdaptGetAuth` gained a required 3rd `area: 'adapt' | 'description'` param, moved the `resolveApiKey` try/catch + `Sentry.captureException` + `console.error` INSIDE the helper, added a 3rd `AdaptGetAuthResult` disposition `{ ok:false, status:401, message, dbError:true }`, added `import * as Sentry`); both call sites `app/api/adapt/route.ts` (+9/-12) and `app/api/adapt/description/route.ts` (+9/-12) deleted their duplicated try/catch and now call `resolveAdaptGetAuth(req, token, 'adapt'|'description')`. New `apps/control-plane/src/lib/__tests__/adapt-get-auth.parity.test.ts` (+117). Tests: `app/api/adapt/route.test.ts` + `app/api/adapt/description/route.test.ts` (+13/-4 each: the pre-existing DB-throw case flipped from `mockRejectedValue(new Error())` → `mockResolvedValue({ …dbError:true })` to match the new no-throw contract). Non-code: `.claude/agents/backend-engineer/lessons.md` (+42, worker self-retro).
- **Modules touched:** control-plane ONLY (1 lib + 2 API routes + 3 test files) + 1 agent lessons file. No SDK / ingest / decision-api / shared / Modal / db-migration / docs-of-record change.
- **Key contracts changed:** **No external / SDK↔API wire contract changed** — real per-tenant SDK traffic (`Authorization: Bearer ${config.apiKey}`) resolves byte-identically pre/post; a DB-outage 401 body is unchanged (`{ code:'FORBIDDEN', message:'Invalid API key' }`). Two control-plane-INTERNAL deltas: (a) `resolveAdaptGetAuth` signature — added a REQUIRED 3rd param `area: 'adapt'|'description'` — breaking to callers (both updated in-PR; type-checked). (b) `AdaptGetAuthResult` — ADDITIVE 3rd union member `{ …dbError:true }` — non-breaking (existing `!authResult.ok` branch subsumes it). The helper's throw→return contract inverted: it USED to propagate `resolveApiKey`'s Rule-K.2 throw (caller `@throws` obligation); it now catches internally and NEVER throws.
