## RETRO-199 — FOLLOW-598 (ADR-0018 §6 Phase-3 bandit-weight staff-write port — the HIGHEST-blast-radius staff WRITE in the epic + global generation-model PUT superadmin gate, PR #600, merged `a9e1923` 2026-07-21T21:08:47Z) — session-50 retrospective-analyst (Opus). **HEADLINE — SECURITY-CLEAN + GUARD-OK: the epic's highest-blast-radius staff write ships correctly gated, atomic, rank-locked at superadmin, and — critically — its `paused=false` mutation was kept INLINE (`.update(abBanditWeights)`), so `scripts/check-staff-write-atomicity.cjs` prints `OK` for this route (re-verified live on merged `main`). This is the deliberate CONTRAST to FOLLOW-597's `labels/[id]` barrel-delegation SKIP (FOLLOW-613): the two ports resolved the guard-coverage tradeoff opposite ways and BOTH are correct-by-their-own-lights (no bandit `@estalara/db` helper exists, so inline is the natural shape here and it costs nothing). FOLLOW-598 completes the ADR-0018 staff-WRITE-PORT sequence (592→598 all merged); NO staff write ports remain — remaining epic work is all non-write: audit-read consumer (FOLLOW-599), hub-links (FOLLOW-606, now unblocked), guard barrel-bypass (FOLLOW-613, which now protects ONLY the single `labels/[id]` SKIP — 598 did NOT add a new SKIP).** The bandit resume write is wired END-TO-END on the business axis: `paused=false` → `getBanditArms` (`bandit-query.ts`) → `/api/adapt` Thompson-sample decision path (`adapt/route.ts:920,1428`) — resuming an archetype genuinely re-enables it in live adaptation, NOT a one-hop. The NEW `staff_audit_log` action `bandit_weights.resume` is the **5th** staff-write producer action (after quiz_config.update, demo_override.update, intent_weights.update, conversion_label.reclassify) and rides the SAME pre-existing HALF_WIRE_P — consumer `/api/audit` still serves `MOCK_ENTRIES` (`audit/route.ts:42`, TODO Sprint 5) — already owned by FOLLOW-599 (now 5 unreadable actions, not 4). Part 2 (global `generation-model` PUT) tightens STAFF callers to `estalara:superadmin` via `requireStaffRole`; the headless `ADMIN_API_SECRET`/`via:'admin_secret'` path is DELIBERATELY EXEMPT (server-to-server automation carries no staff identity; the CEO-Q3 predicate binds staff USERS, not the shared secret) — a documented, CEO-Q3-scoped decision, NOT a gap. ALL five hunt targets came back clean: (a) superadmin gate is correctly ordered BEFORE the mock path AND the staff/agency branches (test at route.test.ts asserts ops-staff→403 with `DATABASE_URL=''`, proving no mock-200 leak); (b) agency path's `access.rawToken` sources from the same JWT as the pre-port `session.rawToken` and the `TenantAccess` union makes a staff result structurally unable to carry `rawToken` → RLS preserved exactly; (c) the ADMIN_API_SECRET exemption is intentional+documented; (d) `bandit_weights.resume` only ever sets `paused=false` — action name matches mutation. NO contradiction with prior "clean" verdicts: RETRO-198 PREDICTED 598 would stay guard-OK if kept inline — CONFIRMED. WIRING clean both checks (the only HALF_WIRE_P is the pre-existing FOLLOW-599 one). NO new FOLLOW filed. CONVENTIONS_PATCH: NO PROMOTION. — 2026-07-21

### 1. Summary of change

- **PR:** #600 (merged 2026-07-21 21:08:47 UTC, squash commit `a9e1923` on `main`, by Pnawrocki9; branch `backend-engineer/FOLLOW-598-bandit-superadmin-write-port`)
- **Files changed:** 4 (+589 / -145) — `api/tenants/[id]/bandit/weights/[archetype]/route.ts` (+166), its `route.test.ts` (+477/-…), `api/admin/generation-model/route.ts` (+39), its `route.test.ts` (+52). No migrations.
- **Modules touched:** control-plane (2 API routes + 2 test files). No SDK/decision-api/ingest/data/docs/config source changes.
- **Key contracts changed:**
  - `PATCH /api/tenants/:id/bandit/weights/:archetype` — auth surface CHANGED: agency-only → `resolveTenantAccess({ allowStaffOverride, minAgencyRole:'agency:admin', tenantId:[id] })`, staff path gated at `access.isSuperadmin` (rank ≥ 3). Response contract UNCHANGED (`{resumed:true, archetype}` / mock `{…,mock:true}`); adds `403 forbidden` (below-superadmin staff) + `500 audit_write_failed` (non-atomic staff write). Breaking for callers: **no** (agency behavior byte-unchanged; staff is a new accepted principal).
  - `staff_audit_log` — NEW producer action `bandit_weights.resume` (5th write action). Additive; no schema change (no migration).
  - `PUT /api/admin/generation-model` — auth TIGHTENED: staff callers now require `estalara:superadmin` (was any staff tier). `ADMIN_API_SECRET` path unchanged. Breaking: **no** today (sole prod account is superadmin); binding as staff accounts are added.

### 2. Verification done in PR

- Test files changed: 2 (`bandit/weights/[archetype]/route.test.ts` rewritten +477; `generation-model/route.test.ts` +52). Assertions added: MANDATORY red-first tenant-fence (superadmin for A binds the real service-role `.update` to A, never B — INV-5); ops-rank staff→403 **with `DATABASE_URL=''`** (proves the superadmin gate fires BEFORE the mock 200 path); superadmin→200 + exactly one attributed `staff_audit_log` row inside ONE `db.transaction()`; audit-insert failure rolls BOTH back → 500 `audit_write_failed` (no orphan resume); agency path unchanged (no tx, no audit); AccessError 401/403/404 mapping; `resolveTenantAccess` called with the URL tenant + `allowStaffOverride:true` + `minAgencyRole:'agency:admin'`; generation-model ops→403 / superadmin→200 / `ADMIN_API_SECRET` preserved. Coverage delta: unknown (est. high — all new branches asserted).
- CI checks: passed pre-merge per PM (59 real gates green; only non-blocking `Rule I` red). Independently re-verified post-merge: `node scripts/check-staff-write-atomicity.cjs` prints `OK` for the bandit route on `main`.

### 3. Wiring Audit

- **CHECK A (dead code):** clean. The route is a Next.js framework entrypoint (suppressed). New local helper `requestIp` is used at the staff audit insert; all new imports (`Sentry`, `createAdminClient`, `staffAuditLog`, `resolveTenantAccess`, `accessErrorToResponse`, `TenantAccess`) are used. No new exported symbol. generation-model adds `getSessionAuthClaims`/`requireStaffRole`/`AuthClaims` imports, all used in the new gate.
- **CHECK B (half-wire):** the NEW `staff_audit_log` action `bandit_weights.resume` has a PRODUCER (this route) but its CONSUMER — `GET /api/audit` — still serves `MOCK_ENTRIES` (`apps/control-plane/src/app/api/audit/route.ts:42`, `// TODO Sprint 5`). This is the SAME pre-existing HALF_WIRE_P already owned by **FOLLOW-599** (now grown to **5** producer write actions unreadable via the mock audit view: quiz_config.update, demo_override.update, intent_weights.update, conversion_label.reclassify, bandit_weights.resume). NOT a new finding — no new FOLLOW; recorded as +1 producer on the tracked wire (consistent with RETRO-190/198 treatment).
- **Business-axis wire — LIVE (not a half-wire):** `abBanditWeights.paused` set false → read by `getBanditArms` (`lib/bandit-query.ts:78,88,108`) → consumed on the Decision-API hot path (`api/adapt/route.ts:920` sample, `:1428` panel). Producer→consumer→render intact end-to-end.
- **Atomicity guard:** `OK` for `tenants/[id]/bandit/weights/[archetype]/route.ts` (mutation + `insert(staffAuditLog)` in the SAME `db.transaction()`), re-verified live on merged `main`. `labels/[id]` and `labels/export` still `SKIP` (FOLLOW-613 barrel bypass / audit-of-export) — 598 did NOT add a SKIP.

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- N/A (material). Four hunt targets checked, all clean: (a) superadmin gate ordered BEFORE the `!DATABASE_URL` mock path and before both the staff and agency branches — an ops-rank staff caller cannot reach a mock-200 or a mutation (asserted with `DATABASE_URL=''`); (b) agency path `access.rawToken` = the same session JWT that pre-port `session.rawToken` used, and the `TenantAccess` union structurally prevents a staff result from carrying `rawToken`, so RLS is preserved exactly on the agency path; (c) the `generation-model` `ADMIN_API_SECRET` (`via:'admin_secret'`) exemption is an intentional, in-code-documented, CEO-Q3-scoped decision (the superadmin predicate binds staff USERS, not the shared server-to-server secret; a global platform knob behind a trusted secret is acceptable, unlike attributable per-tenant staff writes) — a design decision, NOT a gap; (d) `bandit_weights.resume` only ever writes `.set({paused:false, updatedAt})` — the audit action name matches the mutation exactly (never a broader weight mutation).

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught (P0/P1/P2)

- N/A. No path lets a below-superadmin staff caller mutate or receive a false-success; the atomicity guard mechanically confirms same-tx; rollback is unit-tested for no-orphan.

#### 4c. Test coverage gaps

- N/A (material). The subtle case (ops-staff → 403 even with the DB unconfigured, proving gate-before-mock ordering) IS asserted (`route.test.ts`, `describe('PATCH bandit resume — superadmin gate')`, `vi.stubEnv('DATABASE_URL','')`). Tenant-fence, rollback-no-orphan, single-tx, single-audit-row, agency-unchanged, and gen-model ops/superadmin/secret all covered.

#### 4d. Documentation gaps

- N/A. Route header + gen-model gate comment document the auth model, the atomicity requirement, the inline-mutation rationale (FOLLOW-613), and the ADMIN_API_SECRET exemption. ADR-0018 §3a/§4/§6 already cover the pattern.

### 5. Cascading impact

#### 5a. Current sprint tickets affected

- **FOLLOW-599** (audit-read consumer, OPEN): scope grows — `/api/audit` must now render **5** staff-write actions (was 4 at RETRO-198), incl. the newest `bandit_weights.resume`. Still a single tracked HALF_WIRE_P; value/urgency of 599 rises as the producer set is now complete for the write-port epic.

NOTE: 598 ships NO new `/admin/tenants/[id]/bandit` page (it ports an existing API route + a global route), so it adds NO new hub-linkage sighting — the count stays at 3 (RETRO-190/193/198), still HELD.

RETRO-198's prediction ("613 not a blocker for 598 if the mutation stays inline") is CONFIRMED.

#### 5b. Future sprint tickets affected

- No staff WRITE ports remain in ADR-0018 (§6 Phase 0–3 all merged: FOLLOW-592/593/594/595/596/597/598). Any future per-tenant staff write should reuse this INLINE-mutation + single-`db.transaction()` + superadmin/canWrite-gate shape and verify guard-`OK`.

#### 5c. Contracts changed others rely on

- `PATCH …/bandit/weights/:archetype`: the Panel-5 "Anomaly feed" Resume button (analytics dashboard) is the caller — agency behavior byte-unchanged, so no dashboard change required; staff (superadmin) is a newly accepted principal.

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

- Reinforces ADR-0018 §2 INV-5 (service-role staff writes fence tenant IN the query) and §3a (mutation+audit atomic in one tx). Establishes the codified tradeoff: **keep a staff mutation INLINE when no shared `@estalara/db` helper exists, so the atomicity guard stays `OK`** — vs 597's shared-helper-via-barrel path that trades guard coverage (SKIP, FOLLOW-613) for zero agency/staff write-duplication. Both are legitimate; the choice is driven by whether a reusable tx-aware helper already exists.

- **Pattern (HUB-LINKAGE — a new per-tenant staff surface ships WITHOUT its `[id]`-hub link):** count UNCHANGED at 3 (RETRO-190 analytics+quiz, RETRO-193 demo, RETRO-198 labels+intent). Codifying "keep it inline" as a standalone rule would (i) duplicate FOLLOW-613's remit and (ii) be obsoleted the moment 613 lands and makes barrel-delegation guard-safe. **No promotion** — the pattern is a transient artifact of an as-yet-unclosed guard gap, not a durable convention.
- **Meta (my own blind-spot watch):** verified the business-axis wire (paused→adapt) SEPARATELY from the audit-trail wire — easy to conflate "the write is wired" (it is, to `/api/adapt`) with "the audit of the write is wired" (it is NOT — mock `/api/audit`). Recording both explicitly in §3.

### 1. Summary of change

- **PR:** #602 (merged 2026-07-21 22:34:43 UTC, commit `78b8b53`, squash, author Pnawrocki9; branch `backend-engineer/FOLLOW-599-audit-read-consumer`)

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

FOLLOW-599 has now properly closed the `/api/audit` half. The `/api/config` half is UNCHANGED and independently re-verified live on `main`: `config/route.ts:89` (GET) and `:101` (PATCH) read `req.headers.get('x-tenant-id')` as the sole tenant authority with no JWT/session, and `:110` reads the caller ROLE from a spoofable `x-agency-role` header to gate the PATCH mutation. Middleware does NOT protect it: the matcher covers `/api/config`, but the handler falls through the `/admin` and `/dashboard` branches to "All other routes — pass through" (`middleware.ts:~360`) → `NextResponse.next()` with the caller's `x-tenant-id` NOT stripped/overwritten. So `curl .../api/config -H 'x-tenant-id: <victim>' -H 'x-agency-role: agency:owner'` (PATCH) reaches the handler unauthenticated. Still capped at P2 because `config` is an in-memory `configStore` Map stub (no real cross-tenant data today), but `config/route.ts:6` carries `// TODO Sprint 5: read/write tenants table` — the hole SHIPS the moment it's wired (FOLLOW-600 `/settings` surface is the likely wiring point). This is the sole remaining live instance (the other `x-tenant-id` sites — `adapt`, `adapt/description`, `ab/weights`, `demo/.../revoke` — are all "no-longer-an-authority" JWT/HMAC paths, verified by their in-file comments). → **FOLLOW-614** (narrowed successor to the now-half-discharged FOLLOW-491).
- **LG-2 (P4, benign — NO stub) — the `data_source:'mock'` fallback branch is UNREACHABLE in a real no-DB environment (epic-wide, but harmless).** On this staff-only route the order is `resolveTenantAccess(...)` FIRST → its staff path calls `tenantExists(opts.tenantId)` (`session-auth.ts:446`) → `createAdminClient()` (`packages/db/client.ts:188`) which `throw`s when neither `DATABASE_URL_ADMIN` nor `DATABASE_URL_DIRECT` is set → wrapped as `AccessError(500)` → route try/catch → `accessErrorToResponse` → **500 BEFORE** the route's `if (!dbConfigured) return buildMockAuditResponse(...)`. Because `dbConfigured` reads the SAME two env vars, `!dbConfigured` ⟺ `createAdminClient` throws, so the mock branch can only execute when a TEST mocks `resolveTenantAccess`/`tenantExists`. **Verdict: demonstrable dead branch, but NOT a Rule-K.2 gap and NOT a bug.** Rule K.2's mandate (fail loud in prod, never fabricate) is actually UPHELD — a real no-DB prod-class env correctly 500s instead of serving mock rows; the mock path is purely a test-observability convenience. Same structure exists in `admin/labels/route.ts` (`resolveTenantAccess` at :270 before `dbConfigured` at :300); `admin/intent-weights/route.ts` AVOIDS it entirely (no mock branch — 500 fail-loud on unconfigured). The only defect is a docstring that describes the mock as a "dev/CI DB-unconfigured fallback" when it is really "test-only (auth helper mocked)". Minor doc imprecision, not worth a ticket. **No stub filed** (per charter: file only for concrete, demonstrable PROBLEMS).

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught (P0/P1/P2)

- None P0/P1. **P3 (observation, no stub):** `fetchAuditEntries` fetches ALL matching rows then paginates in JS (`allRows.slice(start, start+limit)`) rather than pushing `LIMIT/OFFSET` into SQL. Correct output; a mild scalability smell, but `staff_audit_log` per-tenant is low-volume at pilot scale — not a concrete problem today.

#### 4c. Test coverage gaps

- **TG-1 (folded into FOLLOW-614, not a new stub) —** `/api/config` still has NO spoofed-`x-tenant-id`/`x-agency-role`→403 test; `config/route.test.ts:16/29/49` codifies the header-only auth model (sends `x-tenant-id` as auth, asserts "missing → 401"), so the hole is test-LOCKED-IN. The audit route by contrast is now well-covered (367-line suite incl. the red-first fence test).

#### 4d. Documentation gaps

- Minor (LG-2): the `data_source:'mock'` docstring in `audit/route.ts` (and `labels/route.ts`) overstates when the mock path fires. Non-blocking; not ticketed.

### 5. Cascading impact

#### 5a. Current sprint tickets affected

- None blocked. FOLLOW-599 completes the ADR-0018 §3 audit-READ leg; the write-port sequence (592→598) was already merged.

#### 5b. Future sprint tickets affected

- **FOLLOW-491** — now HALF-discharged (audit leg closed by 599). Its config leg carries forward as **FOLLOW-614**. The original "both are stubs, defer" rationale is now half-invalidated: 599 proved the fix is cheap and is the EXPECTED shape as these routes get wired, so `config` should not remain header-authed once touched.
- **FOLLOW-600** (`/admin/tenants/[id]/settings` surface) — the likely point where `/api/config` gets wired to a real store; MUST move config onto `resolveTenantAccess` FIRST (or it ships LG-1 as a real cross-tenant leak). Flag added via FOLLOW-614.

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern (HALF_WIRE_P closure — `staff_audit_log` consumer):** RESOLVED end-to-end this PR (producer→table→real API read→`StaffAuditView`→hub link). This is a genuine multi-hop closure verified NOT one-hop: the prior "fix" attempts (RETRO-190/198/199) only ADDED producers while the consumer stayed mock; 599 is the hop that actually connects the wire to a render. No rule — a resolved half-wire is not a recurring convention.
- **Pattern (SPOOFABLE-HEADER auth-hole class — trust `x-tenant-id`/`x-agency-role` as auth):** seen in RETRO-153 (FOLLOW-456/491), RETRO-163, RETRO-164 (FOLLOW-473), and now here (config leg). Count ≥2 — BUT **already governed** by the **Rule H amendment (2026-05-23, RETRO-006 §6a — "shipping a mutation endpoint with weak/placeholder auth")** and repeatedly tracked via FOLLOW-456/473/491. **No new rule** — codifying again would duplicate existing coverage; the gap is enforcement (sweep the last sibling), not a missing convention → FOLLOW-614.
- **Pattern (HUB-LINKAGE — a new per-tenant staff surface ships WITHOUT its `[id]`-hub link):** failure count UNCHANGED at 3 (RETRO-190/193/198). **FOLLOW-599 is the FIRST per-tenant surface to ship AFTER the FOLLOW-606 same-PR-link template landed (RETRO-200), and it CORRECTLY self-wired its hub link** ("Audit Log" added to `[id]/page.tsx` in the SAME PR, test-asserted). This CONFIRMS the template works and the promotion trigger (armed by RETRO-200) is **NOT fired** — 599 is a positive/compliant instance, not a new sighting. **No promotion.**
- **Meta (my own blind-spot watch):** I nearly recorded the auth-hole as a fresh one-off finding before grepping the retro history — RETRO-153/163 had ALREADY filed it as FOLLOW-491 covering BOTH legs. Tracing the prior-follow-up chain (step 7) turned a "new stub" into "the correct narrowed successor," and reframed the headline from "closed a hole" to "closed one leg of a known 2-leg class, one leg still live."

### 7. Follow-ups

- **FOLLOW-614** (P2, backend-engineer, 2h): Sweep the last live leg of the `x-tenant-id` spoofable-header class — `/api/config` GET+PATCH (+ `x-agency-role` role spoof on PATCH) — onto `resolveTenantAccess`; narrowed successor to the now-half-discharged FOLLOW-491 (audit leg closed by FOLLOW-599). Includes the spoofed-header→403 test TG-1.

### 8. Cross-references

- Related to **RETRO-153 / RETRO-163** (FOLLOW-491): FOLLOW-599 discharges the `/api/audit` leg of that 2-leg spoofable-header stub; FOLLOW-614 carries the `/api/config` leg forward.
- Related to **RETRO-190 / 198 / 199** (the `staff_audit_log` write-port sequence): those retros each noted the consumer was still the mock `/api/audit` (HALF_WIRE_P, "consumer FOLLOW-599"); this PR is the hop that RESOLVES it end-to-end.

## RETRO-202 — FOLLOW-614 (close the `/api/config` spoofable-header auth hole via `resolveTenantAccess` — the LAST live leg of the `x-tenant-id`/`x-agency-role` class RETRO-153/163 filed as FOLLOW-491 and RETRO-201 re-flagged) — 2026-07-22

**HEADLINE — the unauthenticated spoofable-header class is now FULLY discharged repo-wide (both FOLLOW-491 legs closed: audit by FOLLOW-599, config by this PR), verified END-TO-END by re-grep: zero routes remain that read `x-tenant-id`/`x-agency-role` as an AUTHORITY. But the port ships ONE residual gap on a NARROWER axis: `PATCH /api/config` is the first staff-write port in the epic to OMIT the write-rank gate (`access.via==='staff' && !access.canWrite → 403`) that RETRO-190's port template item (c) and RETRO-199's closing note both mandate and that EVERY sibling staff write enforces — so an `estalara:readonly` staff user (rank 1 < ops 2) can PATCH any tenant's config. P2-capped (in-memory stub, authenticated internal staff only, zero consumers today) but it SHIPS as a real write-tier violation the moment FOLLOW-600 wires the real `tenants` table → FOLLOW-615. Root cause: FOLLOW-614's AC was written as a "remove header trust" sweep and never restated the epic-wide write-rank invariant — the worker implemented the AC faithfully (and even added the FOLLOW-603 option-wiring assertions unprompted) but the gate lived only in prior-retro prose, not the AC.**

### 1. Summary of change

- **PR:** #603 (merged 2026-07-22 07:30:38 UTC, squash commit `3669be2`, author Pnawrocki9; branch `backend-engineer/FOLLOW-614-config-auth-sweep`, backend-engineer/OPUS)
- **Files changed:** 2 (+284 / -77) — `api/config/route.ts` + `api/config/route.test.ts`; no migrations, no new files
- **Modules touched:** control-plane only
- **Key contracts changed:**
  - Auth contract on `GET /api/config`: was "any caller supplying `x-tenant-id`" (no session at all); now `resolveTenantAccess({ allowStaffOverride: true, minAgencyRole: 'agency:viewer' })` (`route.ts:122-124`) — breaking: yes (intentional security fix; tightens from unauthenticated to agency-viewer-or-staff). No in-repo caller existed (grep: zero `fetch('/api/config')` sites outside the route's own test), so nothing broke.
  - Auth contract on `PATCH /api/config`: was spoofable `x-agency-role ∈ {agency:owner, agency:admin}` header gate; now `minAgencyRole: 'agency:admin'` from the VERIFIED claim (`route.ts:143-145`) — breaking: yes (same intentional fix). Both header reads REMOVED from the route.
  - NEW capability (staff axis): staff may now target any tenant via validated `?tenant_id` (previously staff had NO path into config at all) — additive; this is where LG-1 lives.
  - `TenantConfig` type export unchanged; `configStore` in-memory stub unchanged (real-DB wiring = FOLLOW-600).

### 2. Verification done in PR

- Test files changed: `config/route.test.ts` (full rewrite +260/-77, 11 tests, re-run green on merged `main` this retro). Assertions: both-verb SPOOF-CLOSED tests (verified tenant A + spoofed victim headers → operates on A, never the victim), no-auth→401, viewer-below-admin-floor→403 on PATCH, staff `?tenant_id`→200 on both verbs, and the FOLLOW-603 option-wiring assertions on BOTH verbs (`toHaveBeenCalledWith(…objectContaining({allowStaffOverride:true, minAgencyRole:…}))`) — the template note was honored WITHOUT being in the AC (positive). Coverage delta: net-positive.
- CI checks: passed on all real gates; only the pre-existing non-blocking `Rule I` red (per `project_ci_gate_landscape`).
- `node scripts/check-staff-write-atomicity.cjs` re-run live this retro: config route NOT listed (correct — the PATCH mutates only the in-memory Map, no `insert(staffAuditLog)`; the commit deliberately kept it invisible to the guard and documented why in the route header). `labels/[id]` + `labels/export` still the only SKIPs (FOLLOW-613 state unchanged).

### 3. Wiring Audit

- **CHECK A (dead code):** no new files; `route.ts` is a framework-route entrypoint (suppressed). `TenantConfig` export consumed by the colocated test (pre-existing shape). **No dead code introduced.** Pre-existing observation, NOT introduced here: `/api/config` still has ZERO in-repo fetch consumers (grep `'/api/config'` across apps/packages excl. the route+test → only a 2026-05-18 audit doc mention) — it is a consumer-less API awaiting FOLLOW-600's `/settings` page. Not a finding against this PR.
- **CHECK B (half-wire):** no new event/env-var/column/topic/SDK-signal. The PATCH deliberately writes NO `staff_audit_log` row (nothing real to atomically pair with — documented in the route header with the FOLLOW-600 §3a obligation), so no new producer rides the audit pipeline. `Wiring Audit — clean ✅`

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P2, SECURITY — the finding) — `PATCH /api/config` omits the staff write-rank gate; `estalara:readonly` staff can mutate any tenant's config.** Chain, independently verified on `main`: `PATCH` calls `resolveTenantAccess({allowStaffOverride:true, minAgencyRole:'agency:admin'})` (`route.ts:143-145`) → `minAgencyRole` gates ONLY the agency path (`session-auth.ts:404`); the staff path (`session-auth.ts:421-458`) requires only `verifyTracerAdminAuth` OK — which admits ANY `estalara_staff:true` user with NO role floor, readonly included (`tracer-auth.ts:133-137` via `checkStaffSession`, `:154-157` via staff JWT) — plus identified claims + validated `?tenant_id`, then RETURNS `canWrite: STAFF_ROLE_RANK[role] >= 2` (`session-auth.ts:456`) **without enforcing it** (enforcement is by design the ROUTE's job). The route never reads `access.canWrite` — it goes straight to `configStore.set(access.tenantId, updated)` (`route.ts:169`). Contrast EVERY sibling staff write: `quiz/config/route.ts:154`, `demo/override/route.ts:197`, `admin/intent-weights/route.ts:206` (all `via==='staff' && !canWrite`→403), `bandit/weights/[archetype]/route.ts:102` (`!isSuperadmin`→403). This deviates from the port template codified twice: RETRO-190 §"copy THIS shape" item (c) and RETRO-199's "reuse this … superadmin/canWrite-gate shape" closing note; FOLLOW-603's AC template note additionally mandates asserting the gate in every WRITE port. Severity capped P2: the write hits only the per-instance in-memory `configStore` Map (ephemeral, zero consumers), and the attacker must be an authenticated internal staff user — but FOLLOW-600 wires this exact route to the real `tenants` table, at which point this is a live write-tier violation. → **FOLLOW-615** (must land BEFORE or WITH FOLLOW-600). Root cause: FOLLOW-614's AC (a header-trust sweep, filed by RETRO-201) never restated the write-rank invariant — an AC-underspecification instance, see §6.
- **LG-2 (P4, benign — NO stub) — spoof-handling shape diverges from the AC letter, security-equivalently.** FOLLOW-614 AC bullet 2 asked for "rejected (401 no session / 403 mismatch)"; the implementation IGNORES the spoofed headers (request succeeds against the VERIFIED tenant) — the `/api/audit` precedent — rather than the `demo/sessions/[id]/revoke` defense-in-depth mismatch-403 shape (`revoke/route.ts:45-55`). Both shapes are SPOOF-CLOSED (the security property "never operates on the victim tenant" is test-asserted on both verbs); the 401-no-session half of the AC IS implemented. AC-literal deviation only, reconciled here; the sibling "configStore untouched on rejection" assertion is folded into FOLLOW-615 (see 4c).

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught (P0/P1/P2)

- None. (LG-1 is a missing gate, not a mis-executing one; all 11 tests green on `main`, re-run this retro.)

#### 4c. Test coverage gaps

- **TG-1 (folded into FOLLOW-615) —** no `estalara:readonly` staff → 403 test on PATCH; the `staffAccess` fixture hardcodes `role:'estalara:ops', canWrite:true` (`route.test.ts` fixture), so the missing gate is invisible to the suite. Blocked on LG-1's gate existing; the FOLLOW-603 template's write-rank assertion must land with it.
- **TG-2 (folded into FOLLOW-615, minor) —** AC bullet 2's "configStore Map is NOT touched on rejection" assertion was not written (trivially true today by code order — every rejection path returns before `getConfig` — but unasserted, so a future reorder regresses silently).
- Positive worth recording: BOTH verbs carry the FOLLOW-603 option-wiring assertions although the AC never asked — first port to adopt the template spontaneously.

#### 4d. Documentation gaps

- None. The route header is exemplary: documents the closed hole, the DB-coupling of the staff path, and the FOLLOW-600 §3a audit-in-transaction obligation in-file where the next worker will trip over it.

### 5. Cascading impact

#### 5a. Current sprint tickets affected

- None blocked. FOLLOW-613 / FOLLOW-604 / FOLLOW-611 (the session-51 QUEUE candidates) are untouched: 613's guard state is unchanged (config route correctly invisible to the guard — no `insert(staffAuditLog)`); 604's AC ALREADY includes the write-rank gate + FOLLOW-603 assertion (verified `FOLLOW_UPS.md:16419-16431`) so it will NOT repeat LG-1 if implemented as written; 611 unrelated.

#### 5b. Future sprint tickets affected

- **FOLLOW-600** (`/settings` + real-table wiring) — UNBLOCKED on the auth axis by this PR (config is no longer header-authed; the RETRO-201 "must move onto resolveTenantAccess FIRST" precondition is satisfied). But 600 now inherits TWO explicit obligations: (1) **FOLLOW-615's `canWrite` gate must land BEFORE or WITH it** — wiring the real `tenants` table while PATCH is readonly-staff-writable ships a live write-tier violation; (2) the §3a audit-in-`db.transaction()` pattern per the route-header note (also makes the route newly VISIBLE to the atomicity guard — keep the mutation INLINE per the RETRO-198/199 barrel-vs-inline finding or it lands as another FOLLOW-613 SKIP). FOLLOW-600's AC amended in FOLLOW_UPS.md to bind both.
- **FOLLOW-491** — now FULLY discharged (both legs: audit=FOLLOW-599/PR #602, config=FOLLOW-614/PR #603). End-to-end closure verified by repo-wide re-grep, not one-hop: the only remaining `x-tenant-id`/`x-agency-role` sites are (i) middleware SETTING them from VERIFIED claims for `/dashboard` server components (`middleware.ts:311-313,336-338` — a trusted producer, not a consumer of caller input), (ii) `packages/auth/tenant-context` consuming those middleware-set headers under `/dashboard` layouts only, (iii) the answers page reading the middleware-injected meta tag to build a PATH param that `validateTenantAuth` re-checks against SESSION claims (`tenants/[id]/answers/route.ts:72`), and (iv) `demo/.../revoke`'s defense-in-depth mismatch-403 (explicitly non-authoritative). Zero authority sites remain.

#### 5c. Contracts changed others rely on

- None beyond the route's own auth contract — zero in-repo consumers of `/api/config` (§3 CHECK A), so the breaking auth change has an empty blast radius today. FOLLOW-600's future page must send a session (SSR cookie / Bearer), not headers.

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

- `resolveTenantAccess` is now the auth boundary on EVERY per-tenant config/staff surface in control-plane — the ADR-0018 §2 pattern is uniform repo-wide with no header-authed stragglers. The residual non-uniformity is LG-1's missing write-tier gate on this one route.

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern (staff WRITE port ships WITHOUT its write-rank gate):** seen in: THIS retro only (RETRO-190/193/198/199's ports all shipped the gate). Promote-threshold 2 (prior retros), current count **1 prior = 0** — **no promotion.** FOLLOW-615 is the mechanical closure; FOLLOW-604's AC already guards the next port.
- **Pattern (stub-AC under-enumeration faithfully propagated — the AC omits a piece of the epic-wide template and the worker, implementing the AC correctly, ships the omission):** seen in: RETRO-198 (FOLLOW-606's AC missed `/intent`; amended) + THIS retro (FOLLOW-614's AC missed the write-rank gate → LG-1). Current count: **1 prior** — below the ≥2-PRIOR bar (same reading as RETRO-193's hub-linkage hold) — **banked, not promoted.** Candidate rule if it recurs: "a FOLLOW stub whose scope is an instance of a codified template (staff-write port, hub link, …) MUST reference the template checklist in its AC rather than re-deriving requirements."
- **Positive (FOLLOW-603 template self-adoption):** the worker added the option-wiring assertions on both verbs unprompted — first spontaneous adoption; evidence the template note is propagating through lessons/precedent without AC enforcement.

### 7. Follow-ups

- **FOLLOW-615**: Add the missing staff write-rank gate to `PATCH /api/config` (`via==='staff' && !access.canWrite`→403) + red-first readonly-staff→403 test + FOLLOW-603 write-rank assertion + configStore-untouched-on-rejection assertion (backend-engineer, 1h, priority **P2** — MUST land before/with FOLLOW-600's real-table wiring).

### 8. Cross-references

- Related to **RETRO-201** (FOLLOW-599): this PR closes the exact leg RETRO-201's LG-1 flagged and filed; the class (FOLLOW-491) is now fully discharged — RETRO-201's "one leg still live" verdict is RESOLVED, not contradicted.
- Related to **RETRO-190 / RETRO-199** (the port template): LG-1 is the first deviation from template item (c) (write-rank gate) across seven staff ports — the template held 6/7 times; the one miss correlates exactly with the one AC that didn't restate it.
- Related to **RETRO-189 / FOLLOW-603**: the option-wiring assertions shipped (template followed); the write-rank assertion mandate could not be followed because the gate itself is absent (LG-1).
- Related to **RETRO-198 / RETRO-199 / FOLLOW-613**: the PATCH stays correctly INVISIBLE to the atomicity guard today (no audit insert, no real mutation); flagged to FOLLOW-600 that wiring the real table must keep the mutation inline or it becomes the next barrel-SKIP.
- Hub-linkage trigger (RETRO-200, ARMED): NOT fired — this PR ships no page/surface; failure count stays 3.

## RETRO-203 — FOLLOW-615 (add the missing staff write-rank gate to `PATCH /api/config` — `estalara:readonly` staff could mutate any tenant's config) — 2026-07-22

**HEADLINE — CLEAN CLOSURE, END-TO-END, NOT ONE HOP: FOLLOW-615 discharges RETRO-202 §4a LG-1 exactly and completely. The `via==='staff' && !access.canWrite → 403` gate now sits immediately after `resolveTenantAccess` on `PATCH /api/config` (`route.ts:160-165`), byte-for-shape identical to the three ops-tier siblings (`quiz/config:154`, `demo/override:197`, `admin/intent-weights:206`). The gate is the SOLE staff write chokepoint — `configStore` is a module-private `const Map` (`route.ts:87`, not exported, zero external importers verified by grep), `PATCH` is its only writer, and `GET` is intentionally left ungated (readonly staff keeps read, matching the `/api/audit` precedent). Unknown-role staff fail CLOSED (`STAFF_ROLE_RANK[unknown]` → `undefined >= 2` → false → `canWrite:false` → 403). The gap did NOT move one hop downstream: there is no other writer, no other axis, and no other consumer. RETRO-202's LG-1 is RESOLVED, not relocated. This does NOT contradict any prior "clean" verdict — RETRO-202 explicitly filed this gap, so this PR CONFIRMS that verdict. No new gap, no new FOLLOW, no rule promoted (the failure pattern is at count 1 — a clean fix is not a new sighting).**

## RETRO-204 — FOLLOW-613 (close staff-write-atomicity guard bypass 6 — barrel re-export delegated mutation, PR #605, merged `872715f314075256e1167ad25ee94da354999b6f` 2026-07-22T21:01:37Z) — session-54 retrospective-analyst (Opus). **HEADLINE — the shipped fix GENUINELY closes bypass 6 and is independently re-verified LIVE on `main`, not just on the PR's own fixtures: `admin/labels/[id]/route.ts` (FOLLOW-597's live barrel-delegated staff write) flips `SKIP`→**`OK`** (re-run `node scripts/check-staff-write-atomicity.cjs` this session), the sibling `admin/labels/export/route.ts` correctly STAYS `SKIP` (per-name resolution keeps its non-mutating `createAdminClient` import distinct — no false FAIL), and the full fixture suite + real-repo scan pass. The per-name (not per-barrel) resolution is correct and load-bearing exactly as documented. BUT — for the 4th consecutive time on this same guard (bypass 4→5→6, now 7), a fresh INDEPENDENT reproduction finds the SAME class ONE call-shape over, and it is NOT one of the three shapes FOLLOW-613 itself enumerated-and-deferred (FOLLOW-616 bracket access / 617 dynamic import / 618 local-var alias): a NAMESPACE import of a BARREL package — `import * as db from '@estalara/db'; ... db.upsertConversionLabel(tx, ...)` — prints `SKIP` (zero enforcement) in BOTH the co-scoped and out-of-tx directions. This is the exact INTERSECTION of bypass 5 (namespace/property-access delegation, FOLLOW-612) and bypass 6 (barrel re-export, FOLLOW-613) that NEITHER fix closes: FOLLOW-613 upgraded only the NAMED/DEFAULT import-resolution path (`route.ts:291-306`) to run through `resolveExportedNameToConcreteModule`, while the NAMESPACE branch (`:307-308`) still binds the bare barrel entry, and `moduleContainsMutation` cannot follow a barrel's `export … from` re-exports (its walk uses `collectLocalImports`, which visits only `ts.isImportDeclaration`, never `ts.isExportDeclaration`). Verified by controlled reproduction (uncommitted throwaway, deleted, `git status` clean): a namespace import of a CONCRETE module is caught (`FAIL`), a namespace import of a BARREL is not (`SKIP`) — the barrel is the sole differentiator. HYPOTHETICAL today (grep: zero routes use `import * as X from '@estalara/*'`; the only `import * as` sites are `@sentry/nextjs`) — exactly the latent status bypass 6 had at RETRO-197 before FOLLOW-597 made it live — but the highest-likelihood of the four open shapes, because a one-line refactor of the LIVE `labels/[id]` from `import { upsertConversionLabel }` to `import * as db` would silently regress it `OK`→`SKIP`. Filed **FOLLOW-619** (P3, joins 616/617/618 as the 4th open shape). CONVENTIONS_PATCH: **NO PROMOTION** — this IS Rule AE (its point-1 enumeration already names BOTH "a namespace/property-access delegated call" AND "a re-exported wrapper"; the intersection is precisely what AE anticipates), the strongest possible confirmation of AE at its 4th consecutive recurrence, not a new pattern. WIRING clean (CI dev-tooling script; no production symbol; new functions have zero external consumers). — 2026-07-22

### 1. Summary of change

No migrations, no production-code change.
- **Modules touched:** [configs/CI-tooling] ONLY (dev guard script + fixtures + gitleaks allowlist + backlog). NO SDK / control-plane / ingest / decision-api / shared / db-schema / docs.

`Wiring Audit — clean ✅`

- **CHECK A (dead code):** `scripts/check-staff-write-atomicity.cjs` is a CI/dev-tooling entrypoint (run by CI + the test harness — suppressed, non-import consumer). ### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (the finding — a 7th distinct guard bypass, HYPOTHETICAL today, NOT one of FOLLOW-616/617/618) — a NAMESPACE import of a BARREL package + property-access delegated mutation is silently un-enforced (`SKIP`).** Shape: `import * as db from '@estalara/db'; ... await db.upsertConversionLabel(tx, ...)`. Verified by direct reproduction (uncommitted throwaway route tree under a disposable `.repro-throwaway/`, deleted via `git clean -fdx`, `git status` re-confirmed clean): the guard prints `SKIP`, exit 0, for BOTH the mutation co-scoped inside the audit's `db.transaction()` (should be `OK`) AND the byte-identical route with the mutation moved OUTSIDE it (should be `FAIL`) — zero enforcement in both directions, the identical failure class as bypass 4/5/6. **Controlled a/b isolating the root cause:** a namespace import of a CONCRETE module (`import * as store from './real'; store.realUpsert(tx)`) is correctly caught (`FAIL`, bypass 5 stays closed per FOLLOW-612); a namespace import of a BARREL (`import * as store from './barrel'` where the barrel `export { realUpsert as upsertX } from './real'`) is NOT (`SKIP`) — the barrel re-export is the SOLE differentiator. **Root cause, read directly from source (`scripts/check-staff-write-atomicity.cjs`):** `collectLocalImportedIdentifierSources` runs its FOLLOW-613 per-name barrel resolution (`resolveExportedNameToConcreteModule`) ONLY on the named-import (`:298-306`) and default-import (`:290-294`) branches; the NAMESPACE branch (`:307-308`) still does `sources.set(namespaceName, resolvedEntry)` with the bare barrel entry path. When `db.upsertConversionLabel(tx)` is classified (`collectFileFacts` `:432`), it resolves `db`→barrel `index.ts` and calls `moduleContainsMutation(index.ts)` (`:475`) — which finds no DIRECT mutation in the barrel, then walks `collectLocalImports(index.ts)` (`:368`), and `collectLocalImports` (`:709`) visits only `ts.isImportDeclaration` nodes — a barrel has only `ts.isExportDeclaration` re-exports → empty walk → `false` → the call is never promoted to `mutationCalls` → `SKIP`. This is the exact INTERSECTION of bypass 5 (namespace) and bypass 6 (barrel) that FOLLOW-613's module doc-comment mis-declares closed: it states "A NAMESPACE import (`import * as helper`) keeps mapping to the resolved entry module (bypass 5 whole-module semantics)" (`:272-273`) — TRUE for a namespace import of a concrete module, but a silent `SKIP` for a namespace import of a BARREL, because bypass-5 whole-module semantics rely on `moduleContainsMutation` being able to inspect the resolved module, which it cannot do through a barrel's re-exports. **Live status: HYPOTHETICAL** — `grep -rn "import \* as .* from '@estalara/"` across `apps`/`packages` returns zero hits (the only namespace imports in the 6 staff-audited routes are `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nextjs'`, a third-party pkg `resolveSpecifier` returns null for). But it is the HIGHEST-likelihood of the four open shapes: the LIVE `admin/labels/[id]/route.ts` already delegates to `upsertConversionLabel` via a NAMED barrel import — a one-line refactor to `import * as db from '@estalara/db'` (idiomatic, and the exact pattern the `@estalara/db` barrel invites) would silently regress that route `OK`→`SKIP` with CI green. → **FOLLOW-619** (P3, joins 616/617/618 as the 4th open call-shape). This is the Rule AE meta-pattern's 4th consecutive materialization; §6.
- **LG-2 (P4, documented-bound, NO stub) — a mutation helper re-exported through ≥4 NESTED barrels resolves to `SKIP`.** Reproduced: a 4-hop named re-export chain (route→b1→b2→b3→b4→real, each `export { x } from`) prints `SKIP`; a 3-hop chain (route→b1→b2→b3→real) prints `FAIL` (caught) — the boundary is exactly 4 nested barrels, because `resolveExportedNameToConcreteModule`'s named-target shortcut returns the resolved target without recursing at `depth === MAX_DEPTH` (buying one extra level over the `depth-3` bound), then `moduleContainsMutation` cannot follow the 4th barrel's re-export. This is the EXPLICITLY-DOCUMENTED `depth-3` bound (module doc-comment + `resolveExportedNameToConcreteModule` MAX_DEPTH), and is not realistic in-repo (`@estalara/db`'s deepest mutation-helper path is 1 hop; the deepest re-export chain is 2 — `db`→`schema/index`→`<table>` for schema objects, which are not mutation helpers). Not a concrete problem today → per charter, no stub. Recorded so a future retro that hits a real deep-barrel case does not re-derive the boundary.

- **FOLLOW-600 (`/settings` + real `tenants`-table wiring for `/api/config`):** unaffected directly, but its existing AC obligation to keep its future mutation INLINE (not barrel-delegated) so it stays guard-`OK` (RETRO-203 §5b) should be read alongside LG-1 — a namespace-import delegation would ALSO evade the guard, not just a named-import barrel delegation. No AC change needed (inline already satisfies both).

#### 5c. Contracts changed others rely on

- **N/A** — no production/cross-package contract changed. The new guard functions are script-internal (no `module.exports`); the only external artifacts are the `.gitleaks.toml` allowlist entry (CI config) and the FOLLOW stubs.

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

- Reinforces the Rule AE architectural finding that a hand-written AST call-shape guard is only ever a starting point: FOLLOW-613 explicitly enumerated three further shapes (a genuine improvement in discipline over bypass 4/5, which enumerated none) — yet the enumeration STILL missed one, the namespace×barrel intersection, precisely because it sat between two already-"closed" shapes rather than beyond the last one. The durable lesson (already in Rule AE point 3): prefer resolving to the concrete module in the IDENTIFIER-RESOLUTION step over per-syntax special-casing — here, the namespace branch was the one call-classification path NOT upgraded to the per-name barrel resolver, and that omission is the whole gap.

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Meta-pattern (Rule AE — AST-guard call-shape enumeration is never proven complete by closing the shape a regression used):** this is the 4th consecutive materialization on `scripts/check-staff-write-atomicity.cjs` — bypass 4 (RETRO-194) → 5 (RETRO-196, the promotion trigger) → 6 (RETRO-197 latent / RETRO-198 live) → **7 (this retro: namespace-of-barrel)**. **NO PROMOTION — this IS Rule AE, not a new pattern.** Rule AE point 1 already enumerates BOTH "a namespace/property-access delegated call" AND "a re-exported wrapper" as shapes a complete guard must cover; the finding is their INTERSECTION, exactly the class AE anticipates, and Rule AE point 4 is the discipline being exercised right now (a fresh independent reproduction found the same class one shape over → enumerate it NOW → state explicitly: the class is **still open**, tracked by FOLLOW-619, not closed by FOLLOW-613). Promoting a new rule would duplicate AE. Recorded instead as AE's strongest evidence to date (4 hops on one guard). Re: whether AE should be AMENDED to add "and beware the INTERSECTION of two individually-closed shapes" — considered, declined: point 1's "enumerate EVERY syntactic call-shape … before declaring complete" already subsumes intersections; the failure was enforcement of AE point 2 (ask whether the fix covers shapes N+1), not a missing clause.
- **Meta (my own blind-spot watch — recorded per the learning hook):** I nearly stopped after confirming the three shapes the task named (depth, renamed re-export, type-only) all resolved CLEANLY (renamed re-export → FAIL/caught; star-chain → FAIL/caught; depth-3 → caught; depth-4 → the documented bound). The actual live-relevant gap was NONE of those three — it was the namespace×barrel intersection, which I only found by systematically enumerating the CROSS-PRODUCT of {named, namespace, default} imports × {concrete, barrel} sources rather than checking the task's suggested axes in isolation. The controlled a/b (namespace-of-concrete caught vs namespace-of-barrel skipped) was the trace I had to construct to be sure the barrel — not the namespace — was the differentiator.

### 7. Follow-ups

- **FOLLOW-619** (NEW, P3, backend-engineer, 2-3h): Close the guard's namespace-import-of-a-barrel bypass — a `import * as db from '@estalara/db'; db.upsertX(tx, ...)` delegated mutation is silently `SKIP`ped. Route the namespace branch's property-access classification through `resolveExportedNameToConcreteModule` per-accessed-property (mirror the named-import path); red-first fixture pair; correct the module doc-comment's over-claim + the AC-7 enumeration. Joins FOLLOW-616/617/618 as the 4th open call-shape.
- FOLLOW-616/617/618 (EXISTING, referenced): the three shapes FOLLOW-613 enumerated-and-deferred; unchanged, but their "is the space now fully enumerated" AC is now answered NO (619 is the 4th).

### 8. Cross-references

- Related to **RETRO-197 / Rule AE** (FOLLOW-612/613): 613 closes the bypass-6 RETRO-197 predicted; this retro finds the namespace×barrel intersection one shape over — the 4th consecutive AE hop, confirming AE, no promotion.
- Related to **RETRO-198** (FOLLOW-597): 597 made bypass 6 LIVE on `labels/[id]`; 613 restores that route's enforcement (SKIP→OK, re-verified live); LG-1 notes `labels/[id]` is the exact route a namespace-import refactor would regress into the new gap.
- Related to **RETRO-196** (FOLLOW-609→612, bypass 5): LG-1 is bypass 5's namespace/property-access shape applied to bypass 6's barrel target — the two "closed" shapes whose intersection is open.
- Related to **RETRO-194 / RETRO-192** (FOLLOW-608/609, bypasses 3/4): the earlier hops of the same Rule AE arc on this guard.

## RETRO-205 — FOLLOW-600 (per-tenant `/admin/tenants/[id]/settings` staff surface + `/api/config` wired to the REAL `tenants` table, PR #606, merged `19ef714` 2026-07-23T21:27:05Z) — session-56 retrospective-analyst (Opus). **HEADLINE — the ROUTE layer is correct and independently re-verified (auth, INV-5 fence, FOLLOW-615 write-rank gate, §3a single-`db.transaction()` atomicity, guard `OK` live on `main`), but the SURFACE it ships is a FACADE: BOTH column families this PR makes writable — `tenants.allowed_origins` and `tenants.brand_config.{primary_color,logo_url,white_label}` — have ZERO runtime consumers anywhere in the repo, so every control on the new page is producer-only. The "SDK Allowed Origins" box in particular promises a SECURITY control (`tenants.ts:35` "Domains where the Estalara SDK snippet is permitted to run"; MASTER_DESIGN §V.3.4:5021 "Origin validated against tenant.allowed_origins config") that no code enforces — ingest CORS is a hardcoded per-env list (`apps/ingest/src/router.ts:69-73`). TWO HALF_WIRE_P (P1). Separately, LG-1 (P1): the new client SWALLOWS its GET failure (`tenant-config-editor.tsx:76` `.catch(() => {})`) and then PATCHes a FULL body — so a failed load renders plausible DEFAULTS and one click clobbers the tenant's real brand config and WIPES `allowed_origins` to `[]`; this is the exact consumer-side swallow Rule K.2 already forbids AND already greps for, shipped verbatim for the THIRD consecutive staff editor (quiz FOLLOW-595, demo FOLLOW-596, settings FOLLOW-600) — which CONTRADICTS RETRO-193's end-to-end "clean" verdict on the demo surface (that retro analyzed the staff-write axis only, never the client load-failure axis). PROCESS: the merge landed BEFORE any AC validation ran, with "CI green" as the sole control — on a repo where the aggregate `CI` workflow conclusion on `main` is `failure` on EVERY push (Rule I, now 191 violations, up from 179 at FOLLOW-591 → 183 at RETRO-187) and where a SECOND workflow (`Release`) has failed on every run in the last 30 with ZERO mentions in RETROSPECTIVES.md / FOLLOW_UPS.md / QUEUE.md / ESCALATIONS.md. That pattern crosses the ≥2-PRIOR-retro threshold → **Rule AF PROMOTED**. Filed FOLLOW-622…629.) — 2026-07-23

### 1. Summary of change

- **PR:** #606 (merged 2026-07-23 21:27:05 UTC, squash commit `19ef714`, by Pnawrocki9; branch
  `backend-engineer/FOLLOW-600-tenant-settings-surface`). Post-merge close-out commit `07fd72b`.
  Preceded by #607 (`f4dd037`, FOLLOW-620, CH CI image pin) merged 21:12:47Z — a repo-wide CI
  un-breaker, not a dependency of #606's content.
- **Files changed:** 8 (+1298 / -211); no migrations, no schema changes, no new package.
- **Modules touched:** control-plane (1 API route + 1 server page + 1 client component + 4 test
  files). No SDK, ingest, decision-api, Modal, docs, or config changes.

### 3. Wiring Audit

**CHECK A — dead code: clean ✅.** New files: `settings/page.tsx` (Next.js framework route —
suppressed), `settings/tenant-config-editor.tsx` (imported at `settings/page.tsx:26`, rendered at
`:52` — wired), `api/config/route.ts` (framework route — suppressed). New exports: `BrandConfig`,
`TenantConfig`, `ConfigPatch` are **type-only** (suppressed); `StaffTenantConfigEditor` has a real
non-test importer. Corroborated against the actual Rule I job log for this PR (run `30045335580`, job
`89335797339`): 191 violations listed, **none of them from this PR** (grepped the full log for
`StaffTenant|TenantConfig|BrandConfig|ConfigPatch` → zero hits).

**CHECK B — half-wire: TWO FINDINGS, both P1 HALF_WIRE_P.**

- **HW-1 — `tenants.allowed_origins` — HALF_WIRE_P (P1) → FOLLOW-622.**
  - Producer (NEW, this PR): `api/config/route.ts:299,303` (`allowedOrigins: updatedOrigins`) driven by
    the "SDK Allowed Origins" textarea at `settings/tenant-config-editor.tsx:91`.
  - Consumer: **NONE.** `grep -rn "allowedOrigins\|allowed_origins" apps packages --include=*.ts
    --include=*.tsx` (excl. node_modules/.next) returns: this route, this editor, the schema
    (`packages/db/src/schema/tenants.ts:35`), test DDL fixtures — and two allowlists that are

    (`allowedOriginsForEnv` → `PROD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` ± `DEV_EXTRA_ORIGINS`) and

    (`tenants.ts:34`) says "Domains where the Estalara SDK snippet is permitted to run".

  - Zero prior retro has ever mentioned `allowed_origins` (`grep -c` on RETROSPECTIVES.md → 0), so this

- **HW-2 — `tenants.brand_config.{primary_color,logo_url,white_label}` — HALF_WIRE_P (P1) → FOLLOW-623.**

**NOT a half-wire (verified, step-7 closure):** the new `staff_audit_log` action `tenant_config.update`
is fully consumed. FOLLOW-599 replaced the `MOCK_ENTRIES` stub with real reads
(`api/audit/route.ts` — `eq(staffAuditLog.targetTenantId, access.tenantId)`, `action` typed as a plain
`string` with **no allowlist**), and the render leg exists:
`admin/tenants/[id]/audit/audit-view.tsx:105` prints `{e.action}` generically. Producer → consumer →
render traced end-to-end; a 6th action needs no code change to appear. This is the pre-existing
HALF_WIRE_P from RETRO-190/193/198/199 now genuinely CLOSED, not moved one hop.

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P1) — the editor swallows its load failure, then the next click clobbers real config.**
  `settings/tenant-config-editor.tsx:60-78`: the GET does check `r.ok` (`:61 if (!r.ok) throw`) but
  throws straight into `:76 .catch(() => { /* Load silently — defaults already set; a save still fails
  loud below. */ })`. On a 500 (the route's own Rule K.2 path), a 403, or a network blip the component
  keeps `DEFAULTS` (`:34-38` — `#1a73e8`, `logo_url:null`, `white_label:false`, `allowed_origins:[]`)
  and renders them as if they were the tenant's stored config. There is no loading/error state on the
  read path; only `plan` renders as `'—'`. Then `handleSave` (`:82-96`) always PATCHes a **complete**
  body (`brand: config.brand`, `sdk.allowed_origins: parseOriginsInput(originsInput)`), and the route
  merges present keys unconditionally (`route.ts:288-299`; `logo_url` uses an explicit
  `!== undefined` check so `null` is a legitimate write, and `updatedOrigins = patch.sdk?.allowed_origins
  ?? currentOrigins` accepts `[]` as a real value). Net effect: **failed load + one Save = the tenant's
  brand config is overwritten with defaults and its origin allowlist is wiped to `[]`, with a green
  "Settings saved!" confirmation.** The route was deliberately hardened to fail loud; the client throws
  that away — the gap moved exactly one hop downstream, which is the failure mode this retro loop
  exists to catch.
  - **Systemic, not local:** `grep -rn "catch(() => {" -A3 apps/control-plane/src/app/admin --include=*.tsx`
    returns the identical block with the identical comment in **three** editors —
    `quiz/quiz-config-editor.tsx:72`, `demo/demo-override-editor.tsx:87`, `settings/tenant-config-editor.tsx:76`.
    It was copied forward through FOLLOW-595 → 596 → 600.
  - **This is an existing-rule violation, not a new pattern.** Rule K.2's consumer-side clause is
    explicit ("A producer that fails loud paired with a consumer that swallows the failure … is the
    same defect one layer up") and its own **Verification** block literally ships the grep that finds
    all three: `grep -rn "catch(() =>" apps/ --include="*.ts" | grep -v node_modules`. The rule existed;
    nothing mechanical ran it. → **FOLLOW-624** (fix the three editors) + **FOLLOW-625** (mechanise the
    check).
  - **Contradiction with a prior "clean" verdict (reconciled):** RETRO-193 declared FOLLOW-596's demo
    surface clean "end-to-end … producer→consumer→render, NOT a one-hop", and RETRO-198/200 likewise
    treated the quiz/labels/intent editors as clean. Those verdicts are correct **on the staff-write
    axis they analysed** and wrong as a whole-surface verdict: none of them examined the client's READ
    path. I am explicitly re-opening that axis for all three surfaces; the write-path conclusions stand
    unchanged.
- **LG-2 (P3) — GET fabricates a full config for a missing tenant row, PATCH reports a phantom success,
  and a test locks the behaviour in.** `route.ts:186-191` maps a missing row to
  `plan:'free'`, default brand, `allowed_origins:[]`, `updated_at: new Date()` and returns **200**.
  Fourteen lines earlier, the same handler's Rule K.2 comment (`:194-196`) says the opposite: "Returning
  fabricated defaults here would silently misrepresent the tenant's real config on a staff/agency-facing
  settings surface." Both branches cannot be right. On PATCH the same shape produces a 0-row
  `db.update()` that still returns 200 with the "saved" body (`:376-381`). Reach is narrow — staff hit
  `tenantExists` first (404, `session-auth.ts:446-449`) and agency tenant ids come from a signed JWT — so
  the live window is "tenant deleted/soft-deleted while a session is alive", hence P3 not P1. What
  raises it above noise is that `route.test.ts:376` (`'returns defaults (never an error) when the tenant
  row is not found'`) **asserts** the fabrication, so it will survive refactors and any future reader.
  Compounding: `TenantConfig` carries no `data_source`/provenance field, unlike every sibling ADR-0018
  surface (`/api/audit` `data_source:'real'|'mock'`, the analytics/tenant loaders' `live|mock|error`),
  so a caller cannot distinguish stored values from invented ones — the exact sub-shape of the Rule K.2
  amendment of 2026-06-13 (RETRO-072, provenance-enum completeness). → **FOLLOW-627**.
- **LG-3 (P3) — `allowed_origins` is validated as URLs, not as origins.** `route.ts:114-116` uses
  `z.array(z.string().url())`, which accepts `https://x.com/some/path?q=1`, `http://…`, and any scheme.
  An origin allowlist is compared as scheme+host+port (that is exactly how `ingest/src/router.ts:118`
  does `(allowed as string[]).includes(requestOrigin)`), so a stored value with a path will never match
  a browser `Origin` header. There is also no dedupe, no length cap, and no rejection of the empty array
  (`[]` is written as-is; whether that means "deny all" or "inherit" is undefined because there is no
  consumer to define it). Inert today precisely because of HW-1 — which is why it must be fixed *with*
  HW-1, not after. Folded into **FOLLOW-622**.

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught (P0/P1/P2)

- No additional live defect beyond LG-1 (P1) and LG-2/LG-3 (P3), which I classify as logic gaps.
  Adversarial passes that came back **clean**: auth (no `x-tenant-id`/`x-agency-role` read survives —
  `route.ts:159-171,206-218`), INV-5 fence (`eq(tenants.id, access.tenantId)` bound into all four
  queries, `:180,:270,:314`), the `via==='staff' && !access.canWrite → 403` rank gate ordered **before**
  body parsing and any DB touch (`:221-227`), audit attribution (`adminUserId: access.staff.sub`, only
  reachable on the staff branch — the `TenantAccess` union makes `access.staff` structurally
  unavailable on the agency branch), atomicity + rollback + Sentry + fail-loud 500 (`:311-357`), and the
  agency branch left byte-equivalent and deliberately un-audited per ADR-0018 §3.
- **P3 (folded into FOLLOW-624):** the editor's Logo URL field is free text with no client validation,
  while the schema demands `.url()`; a typo yields a 400 whose `details` the error extractor
  (`tenant-config-editor.tsx:99-101`) discards, surfacing only "Invalid request body". Same for a
  malformed origin line.

#### 4c. Test coverage gaps

- **TG-1 (P1, the one that let LG-1 through):** `tenant-config-editor.test.tsx` has exactly **three**
  tests (`:49` renders controls, `:67` no generation-model control, `:82` PATCHes on save) and **all
  three stub a successful GET**. There is no failed-load test, so nothing exercises the defaults-render
  path and nothing asserts that a Save after a failed load is prevented. Covered by FOLLOW-624's AC.
- **TG-2 (P3):** `settings/page.test.tsx` has two tests (404 for unknown tenant, editor renders). No
  test asserts what a `estalara:readonly` staff user sees — today they get a fully editable form and
  discover the 403 only on Save. Rank-aware UI is arguably out of ADR-0018 §4's scope (the gate is
  server-side and correct), so this is UX, not security. Noted, no ticket.
- **TG-3 (P3):** the route suite asserts the LG-2 fabrication as desired behaviour rather than
  questioning it (`route.test.ts:376`). FOLLOW-627 must flip this test, not just the code.

#### 4d. Documentation gaps

- **DG-1 (P1, owned by FOLLOW-622):** `docs/MASTER_DESIGN.md:5011-5024` (§V.3.4) documents per-tenant
  origin validation at the ingest endpoint that does not exist in code. Whichever way FOLLOW-622 is
  resolved (enforce it, or de-scope the control), §V.3.4 and the `api_keys.allowedOrigins` "inherit"
  comment must be brought into line — a design doc that over-states a security control is worse than
  silence.
- **DG-2 (none):** `docs/compliance/ropa.md:260` lists `allowed_origins` and `brand_config` as tenant
  data categories — accurate (they *are* stored), so there is **no** compliance/ROPA divergence. Checked
  explicitly; recorded so a future retro doesn't re-open it.

### 5. Cascading impact

#### 5a. Current sprint tickets affected

- **FOLLOW-604** (P3, staff port of `PATCH /api/tenants/[id]` — the quiz ON/OFF toggle): unaffected but
  now fenced by `api/config/route.ts:56-64` — quiz fields must NOT be threaded through `/api/config`
  (they stay on the FOLLOW-595 surface). The route's docstring states this; the ticket AC should keep it.
- **FOLLOW-616/617/618/619** (guard call-shape bypasses, all P3/hypothetical): unaffected — this route's
  mutation is INLINE, so it is guard-`OK` and cannot regress into a barrel/namespace bypass unless
  refactored.
- **FOLLOW-621** (CH 26.x compat, P3): unaffected by #606, but see §5d — it now silently carries CI's
  version-skew debt.
- No IN_PROGRESS ticket's assumptions are invalidated by this merge.

#### 5b. Future sprint tickets affected

- Any ticket that claims "the per-tenant settings surface is live" is over-claiming until FOLLOW-622/623
  land — the page is currently a persistence layer with no effect.
- Whoever implements FOLLOW-622 must choose an enforcement point (ingest Worker vs `/api/adapt` vs
  decision-api) and will need a tenant lookup on a hot path — a genuine design decision, not a
  mechanical wiring job, which is why it is 4h and not 1h.

#### 5c. Contracts changed others rely on

- `staff_audit_log.action` — 6th value; consumers are generic, verified (§3).
- `/api/config` request/response — sole consumer is this PR's own editor; nothing external to break.
- `tenants.allowed_origins` / `tenants.brand_config` — these now have live writers. Any future consumer
  must assume the values are **operator-entered and unvalidated as origins** (LG-3) and that most
  tenants' rows are still at their `'{}'` / `[]` defaults because there was never a producer before.

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

- **A-1 — NORMALIZED DEVIANCE ON RED CI GATES (severity: HIGH; PM escalation candidate — surfaced here
  per my scope, not escalated).** Asked directly whether a permanently-red gate is eroding the gate set:
  **yes, measurably, and it is now worse than the last time anyone measured.**
  1. `Rule I — wired-or-dead` fails on `main` itself. Violation count over time: **179** when FOLLOW-591
     was filed (SESSION-RETRO 39) → **183** at RETRO-187 (2026-07-20) → **191** on #606's run
     (2026-07-23, job `89335797339`). +12 dead exports have landed unnoticed since the ticket was
     filed, exactly as FOLLOW-591 predicted ("it degrades the CI signal for ALL future work and
     compounds"). #606 itself added **zero** — verified, not assumed — but nobody could have known that
     without reading the log, and nobody did.
  2. Because Rule I is a job inside the `CI` workflow, the **aggregate `CI` workflow conclusion on
     `main` is `failure` on every push** (`f4dd037`, `54e76a7`, `68e6f29`, `67a35e8` — all `failure`;
     `19ef714` `cancelled`). "Is main green?" has no readable answer at the workflow level.
  3. **A second permanently-red workflow that no backlog file mentions at all:** `Release` has
     `conclusion: failure` on **every run in the last 30** and there is **no successful run in the last
     100**. Cause (log, run for `07fd72b`): `changeset publish` → `@estalara/sdk@0.1.0` →
     `E403 … PUT https://npm.pkg.github.com/@estalara%2fsdk - Permission not_found: owner not found`
     (the `@estalara` scope does not resolve under the `Pnawrocki9` package registry). Grep of
     RETROSPECTIVES.md / FOLLOW_UPS.md / QUEUE.md / ESCALATIONS.md for `Release workflow` /
     `npm.pkg.github` / `E403` → **zero hits**. It runs on every push to main, burns ~2.5 min, and fails
     silently into the void. That is the concrete cost of the normalization: a *second* gate reached
     terminal-red and no one noticed for at least three days. → **FOLLOW-626**.
  4. Combined with §2's process deviation, the merge control for #606 was "CI green" evaluated against a
     baseline that is red in two places and unmeasured in one. It came out fine. That is luck, not
     process. → **Rule AF** (§6).
- **A-2 — Merge-before-AC-validation (count 1, banked, NOT promoted).** #606 merged ahead of the PM's
  validation gate; the AC audit ran afterwards and found the ACs met. The risk is not this instance but
  the ordering: had the audit found a gap, the remedy would have been a revert or a follow-up PR on
  `main` instead of a change request on a branch. Rule A binds the PM's READY_FOR_REVIEW transition, not
  the merge click. One sighting — no rule, no ticket. Arming condition: a **second** merge that precedes
  AC validation promotes this (the natural home is a Rule A amendment, not a new letter).
- **A-3 — Interrupted-PM-run recovery: the hazard is real and recurrent, but nothing was left
  inconsistent this time (verified, not assumed).** Session 54's dispatch of FOLLOW-600 died mid-run,
  stranding the implementation uncommitted in the agent worktree; session 55 recovered it per the
  standing "check worktrees before concluding the agent never ran" lesson (this is the **third** such
  stranding — FOLLOW-557/PR #528, FOLLOW-593/PR #581, now FOLLOW-600 — and the remedy ticket
  **FOLLOW-573 (P2) is still open and unscheduled** since RETRO-175). Consistency sweep run this
  session: `git status --porcelain` → clean; `.claude/worktrees` → absent; FOLLOW_UPS.md FOLLOW-600 →
  `DONE + MERGED (PR #606, 19ef714)`; FOLLOW-620 → `DONE + MERGED (PR #607, f4dd037)`; QUEUE.md
  START-HERE reflects both merges; next-free markers (FOLLOW 622 / RETRO 205) match reality; no
  duplicate or half-written entries. **No orphaned backlog edits found.** The one residual artefact of
  the interrupted/rapid-commit pattern is §2's cancelled `main` CI run, not lost work. Recommendation
  stands from FOLLOW-573, not re-filed here.
- **A-4 — CI↔prod ClickHouse version skew introduced by #607's pin (a hidden expiry, partially
  tracked).** FOLLOW-621's third AC does carry the un-pin obligation ("After it lands: un-pin OR bump
  the FOLLOW-620 CI pin to a 26.x tag in the SAME PR"), so the expiry is *documented* — but it is P3
  "opportunistic" with no trigger that ever fires on its own. Meanwhile CI now proves the migration
  chain against **25.8** while prod ClickHouse Cloud runs whatever version ClickHouse Cloud decides;
  the moment prod crosses into 26.x, the CH gates stop being evidence for prod and **nothing in the repo
  will notice** — the failure mode would be a green CI and a broken prod migration, which is strictly
  worse than the loud repo-wide breakage #607 just fixed. → **FOLLOW-629** (a version-drift detector on
  the existing daily CH schema-validation cron; cheap, and it converts a silent expiry into a loud one).
- **A-5 — Other unpinned upstream dependencies in CI (swept, one real finding).** Full sweep of all 12
  workflows: only two `image:` entries exist and both are now pinned (`ci.yml:302,361`). Remaining
  floats, in descending risk: (a) **`pip install modal httpx fastapi` — `modal-deploy.yml:66`,
  completely unpinned, running under `environment: production`, and it is the step that registers and
  deploys the prod Modal ML functions.** This is the same class as `clickhouse-server:latest` with a
  larger blast radius — an upstream `modal` CLI major bump can change deploy semantics against
  production with no repo change; (b) `sudo apt-get install -y k6` (`load-test.yml:40`) — same class,
  low stakes; (c) all `actions/*@v4`, `pnpm/action-setup@v4`, `dopplerhq/cli-action@v3`,
  `cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3`, `gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v2`, `changesets/action@v1` float on major
  tags — industry-normal, out of scope. → **FOLLOW-628** for (a) + (b).

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **P-1 — "A CI gate that is permanently red is functionally a disabled gate: the red is normalized,
  new regressions inside it are invisible, and a second gate can reach terminal-red without anyone
  noticing."** Seen in: **SESSION-RETRO 39** (filed FOLLOW-591 at 179 violations, arguing exactly this),
  **RETRO-187** §2/§6 (183 violations; "the standing pre-existing non-blocking Rule I noise"; declined
  promotion at "single sighting"), **RETRO-188** §5/§6 (+8 more; filed FOLLOW-602), **RETRO-205**
  (this — 191 violations, plus the previously-unseen `Release` workflow red on every run, plus a merge
  decided on "CI green"). Promote-threshold 2, **current count 3 PRIOR + this one → THRESHOLD MET →
  PROMOTED as Rule AF** (§CONVENTIONS_PATCH). The promoting retro does not inflate the count (same
  adjudication as Rules AA/AB/AC/AD/AE/V/Q). Note this is deliberately NOT a duplicate of FOLLOW-591:
  591 is the *remediation ticket* for one gate; AF is the *behavioural rule* that stops the next gate
  from rotting while 591 sits unscheduled, and it makes the baseline comparison an explicit obligation.
- **P-2 — "A staff editor swallows its GET failure, renders DEFAULTS as if they were stored values, and
  then PATCHes a FULL body — so one click clobbers real data."** 3 code instances (quiz/demo/settings)
  but **count 1 as a retro finding** — RETRO-193 and RETRO-198/200 saw these surfaces and declared them
  clean on the write axis. **NOT promoted**, and deliberately so: this is already Rule K.2's
  consumer-side clause, whose Verification block already ships the exact grep that finds all three. The
  failure is *enforcement*, not a missing rule — the same diagnosis RETRO-204 reached for Rule AE
  ("point-1 already enumerates it; the failure was point-2 enforcement"). Remedy is mechanical
  (FOLLOW-625), not textual. **Arming condition:** if a fourth instance ships *after* FOLLOW-624/625
  land, that is a recurrence-despite-a-fix and warrants a Rule K.2 amendment codifying "a staff editor
  MUST NOT enable its write control until a successful read has populated it".
- **P-3 — "A new UI producer for a long-inert column passes every wiring gate, because Rule H checks
  consumers at schema-creation time and Rule I only sees exported symbols."** Count 1 (this retro, but
  **two independent instances inside one PR** — HW-1 and HW-2; per the anti-undercount guardrail both
  are listed separately in §3 and get separate tickets). **Held, not promoted.** Arming condition: the
  next staff surface that ships a control over a zero-consumer column.
- **P-4 — "A pin applied to un-break CI creates an untriggered expiry."** Count 1 (A-4). Held; the
  detector in FOLLOW-629 is the cheap remedy, and if a second pin-with-no-trigger appears this becomes
  a candidate amendment to Rule Q (gate-must-prove-it-ran) rather than a new letter.

## RETRO-206 — FOLLOW-624 (stop staff config editors clobbering config on load failure) — 2026-07-24

### 1. Summary of change

- **PR:** #608 (merged 2026-07-24 07:28 UTC, squash commit `3b0b4a3`)
- **Files changed:** 7 (+508 / −15) — 3 editor components, 3 new `.test.tsx`, 1 lessons doc
- **Modules touched:** [control-plane (staff admin UI), docs (agent lessons)]
- **Key contracts changed:** none. No schema/event/column/env/SDK-signal added. Pure consumer-side
  bugfix to three already-wired editors of `/api/config`, `/api/quiz/config`, `/api/demo/override`
  (each `?tenant_id=<id>`). A new internal `loadStatus` state was added *inside* each component
  (not a cross-module contract). `tenant-config-editor` additionally now reads the route's existing
  zod `.flatten().details` (a field the route already emitted — new consumer of an existing signal,
  not a new producer). breaking: no.

### 2. Verification done in PR

- Test files changed: 3 new (`tenant-config-editor.test.tsx` +105, `quiz-config-editor.test.tsx`
  +108 [was ZERO before], `demo-override-editor.test.tsx` +110 [was ZERO before]). Assertions added:
  per editor — GET-rejects/500 → error alert + Save disabled + no PATCH/POST/PUT issued; GET-succeeds
  → unchanged; retry-recovers-without-reload; (tenant-config only) validation-`details`-surfaced.
  Coverage delta: +2 previously-untested editors now covered; the TG-1 hole RETRO-205 named is closed
  **on the three admin editors**. Red-first per AC3 (7 failed / 6 passed pre-fix, then green).
- CI checks: PR body claims `tsc`/eslint/prettier/`check-rule-h.sh`/pre-push hooks all green; ESC-039
  resolution note confirms all real gates green (only pre-existing repo-wide `Rule I` red, also red on
  `main` `d89757f` — not a regression). Not independently re-run this session (read-only retro).

### 3. Wiring Audit

**CHECK A (dead code) — clean ✅.** No new file/export added (the two new component files are `.test.tsx`,
suppressed as test files; the three edited components are pre-existing and each rendered by a live page
wrapper — `admin/tenants/[id]/{settings,quiz,demo}/page.tsx`). No orphaned symbol.

**CHECK B (half-wire) — clean ✅** for what the PR added. The new `loadStatus` state is produced (fetch
outcome) and consumed (alert render + Save-disable + `handleSave` early-return) inside each component —
producer→consumer→render all present. The newly-read validation `details` has a live producer
(`/api/config` route's zod `.flatten()`), so it is not a consumer-only half-wire.

*(The systemic finding below is NOT a wiring-audit class — it is an INCOMPLETE-FIX / gap-moved-one-hop
finding, recorded in §4a and §8, per the step-7 closure-trace discipline.)*

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P1, HEADLINE — the fix is incomplete; the gap moved one hop, not closed).** FOLLOW-624 fixed
  the **three admin/staff editors** under `admin/tenants/[id]/` but left **three sibling consumers with
  the byte-identical swallow-then-Save-defaults shape untouched** — and two of them write to the *exact
  same routes* the fixed editors write to:
  1. `apps/control-plane/src/app/dashboard/quiz/page.tsx:96-114` — `void fetch('/api/quiz/config')`,
     `if (!r.ok) throw` (`:98-100`) straight into `.catch(() => { /* load silently — defaults already
     set */ })` (`:111-113`); `handleSave` (`:162-187`) POSTs the **full** `config` blob
     (`JSON.stringify(config)`, `:171`) to the **same `/api/quiz/config`** the fixed
     `quiz/quiz-config-editor.tsx` writes. Failed GET + Save = tenant's live SDK-consumed
     `quiz_config` (`accent_color`, `language`, `micro_polls_enabled`) reverts to `DEFAULTS` (`:72-75`)
     under "Settings saved!". **This is the ORIGINAL surface the admin editor was copied FROM**
     (FOLLOW-595). Tenant-operated → routine use → arguably higher blast radius than the staff path.
     Severity **P1**.
  2. `apps/control-plane/src/app/dashboard/demo/override/page.tsx:89-108` — **worse**: the load has
     **no `!r.ok` guard at all** (`:91 .then((r) => r.json())`), so a 500's error body is parsed as
     config and `d.enabled ?? false` (`:96`) renders DEMO MODE **OFF** with no alert; `.catch(() => {})`
     (`:105-107`) swallows network rejects. `handleSave` (`:110-148`) PUTs the full override to the
     **same `/api/demo/override`** as the fixed `demo/demo-override-editor.tsx`. Failed/errored GET +
     Save = a tenant's live DEMO override is silently turned OFF or reset. Severity **P1**.
  3. `apps/control-plane/src/components/generation-model-settings.tsx:71-91` — `.catch(() => { /* Load
     silently — defaults already set */ })` (`:88-90`), no `!r.ok` guard (`:73 .then((r) => r.json())`);
     `handleSave` (`:93-127`) PUTs `{ generation_model }` to `/api/admin/generation-model`. Failed GET
     renders the `'claude-sonnet-4-6'` default (`:62`); a Save resets the **GLOBAL** description-
     generation model and busts the description cache. Smaller blast radius (single global value; only
     staff PUT succeeds — agency gets a server-side 403, so the agency-side clobber is blocked at the
     route, not the client), so **P2** — but same class, and it is the SHARED component rendered by
     **both** `/admin/settings` and `/dashboard/settings` (`grep -rln GenerationModelSettings app` →
     both), so the swallow is live in both zones from one file.

  Grep that finds all six (three fixed + three missed):
  `grep -rn "catch(() =>" apps/control-plane/src --include=*.tsx` (Rule K.2's own Verification block
  specifies the **repo-wide** `grep -rn "catch(() =>" apps/`; FOLLOW-624's PR body instead ran
  `grep … apps/control-plane/src/app/admin` — the rule's wide grep was narrowed to `/admin`, which is
  precisely why the three non-`/admin` twins were not seen). → **FOLLOW-630**.

- **LG-2 (P2, FOLLOW-625 mechanization is itself under-scoped).** FOLLOW-625's AC scopes the CI guard to
  `apps/control-plane/src/app/**`. `generation-model-settings.tsx` lives in **`src/components/`**, OUTSIDE
  that glob — so the mechanized guard, as specified, would catch the two dashboard `app/**` twins
  (LG-1.1/1.2) but **silently miss the shared component (LG-1.3)**, re-creating the same scope-blind-spot
  one level down. The guard's own proof AC ("the three FOLLOW-624-fixed editors pass") validates only
  against the admin three, so a green FOLLOW-625 could ship while LG-1.3 still swallows. → amendment
  appended to **FOLLOW-625** AC (scope must include `src/components/**` and any client component that
  populates editable state, not only `src/app/**`).

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught (P0/P1/P2)

- The three LG-1 instances ARE the live defect (classified as logic gaps, consistent with RETRO-205's
  treatment of the identical admin instances as §4a LG-1). No *additional* bug in the merged diff: the
  fix on the three admin editors is correct and end-to-end (traced in §8). Adversarial pass on the fix
  came back clean — `handleSave` early-returns on `loadStatus !== 'loaded'` as defense-in-depth beyond
  the disabled button; the no-row 200 case is correctly left as legitimate state (not treated as error).

#### 4c. Test coverage gaps

- **TG-1 (P1, folded into FOLLOW-630).** The three new admin test files assert BOTH load directions, but
  the three dashboard/shared twins (LG-1) have **no failed-load test** — `dashboard/quiz/page.tsx` and
  `generation-model-settings.tsx` tests (where they exist) stub a successful GET, the exact hole RETRO-205
  TG-1 named for the admin side, still open on the dashboard side. FOLLOW-630 must ship red-first
  failed-load + no-write tests for all three, mirroring FOLLOW-624 AC3.

#### 4d. Documentation gaps
