    `:127-132`, without reconciling. `apps/ingest/src/observability.ts:8` confirms Sentry no-ops
    without the DSN. The fallback channel is no better: `apps/ingest/wrangler.toml` has **no
    `logpush` and no `tail_consumers`** (grep returns nothing), so `logger.warn` is retrievable only
    during a live `wrangler tail` session.
  - Why this is P1 and not a doc nit: **AC 2's entire stated purpose** — quoted verbatim in the
    shipped docstring at `handlers/events.ts:47-52` — is that "a mis-pasted env is visible in
    Sentry/logs **without needing** a request to fail." On the ingest plane that sentence is false
    today. The same mute also silences the *pre-existing* `origin_policy_unconfigured` Sentry ERROR
    (`events.ts:212`), which §5a shows is the **only** automated detector of the residual
    wrong-value failure this PR consciously did not close in code.
- **Note 1 — no new env var; the operator producer is unchanged and still unvalidated.** Nothing in
  either app checks the pasted UUID against a real `tenants.id`, though the control-plane already
  holds a Postgres handle in the same function that reads it (`brand-identity.ts:298-303`). See §4a
  LG-2 / FOLLOW-695.
- **Note 2 — the runbook probe is a *manual* consumer, and the charter's precedent says so.** The
  §Step 0 2xx probe (`BRAND_PROVISIONING.md:107-134`) is the only end-to-end verification that the
  three unsynced stores agree. RETRO-220's Rule AH adjudication ("documentation standing in for code
  is a deferral, not a closure") applies; FOLLOW-662 already exists to mechanize exactly this class
  of operator-executable instruction. Not re-filed; cross-referenced in §5b.

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P2) → FOLLOW-695 — the FOLLOW-660 400 message is now false in a SECOND way, on a branch
  this PR created.** With a **malformed** env, `isTreatedAsExternalBrand` no longer takes the
  exact-match branch; it falls through to the tenant-count probe (`brand-identity.ts:300-306`). So
  malformed + ≥2 tenants + omitted hash now reaches step 7b, which answers 400 with
  *"consent_text_hash is required: FIRST_PARTY_TENANT_ID is not configured and more than one tenant
  exists"* (`api/v1/consent/platform-registration/route.ts:380-383`) and tells the operator to go
  set the env. **The env IS configured** — it is garbled. The operator will open Doppler/Vercel, see
  a value, and conclude the message is wrong. This is RETRO-222 §4a LG-2's defect shape (a
  fail-closed path asserting a state that is false on the branch that reached it) acquiring its
  **third** reaching branch: count>1, count-read-failure, and now malformed-env. Same sentence, same
  file, three different causes. Note honestly that FOLLOW-674 already asks for the count-read split;
  FOLLOW-695 extends it rather than duplicating it.
- **LG-2 (P2) → FOLLOW-695 — the residual wrong-value axis is closeable in code on the control-plane
  plane and was not closed.** `isTreatedAsExternalBrand` already has `db` in hand and already
  queries `tenants` on the fallback path. A `valid` env that matches **no** `tenants.id` row is
  provably an operator typo and is distinguishable from an intentional scoping — unlike on the
  ingest plane, where the Worker has no Postgres on a zero-I/O hot path and the PR's "not
  distinguishable by construction" claim (`INGEST_WORKER_DEPLOY.md:130-132`) is **correct**. Scoping
  the honesty in both directions: a control-plane check does **not** prove the *ingest* secret is
  right, because the three stores are unsynced by design — but it converts the most likely operator
  error (one mistyped digit, pasted identically everywhere) from "silent 100% traffic loss detected
  by a manual probe" into "a startup/first-use warning with a real DSN behind it."
- **LG-3 (P3, note only — traced, NOT filed) — a malformed env now costs a DB round-trip per
  request on three control-plane surfaces.** Pre-fix, malformed took the zero-query exact-match
  branch; post-fix it probes `tenants` on every consent GET, consent POST and DSR initiate. The
  trade is correct (deny-everyone was the worse outcome) and the state is an error state, so this is
  recorded rather than ticketed. It does, however, mean **FOLLOW-674's soft-delete-blind probe
  (RETRO-222 §4a LG-1) gains a fourth way to be reached.**

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught — N/A. Six claims re-verified rather than accepted:

- **"All three comparison functions canonicalized"** — true at the merge commit; each of
  `origin-gate.ts:222-232`, `brand-identity.ts:226-229`, `brand-identity.ts:290-296` applies
  `.trim().toLowerCase()` to the tenant operand and compares against `resolved.value`, which is
  already trimmed + lower-cased.
- **"Malformed degrades to OFF, never deny-all"** — true on both planes, and the two meanings of
  "off" differ correctly per plane (ingest: guard disabled; control-plane: fall through to the
  count probe, which is the FOLLOW-660 safety net, not a blanket allow).
- **The compliance direction of the malformed fallback is SAFE, contrary to first appearance** —
  I checked whether routing malformed into the count probe re-opens the FOLLOW-660 fabrication.
  It does not: ≤1 tenant → the only tenant *is* Estalara, so defaulting the canonical hash is
  correct; >1 tenants → the probe requires an explicit hash. Both sub-cases verified against
  `brand-identity.ts:300-306` + `route.ts:375-386`. Stated explicitly because the axis is
  non-obvious and a future reader will otherwise re-derive it.
- **Warn-once placement is not gated on the failure** — `events.ts:157` runs unconditionally after
  auth, before the `policy.mode` branch, so a malformed env warns even when no request would have
  been refused. That is what AC 2 asked for and it is implemented correctly. (It does require ≥1
  *authenticated* request to fire; a total auth outage would suppress it. Negligible.)
- **Module-level warn-once state is right for both runtimes** — a CF isolate and a warm Vercel
  instance both reuse module scope; both reset on redeploy, which is the desired "a fixed env stops
  warning" behavior.
- **`UUID_RE` does not over-reject real ids** — it is shape-only (no version/variant nibble
  constraint), so Postgres-generated v4 ids and the repo's hand-written fixtures both pass. A
  stricter RFC-4122 regex would have rejected e.g. `route.test.ts:65`'s
  `a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890`. The looser choice is the correct one.

#### 4c. Test coverage gaps

- **TG-1 (P2) → FOLLOW-696 — AC 3 says "add the missing case-variant tests on both sides"; it was
  satisfied per-APP, not per-CONSUMER.** The new control-plane describe
  (`brand-identity.test.ts:204-236`) exercises **only `isFirstPartyTenant`**. The sibling consumer
  `isTreatedAsExternalBrand` — reached by `isUnprovisionedExternalBrand` and
  `requiresExplicitConsentHash`, i.e. the consent GET 409, the consent POST 400 and the DSR alarm —
  has **no case-variant test at all**; its three existing cases (`:106,:115,:124`) stub exact-case
  values. Textbook **Rule S**: symmetric set (the module's brand predicates), unequal verification
  tier — and the same tier inversion RETRO-222 §4c TG-1 and RETRO-224 §4c TG-4 already recorded on
  this exact file. Ingest, by contrast, got both the unit axis (`origin-gate.test.ts:172-198`) and
  the end-to-end axis (`index.test.ts:1758-1830`).
- **TG-2 (P2) → FOLLOW-696 — the "ONCE" half of AC 2 is untested on both planes, and the existing
  assertions are silently order-dependent.** No test asserts that a *second* malformed read does not
  warn, and `firstPartyTenantIdMalformedWarned` (`events.ts:55`, `brand-identity.ts:179`) has no
  reset hook. `brand-identity.test.ts:225`'s `mockCaptureMessage.mockClear()` therefore only works
  because that test happens to be the first malformed read in the file; a second such test added
  later would assert against a no-op and the suite would go red for a reason unrelated to the
  defect. Same latent trap in `index.test.ts:1795`.
- **TG-3 (P2) → FOLLOW-696 — the consent-POST route suite was not touched and now has a wholly
  uncovered new branch.**
  `apps/control-plane/src/app/api/v1/consent/platform-registration/route.test.ts` is not in the
  diff. It survives only because its fixtures happen to be well-formed UUIDs (`:65`, `:350`,
  `:420`/`:621` — verified). Consequence: the **malformed → count-probe** path this PR created for
  that route (the path LG-1 mis-reports) has zero coverage, including the FOLLOW-660 case that
  asserts *"env SET → count query never runs"* (`:478`), which is now conditional on well-formedness
  and is nowhere pinned as such.
- **TG-4 (P3, no stub) — the fixture substitutions in `dsr-routes.test.ts` preserve intent; the
  audit is recorded because the question was asked.** Verified case by case against `initiate/route.ts:229`
  (`isUnprovisionedExternalBrand` → `isTreatedAsExternalBrand`):
  - `:492` and `:526` (the two *external-brand* cases): pre-fix, env `'some-other-first-party-uuid'`
    + claims `'tenant-uuid-001'` took the env-SET branch → external, **zero DB queries**. Post-fix,
    `OTHER_FIRST_PARTY_UUID` + the same claims takes the `valid`-non-matching branch → external,
    **zero DB queries**. Identical branch, identical query count. **Intent preserved**, and the
    substitution was *necessary*: without it the env would classify `malformed`, fall through to the
    count probe, and hit `mockSelect` with only two `mockReturnValueOnce` primed by `primeSelects`
    (`:468-471`) — the tests would have started exercising an unprimed third select. The author
    caught a real trap.
  - `:507-515` (the *first-party* case) is the only one whose intent is narrowed, and only
    cosmetically: it now overrides the claims for this test alone via `mockResolvedValueOnce`, so it
    no longer shares the file's canonical `TENANT_CLAIMS.tenant_id`. Two residual risks, both
    fail-LOUD rather than silent: (i) if `initiate/route.ts` ever calls `getAuthClaims` twice, the
    second call returns the non-UUID `TENANT_CLAIMS` and the test flips to "external → alert" and
    **fails**; (ii) the assertion `mockCaptureMessage).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` remains the real
    proof and is unchanged. **No silent narrowing found.**
  - Standing consequence worth naming: `TENANT_CLAIMS.tenant_id = 'tenant-uuid-001'` is not
    UUID-shaped, so **no** test in that file can reach the `valid`-match branch without a local
    override. That is a fixture-hygiene debt, not a defect — P3, no stub.

### 5. Cascading impact

#### 5a. Current sprint tickets affected

- **Prior-follow-up closure check (algorithm step 7) — FOLLOW-678 claims to close RETRO-223 §4a LG-1
  (+ §4c TG-1 + §4d DG-1). Traced END-TO-END across five hops, not one.**
  `PRODUCER (operator → 3 unsynced stores)` → `CLASSIFIER resolveFirstPartyTenantId` (both apps,
  `origin-gate.ts:176` / `brand-identity.ts:165`) → `CONSUMERS` (all three named functions,
  `origin-gate.ts:222`, `brand-identity.ts:226`, `:290`) → `EFFECT` (403 / 400 / 409 / DSR alarm) →
  `DETECTION` (Sentry + the runbook probe). Verdict **per axis**:
  - **case + incidental-whitespace axis: REAL, verified closure.** Both directions of the compare,
    both apps, unit + end-to-end, with red-first evidence (§2).
  - **malformed axis: REAL closure, and it also fixed a latent inversion nobody had named** — pre-fix
    a garbled paste meant *deny every tenant*, on both planes.
  - **wrong-but-well-formed axis: NOT closed in code.** It is mitigated by honest docs + a manual
    §Step 0 probe. Its only automated detector on the ingest plane is the `origin_policy_unconfigured`
    Sentry ERROR at `events.ts:212`, which is **mute** (no DSN, §3), and the SDK still cannot see the
    403 — re-verified at HEAD, `packages/sdk/src/core/events.ts:105-104`: `await fetch(...)` with no
    `res.ok`/`res.status` inspection and a `catch` that only fires on a network throw.
  - **Meta-verdict on the three-retro "closure was really a relocation" pattern (the PM's explicit
    question): the pattern CONTINUES structurally but has changed character, and that is progress
    worth naming.** In FOLLOW-097→114→127→141, and again in #627→#629→FOLLOW-684, each step declared
    closure and the gap moved *unannounced*. Here the residual is named in four merged surfaces, given
    a diagnostic procedure, and explicitly excluded from the safety claim. **It is a labelled
    deferral, not a silent relocation.** The one thing that keeps it in the pattern's orbit is
    §3 CHECK B: the deferral's *detector* is unwired, so "labelled" is currently doing all the work.
- **FOLLOW-680's premise is UNCHANGED by this PR — and its evidence is now stronger.** The stub cites
  the SDK's response-discarding as the reason the ingest side fails silent; that is still true at

  remaining** 100%-traffic-loss mode on this var, so FOLLOW-680 is no longer "nice observability for

- **FOLLOW-674's blast radius widened** (RETRO-222 §4a LG-1, soft-delete-blind count probe): the

- **FOLLOW-677 needs new content, not just the missing row**: the control-plane matrix row it asks

- **FOLLOW-662 (Rule AH mechanization — verification gate for operator-executable runbook

- **QUEUE §session-63 head contains a class-closure over-claim.** It states this PR *"closes the

#### 5b. Future sprint tickets affected

- **The 3-brand external onboarding wave** now has a hard, mandatory, *manual* gate in its critical
  path (§Step 0's 2xx probe). If FOLLOW-693 does not land first, that probe is the only thing

#### 5c. Contracts changed others rely on

- **One env var, TWO consumers, and the malformed axis now resolves in OPPOSITE directions per plane
  — by design, and correctly.** Ingest malformed → guard OFF (no Postgres on a zero-I/O hot path).
  Control-plane malformed → tenant-count probe → fail CLOSED on ≥2 tenants. This *extends* RETRO-222
  §5c's unset-axis asymmetry finding onto the malformed axis; it does not contradict it. Both are
  documented in-code. Recorded so nobody later "harmonizes" them into a single wrong behavior.
- **New 403/400/409 reachability conditions** for the out-of-repo `app.estalara.com` caller are
  unchanged in kind; only the malformed-env branch moved (§4a LG-1). No SDK, decision-api, package
  export, migration or DDL change. Legal identity and tenant ids stay off the browser wire.
- **A new platform-wide observability signal** (`first_party_tenant_id_malformed`) enters the tag
  vocabulary with no registry entry (§3 CHECK B) — the second such entry in two days, after #629's
  `brand_identity` tag.

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

- **Rule AA split:** code axis **CLOSED for two of three axes**; the third is a *labelled* deferral
  to an operator procedure. Prod axis **OPEN in a new way** — unlike #627 (shipped-and-inert) and
  #629 (live), this guard is live *and* its safety net's detector is unarmed.
- **"Fail-loud" now has a third failure mode in this codebase, and it is the one nobody owns.** #627
  established refuse-rather-than-guess; #629 established refuse-where-a-wrong-record-would-be-written
  / alert-where-refusing-would-obstruct-a-right; #630 establishes degrade-to-off-and-warn. The first
  two are enforced by control flow. The third is enforced **entirely by observability** — and this
  repo has now shipped three such alarms (FOLLOW-495's `clickhouse_push_failed_post_ack`, #629's
  `brand_identity`, #630's `first_party_tenant_id_malformed`) with zero alert rules between them.
  That is the architectural fact behind §6's rule promotion.
- **Deliberate duplication over extraction is a defensible call that the repo's gate then
  mis-scores.** The implementer documented why (`brand-identity.ts:144-147`: distinct app-local
  warn-once side effects, neither app imports the other's runtime) and I agree with the reasoning.
  The cost is two `UUID_RE`s, two classifiers, two test suites at unequal tiers (§4c TG-1), and a
  Rule I false negative (§3). FOLLOW-691 asks for the decision to be made explicitly rather than by
  default.

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern P-9 (PRODUCER-ONLY ALARM) — 3rd sighting, ≥2 PRIOR numbered retros → Rule AJ PROMOTED.**
  *"A PR ships a new failure-detection signal (Sentry capture / structured log) as the ONLY thing
  that makes a silent failure visible, and ships no consumer for it — no alert rule, no registry
  entry, and sometimes no DSN in the environment it must fire in. The PR's 'fail-loud' claim then
  rests on a channel nobody is listening to."*
  **PRIOR 1 — RETRO-154 §4a LG-1 → FOLLOW-495** (verified as cited, `RETROSPECTIVES.md:24291`): after
  FOLLOW-459 moved the ClickHouse insert past the ACK, `clickhouse_push_failed_post_ack` became the
  *only* signal that the sole prod events store dropped a batch, and no alert rule keys off it; the
  follow-up is still open (re-scoped by FOLLOW-515, still not closed). Count 1.
  **PRIOR 2 — RETRO-224 §4d DG-3 → FOLLOW-688** (verified, `RETROSPECTIVES.md:35392`,
  `FOLLOW_UPS.md:19639`): #629's `brand_identity: unprovisioned_external` tag is the entire
  enforcement mechanism on the DSR path and is in no rule in `docs/ops/DSR_ALERTING.md`, while the
  runbook instructs the operator to *"confirm the alert stops"*. Count 2.
  **TRIGGER — this retro §3 CHECK B**, and it is the strongest instance of the three because the
  channel is not merely unrouted but **absent** (`SENTRY_DSN_INGEST` unset per
  `INGEST_WORKER_DEPLOY.md:123`, no `logpush`/`tail_consumers` in `wrangler.toml`), while the
  shipped docstring promises the opposite. Both banked occurrences are PRIOR retros → threshold met;
  **the promoting retro does not inflate the count** (adjudication shared with
  AA/AB/AC/AD/AE/V/Q/AG/AH/AI).
  **Checked against existing rules before minting, per RETRO-224's discipline:** Rule K.2 governs
  whether a fire-and-forget path *emits* a signal and refuses to swallow errors — this PR fully
  conforms to K.2. Rule Q governs a CI gate proving its assertion *ran*. Rule AA governs whether an
  operator has *performed* a step. **None of them requires an emitted runtime signal to have a
  consumer.** AJ is a genuinely new axis, not a fourth rule on the doc-truth axis.
  → **Rule AJ codified** (letter AJ = next in the double-letter sequence after AI).
- **Pattern P-4 (CLASS-CLOSED-ON-ONE-CONSUMER, RETRO-222 §6) — examined against its own
  pre-authorization and NOT triggered. Count stays 0 priors, HELD.** Its pre-authorization reads
  "the next independent sighting of a fail-open class declared closed while **a second consumer of
  the same switch** retains the old semantics." Here **both** consumers were fixed; what remains open
  is a different *axis* of the same switch, not a second consumer. The QUEUE over-claim (§5a) is
  therefore an instance of a *different* shape and I refuse to bend P-4's premise to catch it —
  premise-bending is precisely how RETRO-224 caught itself mis-applying RETRO-222's 409 precedent.
- **Pattern P-10 (NEW) — "NAME-COLLISION GATE BYPASS": a symbol deliberately duplicated across two
  apps satisfies a name-based wiring gate for both copies, so the unwired copy scores as wired.**
  Evidence: §3 CHECK A + `scripts/check-rule-i.sh:95-105`. Prior art examined and **rejected as
  priors**: Rule J (mirror-code sync) governs *drift* between intentional duplicates, not gate
  scoring; Rule I is the gate being bypassed, not a sighting of the bypass. **Count 1, HELD, NO
  PROMOTION** — the remedy is a ticket (FOLLOW-692), not prose, and one sighting is below the bar.
  **Pre-authorized:** promote on a 2nd numbered-retro sighting of a mechanical gate scored by
  unscoped symbol name.
- **Rule S sightings ×2 (no promotion, long codified) —** §4c TG-1 (only one of the two control-plane
  consumers got the case-variant test AC 3 asked for) and the persisting tier inversion on
  `brand-identity.test.ts` first named in RETRO-222 §4c TG-1.
- **Rule AI sighting (no promotion — promoted by RETRO-222) —** §4d DG-1, three surfaces still
  asserting the pre-#630 state, including MASTER_DESIGN.
- **Rule AH sighting, count 7 (no promotion) —** §3 CHECK B Note 2 / §4d DG-3: the wrong-value axis
  is discharged by an operator instruction rather than code. Unlike the AH instances that earned the
  rule, this one is *honestly labelled* — recorded as a conforming instance, not a violation.
- **Rule AG sighting (no count change) —** this PR appended 29 lines to
  `.claude/agents/pm-orchestrator/lessons.md`, the 5th independent PR of this wave to append to a
  shared agent lessons log. Codified RETRO-219, remedy ticketed FOLLOW-650, no collision reported.

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P1, → FOLLOW-697) — the gate is keyed on the diagnosis, not on the evidence: a
  PROVISIONED external brand that submits the canonical Estalara hash is neither refused nor
  alerted.** `route.ts:435` gates the whole block on `isUnprovisionedExternalBrand(...)`, which
  returns `false` immediately when `identity.isFallbackIdentity` is false
  (`brand-identity.ts:349`). So for a tenant that HAS `brand_config.brand_name = 'Costa Sol
  Properties'`, `route.ts:447` is never evaluated and the insert at `:537` stores
  `CANONICAL_CONSENT_TEXT_HASH` — an audit record attesting that Costa Sol's visitor agreed to
  **Estalara / Time2Show, Inc.'s** disclosure. This is the *identical* fabrication the ticket set
  out to close, and it is **more** provable for a provisioned brand, not less: we render that
  brand's text ourselves (`renderPlatformConsentText(identity)` + `computeConsentTextHash`, both
  already used by the GET at `route.ts:270,279`), so its correct hash is computable and provably ≠
  the canonical one. The refusal predicate should be `isTreatedAsExternalBrand && hash ===
  CANONICAL` (evidence), not `isUnprovisionedExternalBrand && hash === CANONICAL` (diagnosis). The
  AC-4 matrix hid this: it enumerated 4 cases along a *diagonal* of a 2×2 grid (provisioned ×
  hash-kind) and never opened the `provisioned × canonical` cell — the test at `:634` pairs
  *provisioned* with a *brand-specific* hash (`'e' + '0'.repeat(63)`), and the test at `:566` pairs
  *canonical* with *unprovisioned*. **Blast radius:** the tenants furthest along in onboarding (the
  ones an operator already seeded) are the ones with no gate.
- **LG-2 (P1, → FOLLOW-698) — the 422 can refuse and DISCARD the first-party tenant's genuine
  consent, on a fail-closed inference, with a false message and the wrong remediation.**
  `isUnprovisionedExternalBrand` delegates to `isTreatedAsExternalBrand`, whose env-unset branch
  probes the tenant count and **fails CLOSED** (`brand-identity.ts:304-313`: `catch → return true`).
  Two reaching states, both documented as expected by this repo's own runbook:
  1. `FIRST_PARTY_TENANT_ID` unset + ≥2 tenant rows — `BRAND_PROVISIONING.md:316-320` states this
     outright: *"the moment a second tenant row exists with `FIRST_PARTY_TENANT_ID` still unset,
     every tenant — **including Estalara** — is treated as external"*. Estalara's own tenant also
     has `isFallbackIdentity === true` (nobody seeds `brand_name` for the brand that IS the
     fallback), so `route.ts:435` is **true for Estalara**.
  2. the count probe throwing (transient DB fault) — reachable **today**, at 1 tenant.
  In either state, step 7b (`route.ts:378-392`) tells the caller *"Set FIRST_PARTY_TENANT_ID … **or
  send an explicit consent_text_hash**"* — and the caller that follows the second half of that
  advice for Estalara sends the **canonical** hash (correct for Estalara!) and is answered by
  `route.ts:447` with **422 `consent_text_hash_fabricated`**, a message asserting the hash is
  *"provably the wrong text"*, a remediation (`PATCH brand_config.brand_name`) that is wrong for the
  first-party tenant, and **a visitor's real consent thrown away**. Two gates 55 lines apart give
  contradictory instructions. The neighbouring FOLLOW-660 test is the witness: `:478` *"env UNSET +
  a SECOND tenant + explicit hash → 201"* passes **only because** its fixture hash is
  `'c' + '0'.repeat(63)`; substitute `CANONICAL_CONSENT_TEXT_HASH` — the live first-party value —
  and the same scenario returns 422. **This inverts the ticket's own AC-3 principle** (*"refusing
  would discard a consent the visitor already gave"*): the ticket refused to discard a consent on a
  *guess* in the general case, and then discarded one on a *fail-closed inference* in the sub-case
  it did implement. This is RETRO-222 §4a LG-2's defect shape (a fail-closed path answering a 4xx
  that asserts a false state) on its **fourth** reaching branch — and the first that destroys data
  rather than merely lying (§6).
- **LG-3 (P2, folded into FOLLOW-697 AC, cross-ref FOLLOW-379) — the refusal is EN-only by
  construction, and nothing says so.** `CANONICAL_CONSENT_TEXT_HASH` (`lib.ts:51`) is the EN §6.1
  hash; `HANDOFFS.md:2857` invites a custom hash *"ONLY if you display a translated version"*. An
  unprovisioned external brand rendering the **PL/ES translation of Estalara's** text therefore
  submits a non-canonical hash and is **not** refused — the same fabrication, one locale sideways.
  Neither the 7c comment block (`route.ts:394-418`) nor the ticket AC states this scope limit. Ties
  directly to the long-open FOLLOW-379 (per-locale hash accuracy, P2, filed by RETRO-104).
- **LG-4 (P2, → FOLLOW-703) — the attestation this wave protects is unreadable and, after a rename,
  unverifiable.** `consent_records` stores `consentTextHash` + `tosVersion` and **no brand name, no
  legal entity, no text snapshot** (`consent_records.ts:20-56`). The hash's meaning is resolvable
  only by re-rendering `renderPlatformConsentText(identity)` from **live, mutable**
  `tenants.brand_config` — which a tenant's own `agency:admin` can rewrite through the unaudited
  PATCH branch (FOLLOW-687). So a brand rename silently invalidates every prior attestation's
  reproducibility, and no reader exists to notice (§3 Note).
- **LG-5 (P1 severity, ticket already exists — RECOMMEND ELEVATING FOLLOW-687 P2 → P1) — this PR
  makes the gate self-service-bypassable by the tenant it gates.** Both the refusal (LG-1) and the
  alarm are conditioned on `isFallbackIdentity`, i.e. on the *absence* of
  `brand_config.brand_name` — a key the tenant's own `agency:admin` can set to **any string**
  through `PATCH /api/config`'s unaudited agency branch (FOLLOW-687, `api/config/route.ts:281-283`
  vs the staff-only `staff_audit_log` write at `:400-425`). One self-service PATCH with
  `brand_name: 'x'` silences the Sentry capture *and* disables the 422, after which the canonical
  Estalara hash can be posted freely (LG-1). Before #631 that PATCH only changed e-mail/consent
  *rendering*; after #631 it flips a **compliance enforcement gate**. I am not re-filing this —
  FOLLOW-687 owns the fix — but its priority no longer matches its blast radius. Surfaced for the
  PM (§5).

- **None.** Six re-verified claims, all correct as shipped: (1) gate placement is genuinely

  `fetchBrandIdentity` failure wrapper returns a real 500 with `data_source:'db', degraded:true`

#### 4c. Test coverage gaps

- **TG-1 (P2, → FOLLOW-702) — all four new cases pin `FIRST_PARTY_TENANT_ID` to a SET value
  (`route.test.ts:553`), so the only branch reachable in prod today is untested on this gate.** This

  **repeated on the sibling surface one merge later**. Consequences: the env-unset + ≥2-tenant

  as proof of AC-5 "zero extra cost" prove it **only under env-SET**. Rule S shape.
- **TG-2 (P2, → FOLLOW-702) — the `provisioned × canonical hash` cell (LG-1) has no test**, and
  neither does `first-party × canonical hash × env-unset × 2 tenants` (LG-2). The AC-4 matrix was
  taken as the test plan; nobody re-derived the full grid.
- **TG-3 (P3, → FOLLOW-702) — a pre-existing test now silently exercises the new alarm without
  asserting it.** `:478` (FOLLOW-660, env-unset + 2 tenants + explicit hash) now traverses
  `route.ts:435` with a fallback identity and fires a Sentry `error` that nothing asserts (its
  `beforeEach` was updated to `mockTenantSelectLimit.mockResolvedValue([])`, `:457`). Harmless
  today; it means the suite cannot distinguish "alarm fires correctly" from "alarm fires for the
  wrong tenant".

#### 4d. Documentation gaps

- **DG-1 (P1, → FOLLOW-699, Rule AI) — the helper's own contract docblock still enumerates two call
  sites.** `brand-identity.ts:333-337` says *"Callers decide the consequence, because it differs by
  surface (see each call site)"* and then lists exactly the GET (refuses) and the DSR (alerts but
  sends). The third caller — with a **hybrid** consequence no reader would predict from that list —
  was added without touching it. Rule AI names *"the changed file's own API docblock"*; the spirit
  covers the docblock that documents the contract being extended.
- **DG-2 (P1, → FOLLOW-699, Rule AI) — three integration/operator documents still describe the
  pre-#631 world:** `backlog/HANDOFFS.md:2795-2867` (the POST contract handed to the only caller —
  no 422, and `:2864`/`:2867`'s status policy still written for the duplicate-nonce 409);
  `docs/runbooks/BRAND_PROVISIONING.md:306-308` (two-surface enforcement table, now three) and
  `:578-586` (troubleshooting: consent GET 409 and DSR e-mail only); and
  `docs/compliance/EXTERNAL_BRAND_GOLIVE_CHECK-2026-07.md:306` (*"always compute and send its own
  `consent_text_hash`"* — following it is now the path into both the 201-with-silent-alarm and, for
  an Estalara-derived text, the 422). The PR changed 0 documentation files.
- **DG-3 (P2, Rule AH sighting — count 8) — the in-code cost claim is true only under env-SET.**
  `route.ts:414-418`: *"today's live first-party traffic pays no additional query beyond this one
  brand-identity lookup, and its response stays byte-identical."* Today's live state is
  `FIRST_PARTY_TENANT_ID` **unset** with a fallback identity (the premise RETRO-224/225 and
  FOLLOW-686 AC-4 all rest on), and in that state **neither** short-circuit applies:
  `isFallbackIdentity` is true, the env branch is not taken, so `route.ts:435` costs a
  `fetchBrandIdentity` select **plus** a second tenant-count probe on every POST — 2 extra queries,
  not 0. The sentence is correct for the go-live configuration and false for the running one; it
  needs the condition stated, exactly as FOLLOW-686 AC-4 already demands for
  `BRAND_PROVISIONING.md:269`. Folded into FOLLOW-698.
- **DG-4 (P2, positive) —** the route's own `Responses:` docblock **was** updated in the same diff
  (`route.ts:38-40`), and the 7c comment block records the AC-3 scoping decision, its rationale and
  its owner. That is the Rule AI/AH-conforming half of this PR and the reason DG-1/DG-2 are
  omissions of *reach*, not of discipline.

### 5. Cascading impact

#### 5a. Current sprint tickets affected

- **FOLLOW-685 (P1, backend-engineer, the PM's declared next pick) — scope is now short by two
  items, and one of them is the very gap this ticket deferred.** Verified against its stub text
  (`FOLLOW_UPS.md:19536-19574`): its 5 ACs cover the GET's handoff, method-scoping the 409, the
  go-live-check reconciliation, Rule AH verification and a §H.8 sentence. It is explicitly
  *"Docs/handoff only; no code."* It therefore does **NOT** cover (i) documenting the new **422**
  (→ FOLLOW-699, fold in if executed together) and, decisively, (ii) **the CEO/DPO policy ruling on
  the general case** (brand-specific, non-canonical hash from an unprovisioned external brand). The
  PR's own "NEXT" line and the QUEUE both gesture at FOLLOW-685 for that decision; its text merely
  *quotes* the deferral as context for a docs task. **Answering the brief's specific question: no,
  FOLLOW-685 does not cover it — filed as FOLLOW-701 so it cannot fall between the two tickets.**
- **FOLLOW-688 (P2, devops-engineer)** — under-scoped as of this merge: it registers an alert for
  the DSR producer only, while the same tag now has three producers and the newest one is the sole
  compensating control for an intentionally-unrefused write path (§3 HW-2) → FOLLOW-700.
- **FOLLOW-674 / FOLLOW-686 / FOLLOW-695 (the count-probe class, all P2, all open)** — this merge
  adds the **fourth** surface and changes the class's character: on the three prior surfaces a
  swallowed read error produced a *false statement*; here it produces a *refused write* (LG-2). The
  class should be re-priced accordingly and fixed once, in the helper, rather than four times at
  four call sites.
- **FOLLOW-696 (P2)** — its AC *"the malformed→count-probe branch on the consent POST route
  suite"* now has a second consumer in the same route (7c as well as 7b); whoever executes it
  should cover both.
- **FOLLOW-379 (P2, open since RETRO-104)** — becomes load-bearing: the locale axis is now the
  documented way to *avoid* the new refusal (LG-3).
- **QUEUE over-claim, surfaced not written (charter).** `backlog/QUEUE.md:8-10` (session-66 head)
  states the POST *"now gates on `isUnprovisionedExternalBrand` before every write, closing the last
  of the three consent-fabrication surfaces."* Accurate on the mechanism, over-claimed on the
  outcome: the write is gated only in the `unprovisioned × canonical` cell; `provisioned ×
  canonical` is ungated and unalerted (LG-1), the general case is un-refused **by design** with its
  compensating alarm unrouted (HW-2), and the gate is bypassable by the gated party (LG-5).
  Suggested wording: *"closes the provable-fabrication sub-case on the write surface; the general
  case and the provisioned-brand cell remain open (FOLLOW-697/701)."*

#### 5b. Future sprint tickets affected

- **FOLLOW-687 (P2 → recommend P1)** — see §4a LG-5. A ticket about *audit-logging* a config write
  is now also a ticket about *who can disable a compliance gate*.
- **FOLLOW-656 / the external-brand go-live gate** — the go-live checklist item 7
  (`EXTERNAL_BRAND_GOLIVE_CHECK`, `BRAND_PROVISIONING.md:568-586`) now has a third possible outcome
  (POST 422) an operator will not recognise; and its instruction (c) at `:306` leads into it.
- **Any second-tenant onboarding** — the first registration attempt after a second `tenants` row
  exists, with `FIRST_PARTY_TENANT_ID` still unset, now fails **both** legs for Estalara itself (GET
  409, POST 400-or-422). §Step 0 was already mandatory; it is now load-bearing for the first-party
  flow's availability.

#### 5c. Contracts changed others rely on

- The POST's public error contract gained a status class. The only caller is out-of-repo and
  undocumented for it (§3 HW-1). Fail-safe by luck via `HANDOFFS.md:2867`, not by design.
- `isUnprovisionedExternalBrand`'s *documented* contract (two consequences) no longer matches its
  three call sites (§4d DG-1) — the next consumer will copy the wrong precedent.
- The Sentry tag `brand_identity: unprovisioned_external` is now a multi-surface signal whose
  `route` tag is the only discriminator; any alert rule written later must key on both tags.

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

- **"The hash is the attestation."** Four PRs have hardened *which* hash gets written, while the
  column has zero readers and is absent from the data subject's own export (§3 Note, LG-4). The
  invariant worth stating in MASTER_DESIGN §H.8 is that a registration consent record must be
  *reproducible* — hash + the identity/text version it was computed from — not merely *correct at
  write time*.
- **"Fail-closed is the safe direction."** True while the guard's consequence is *refuse to serve*
  (GET) or *require more input* (7b). Once the same fail-closed value is allowed to *destroy a
  submitted consent* (7c), the safe direction inverts: an unknown must not be laundered into a
  refusal of a write. This is the assumption the new Rule K.2 amendment records (§6).

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern P-11 (FAIL-CLOSED-VALUE LAUNDERING) — 4th sighting, 3 PRIOR numbered retros → Rule K.2
  AMENDMENT PROMOTED.**
  *"A shared predicate that fails CLOSED returns a plain boolean, so its 'I could not determine
  this' is indistinguishable from 'I determined this is true'. Every caller then renders that value
  as a statement of FACT to a client, with a non-retryable 4xx — and once such a predicate guards a
  WRITE, the laundered unknown silently destroys user data."*
  **PRIOR 1 — RETRO-222 §4a LG-2 → FOLLOW-674** (still open): the consent POST's 400 asserts *"more
  than one tenant exists"* when the count read merely **failed**. Count 1.
  **PRIOR 2 — RETRO-224 §4a/DG → FOLLOW-686** (still open, `FOLLOW_UPS.md:19576`): the same
  swallowed read makes the consent **GET** answer 409 `brand_identity_not_provisioned` — *"a false
  statement"*, in a handler where the sibling DB failure 15 lines above correctly returns 500.
  Count 2.
  **PRIOR 3 — RETRO-225 §4a LG-1 → FOLLOW-695** (still open): the malformed-env branch gave the
  same 400 message a **third** reaching branch. Count 3.
  **TRIGGER — this retro §4a LG-2**, and it is a qualitative escalation, not a fourth repetition:
  on the three priors the laundered unknown produced a *false sentence*; here it produces a **422
  that refuses a write and discards a consent the visitor actually gave** — while the same PR's AC-3
  refused to discard a consent on a *guess*. Three PRIOR numbered retros, three separate open
  tickets, one shared helper, zero rules: that is the textbook codification case. **The promoting
  retro does not inflate the count** (adjudication shared with AA/AB/AC/AD/AE/V/Q/AG/AH/AI/AJ).
  **Checked against existing rules before minting, per RETRO-224/225 discipline:** Rule K.2's parent
  ("a configured-but-failed dependency must fail loud, never silently degrade") is the same root —
  `brand-identity.ts:308-313` *does* `console.error`, so the emission half conforms, and the defect
  is entirely in what the caller then **asserts**. Rule AJ governs whether an emitted signal has a
  consumer (a different axis — HW-2 covers that separately here). Rule S is test mechanics; Rule
  AH/AI are doc-truth. **Because the root is shared with K.2, this ships as a K.2 amendment, not a
  new letter** — the same call RETRO-135 made for the fire-and-forget sub-shape.
  → **Rule K.2 amendment (fail-CLOSED-value laundering / never-refuse-a-write) codified.**
- **Pattern P-12 (NEW) — "GATE KEYED ON THE DIAGNOSIS, NOT THE EVIDENCE": a guard conditions its
  refusal on the *explanation* for a defect (here: the brand is unprovisioned) rather than on the
  *proof* of the defect (here: a non-Estalara tenant submitted Estalara's hash), so the class stays
  open for every instance that has a different explanation.** Evidence: §4a LG-1. Prior art examined
  and **rejected as priors**: RETRO-224 §6 P-7 ("GATE-ON-THE-UNUSED-DOOR" — a gate on the surface
  nobody calls) is about the *surface*, not the *predicate*; Rule AE (enumerate every call-SHAPE a
  guarded action can take) is about syntax, not about the predicate's semantics — adjacent, and I
  considered folding P-12 into AE as an amendment, but AE's verification is an AST/grep procedure
  that cannot see this. **Count 1, HELD, NO PROMOTION** — the remedy is a ticket (FOLLOW-697), and
  one sighting is below the bar. **Pre-authorized:** promote on a 2nd numbered-retro sighting of a
  guard whose predicate is narrower than the evidence it acts on.
- **Rule AJ sighting — count 1 since codification, and it is a VIOLATION, not a conforming
  instance.** §3 HW-2. Recorded factually: Rule AJ was merged to `main` in `a2106cfa` **before** the
  worker's `70d2a70a`, and the delegation brief (`QUEUE.md:104-107`) named Rules K.2 and AA as
  applicable but not AJ — so this is at least as much a dispatch-brief gap as a worker gap. Worth
  the PM's attention: a rule codified the same day did not reach the next brief.
- **Rule AH sighting, count 8 (no promotion) —** §4d DG-3: an absolute cost/"byte-identical" claim
  that holds only in the go-live configuration, asserted about "today's live traffic". Same shape as
  the `BRAND_PROVISIONING.md:269` instance RETRO-224 filed as FOLLOW-686 AC-4 — which is still open,
  so this is the class recurring while its ticket waits.
- **Rule AI sightings ×2 (no promotion — promoted by RETRO-222) —** §4d DG-1 (helper docblock) and
  DG-2 (three integration/operator docs, incl. `HANDOFFS.md`, which Rule AI names explicitly). A
  2-file PR that changes a public error contract and touches no doc is the canonical AI shape.
- **Rule S sightings ×2 (no promotion, long codified) —** §4c TG-1 (the env-SET-only fixtures,

- **Rule AG (no sighting) —** this PR appended nothing to any agent `lessons.md`; the 5-PR streak of

### 1. Summary of change

- **PR:** #632 (merged 2026-07-27T21:04:43Z, squash commit `300cbfb`) — "fix(control-plane):
  evidence-keyed consent gate, tri-state brand scope [FOLLOW-697][FOLLOW-698]"
- **Files changed:** 5 (+695 / −66) — 2 source, 2 test, 1 agent `lessons.md`
- **Modules touched:** control-plane (consent POST route + shared `brand-identity` helper). No SDK,
  ingest, decision-api, shared, docs, config, schema or migration.
- **Key contracts changed:**
  - `brand-identity.classifyTenantBrandScope()` — **NEW export** (was module-private
    `isTreatedAsExternalBrand`, `boolean` → tri-state) — breaking: no (the boolean wrappers are
    preserved and collapse `scope !== 'first_party'`)
  - `brand-identity.TenantBrandScope` — **NEW exported type** — breaking: no
  - `brand-identity.rendersFirstPartyIdentity()` — **NEW export** — breaking: no
  - `POST /api/v1/consent/platform-registration` — the 422 `consent_text_hash_fabricated`
    **widened** (new provisioned-brand branch, `route.ts:493-524`) and **narrowed** (no longer

    `{ data_source: 'db', degraded: true }` at `route.ts:565-573` — breaking: **yes, for the
    out-of-repo caller** (a new status class on a mutating endpoint)
  - Sentry tag `brand_identity` gained **two new values**: `consent_text_hash_mismatch`
    (`route.ts:507`, `:538`) and `first_party_unidentifiable` (`route.ts:592`)

**Independent verification of the collapse claim (the PR's load-bearing non-regression argument).**
`isTreatedAsExternalBrand` is now `(await classifyTenantBrandScope(db, tenantId)).scope !==

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P0 — the headline; the whole 4-PR gate refuses a string that is not the hash of any
  text).** `CANONICAL_CONSENT_TEXT_HASH` (`lib.ts:51-52`,
  `a3f2e1d4c5b6a7f8e9d0c1b2a3f4e5d6c7b8a9f0e1d2c3b4a5f6e7d8c9b0a1f2`) is a **hand-typed
  placeholder**, not a SHA-256 digest. **Proof, three independent lines:**
  1. *Structure.* Split the constant into bytes and take the first nibble of each:
     `afedcbafedcbafedcbafedcbafedcbaf` — the 6-cycle `a,f,e,d,c,b` repeated exactly 32 times, with
     the second nibbles walking `3,2,1,4,5,6,7,8,9,0…`. A SHA-256 output with that structure has
     probability ≈ 16⁻³² of occurring.
  2. *Exhaustive recomputation.* I hashed **60 normalisations** of the two candidate source texts —
     `docs/compliance/PRIVACY_NOTICE_TEMPLATE.md` §6.1 as-committed and
     `renderPlatformConsentText()`'s template with the Estalara identity — crossing
     {raw | paragraph-unwrapped | rendered} × {markdown bold kept | stripped} × {`[agency …]`
     placeholders kept | substituted} × {as-is | +trailing LF | CRLF | trimmed | whitespace
     collapsed}, plus the whole §6.1 section and the whole file. **Zero matches.** The two values
     that DO exist: `computeConsentTextHash(renderPlatformConsentText(estalara))` =
     `821216cd2cca1814e7a42d2f749d19da1e634949ec654b652fd6cecf7d5cf6fa`; SHA-256 of the doc's §6.1
     bytes = `201c5b326baa3f96d49f3c7a9e5082fd7e2bfcb1165e59731dcaa8a552c04d18`.
  3. *History.* `git log -S` on the literal: introduced in `f810f72e` (FOLLOW-374, 2026-06-21) and
     **never changed since** — six weeks and four hardening PRs later it is byte-identical.

  **Consequences, and this is why it is P0 rather than a code-quality nit:**
  - **(i) The refusal set is un-producible.** The 422 fires iff `body.consent_text_hash ===
    CANONICAL_CONSENT_TEXT_HASH` (`route.ts:495`, `:609`). No honest caller can produce that value
    by hashing anything — the documented GET-then-echo flow returns `computeConsentTextHash(...)`
    (`route.ts:286`), i.e. `821216cd…`. And a **dishonest** caller — the actual threat model: a
    brand that copies Estalara's rendered consent text and hashes it, or hashes the published §6.1
    doc — produces `821216cd…` or `201c5b32…`, **neither of which is refused**: for a provisioned
    brand it lands in the alert-only branch (`route.ts:527-546`, write proceeds); for an
    unprovisioned one it lands in `route.ts:596-624`'s alert-and-write. **The fabrication the chain
    FOLLOW-659 → 660 → 684 → 697/698 was built to stop is the one case it does not catch.** The
    only way to trip the 422 is to copy the constant out of this repo's source (it appears nowhere
    a caller reads — not in HANDOFFS, not in the runbook, only `lib.ts:52`,
    `.gitleaks.toml:176-180` and the backlog).
  - **(ii) Every default-path consent record attests nothing.** `route.ts:703` writes
    `body.consent_text_hash ?? CANONICAL_CONSENT_TEXT_HASH`, and `HANDOFFS.md:2842` instructs the
    only caller: *"optional; omit to use the canonical EN §6.1 SHA-256 hash."* Omission is the
    documented go-live flow (FOLLOW-374). So the `consent_text_hash` column of the live
    registration flow holds a value that is not the digest of any text ever rendered, displayed or
    published — a GDPR Art. 7(1) "demonstrate that the data subject consented" record that cannot
    be reproduced from any artifact. Row count in prod is unknown from here (no DB access) and is
    an operator step in **FOLLOW-706**.
  - **(iii) A defect has been promoted to a documented invariant.** Because the constant ≠ the
    computed hash, #632 had to add `rendersFirstPartyIdentity()` (`brand-identity.ts:385`) purely to
    stop the new gate mis-accusing a tenant provisioned AS Estalara — the guard's own docblock
    (`:378-382`) and `route.ts:426-430` both state the divergence as a *fact to be worked around*.
    The placeholder is now load-bearing in two files and pinned by a test (§4c TG-2). Fixing the
    constant is therefore no longer a one-line change. → **FOLLOW-704** (P0), **FOLLOW-705**,
    **FOLLOW-706**.
- **LG-2 (P1) — the two legs of the same endpoint disagree about the hash of the same text.** GET
  returns `computeConsentTextHash(consentText)` = `821216cd…` for the Estalara identity
  (`route.ts:286`); POST's default writes `a3f2e1d4…` (`route.ts:703`). A caller that follows the
  audit-loop design (GET → echo on POST, the whole point of FOLLOW-654 leg 2) and a caller that
  follows `HANDOFFS.md:2842` (omit) produce **two different hashes for the identical rendered
  text**, both stored in the same column, indistinguishable to any future auditor. This is a
  producer/producer inconsistency **inside one route file**, and no test compares the two legs. →
  **FOLLOW-704** AC-3.
- **LG-3 (P1) — the omitted-hash path bypasses the new provisioned-brand gate entirely, and it is
  reachable in the documented go-live configuration.** Branch (a) is guarded on
  `body.consent_text_hash !== undefined` (`route.ts:493`). Trace for a tenant that is the
  first-party tenant **and** provisioned with a non-Estalara brand — precisely the CEO-ratified

  private-label re-brands of app.estalara.com): step 4b `isFirstPartyTenant` → true → pass

  pass (`route.ts:385`); step 7c branch (a) → hash undefined → **whole block skipped**; `:703`
  writes the canonical constant. **A record attesting Estalara/Time2Show text under a brand whose
  own text this route renders and can hash — no 422, no alert, no log line.** Reachable in BOTH
  configurations (env SET to that tenant, or env unset with it as the sole tenant). The route has
  `expectedHash` in scope at `:492` and does not use it as the default. → **FOLLOW-707**.
- **LG-4 (P2, severity-P1-but-already-ticketed) — the gate has a SECOND self-service escape
  hatch.** RETRO-226 §4a LG-5 found the first (a tenant's own `agency:admin` can set

- **LG-5 (P2) — the EN-only scope note is narrower than the actual gap.** `EN_ONLY_SCOPE_NOTE`

  callers should express their INTENT"* — was consciously reversed for the write path and the

  (HW-1/HW-2).

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

- **"The hash is the attestation."** Four PRs hardened *which* hash gets written; LG-1 shows the
  default value is not the digest of any text, LG-2 shows the two legs disagree, and FOLLOW-703
  shows nobody reads it. The invariant worth stating in MASTER_DESIGN §H.8 is **reproducibility**:
  a registration consent record must be re-derivable from a versioned artifact (identity + text
  version + hash), and any constant claiming to be a digest must be test-pinned to its derivation.
- **"Fail-closed is the safe direction" — resolved correctly here.** #632 is the Rule K.2 amendment's
  own worked example and it holds up under adversarial reading: the unknown is legible
  (`indeterminate`), it never refuses a write, and the two surfaces where fail-closed IS right kept
  it. This is the first merge in the 659→698 chain where the *mechanism* is right and the remaining
  defects are all about *which value* the mechanism compares against.
- **"A gate that is tested green is a gate that works."** The AC-4 grid was 4/4 green in #631 and
  missed a cell (RETRO-226); the grid is now 8+ cells green in #632 and misses the entire realistic
  threat vector, because every cell was built from the same constant the gate keys on. Tests that
  draw their fixtures from the implementation's own constants cannot falsify that constant.

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern P-12 (GATE KEYED ON THE DIAGNOSIS, NOT THE EVIDENCE) — count 2 (1 prior retro + this
  trigger). HELD, NO PROMOTION.** RETRO-226 §6 coined it at count 1 with an explicit
  pre-authorisation: *"promote on a 2nd numbered-retro sighting of a guard whose predicate is
  narrower than the evidence it acts on."* §4a LG-1 is exactly that shape one level deeper: #632
  applied the evidence principle to one side of the comparison (it now COMPUTES the provisioned
  brand's own correct hash) while leaving the other side a **proxy token** — a hardcoded constant
  standing in for "Estalara's hash" instead of `computeConsentTextHash(renderPlatformConsentText(
  estalara))`. The predicate is again narrower than the evidence, and the residue is the realistic
  attack. **Arithmetic, stated openly because two readings exist:** this analyst's charter promotes
  at *"the same pattern appears in ≥2 **prior** retros"*, and the house adjudication (RETRO-145 Rule
  Q: *"RETRO-006 + RETRO-007 are both prior … the promoting retro does not inflate the count"*;

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P1) — the new gate stops one hop short of the value the whole exercise exists to make
  reproducible.** `runCheck()` computes `canonicalHash` (`check-consent-text-sync.mjs:203`) and
  prints it, but never compares it to `CANONICAL_CONSENT_TEXT_HASH` (`lib.ts:74`). So after the PR
  whose stated purpose was *"state the normalisation precisely enough to be executable … so the two
  artifacts cannot drift again"*, the one artifact that has never been checked against anything —
  the constant, which RETRO-227 §4c TG-1 showed is only ever compared to itself — is still not under
  a machine check. The omission is deliberate and ticketed (the constant is a known-wrong
  placeholder; fixing it is FOLLOW-704), and the PR says so. The gap is about *where* the eventual
  assertion lands: FOLLOW-704 AC-2 asks only for a **unit test**, and a unit test in
  `route.test.ts` is exactly the artifact class that already failed to catch this for six weeks. The
  three-line assertion belongs in this gate, which already has both operands in scope. → **FOLLOW-714**.
- **LG-2 (P1) — the investigated finding, CONFIRMED REAL AND UNTICKETED: the consent text names a
  withdrawal channel that resolves to nothing, and the only implemented DSR intake is closed to the
  data subject.** I investigated this independently rather than accepting the worker's and the PM's
  read. Four lines of evidence:
  1. **The served text.** `lib.ts:135`: *"You can withdraw this consent at any time by contacting the
     agency's DSR contact."* No address, no URL, no in-product affordance. `lib.ts:137` names
     `compliance@estalara.com` but scopes it to *"{brandName}'s privacy documentation"* — a
     documentation contact, not the stated withdrawal channel. Identical bytes in the published
     mirror (`PRIVACY_NOTICE_TEMPLATE.md:249`, `:255`).
  2. **No other document supplies the missing address to the data subject.** `ropa.md:20` gives
     `compliance@estalara.com` as the **DPO contact** and `dpia.md:5` calls it a *"Placeholder
     contact"*; neither is an artifact an investor reads at registration.
     `PRIVACY_NOTICE_TEMPLATE.md:60` and `:86` still carry `[tenant DSR contact]` — unfilled slots in
     the tenant-embed template (legitimate there, it is a template; but it means no filled DSR
     address exists anywhere in the compliance corpus).
  3. **No code path lets the data subject start a DSR.** `POST /api/dsr/initiate` is **JWT-gated to
     tenant staff**: *"Auth: Bearer JWT (tenant-scoped agency user)"* and *"403 when the
     authenticated user is not a tenant user"* (`apps/control-plane/src/app/api/dsr/initiate/route.ts:7`,
     `:74-76`); the OTP is mailed to the subject only after **an agency admin** initiates on their
     behalf. There is no public DSR page in the control-plane (`apps/control-plane/src/app` contains
     only `sign-in`, `register`, `dashboard/*`, `admin/*`), and the consent route itself exposes only
     `GET` and `POST` — **no withdrawal endpoint** (`route.ts:186`, `:297`). The §6.3 DOM opt-out
     toggle is explicitly *not* withdrawal (`HANDOFFS.md:2869-2872`: it "does NOT affect
     buying-intent identification, lead ranking, or agent-facing chat summaries").
  4. **The documented intake procedure points at an endpoint that does not exist.** `dpia.md` §8
     step 3: *"The tenant submits a DSR request to the Estalara DSR endpoint
     (`POST /api/v1/dsr/request`)"* — `find apps -ipath "*v1/dsr*"` → **nothing**; the real route is
     `POST /api/dsr/initiate`. So even the mediated path is documented against a phantom.

  **Why this is a live gap and not a nit.** Art. 7(3) requires withdrawal to be as easy as giving
  consent: giving is one checkbox click at registration; withdrawing requires the subject to guess an
  address, reach staff, and have staff run a flow the subject cannot see. Art. 13(1)(a)–(b) requires
  contact details in the disclosure. The text has been served since 2026-06-21 (`PLATFORM_REGISTRATION_TOS_VERSION`).
  **This is a Rule N sighting** — a compliance disclosure asserting a user-facing behaviour
  ("withdraw at any time by contacting X") where no non-test symbol implements a subject-reachable X.
  It is **not** covered by FOLLOW-145 (P2, OPEN, RETRO-023), which is the *SDK consent-banner*
  withdrawal affordance for anonymous embed visitors — a different consent artifact, a different
  code surface, a different subject population; the shared root is the reason both should be
  answered in one DPO conversation. → **FOLLOW-710**.
- **LG-3 (P2, and this is the axis the PR and RETRO-227 did not analyse — step-8 multi-axis) — the
  canonical text is brand-parameterized on the identity fields and hardcoded on the
  subject-visible contact, and two docblocks contradict each other about it.** The ruling's own
  decisive argument is that the renderer *"is brand-parameterized, so it is defined for every
  deployment"*. True of `${brandName}` / `${legalEntity}` — **not** true of the contact:
  `lib.ts:137` emits `compliance@estalara.com` for **every** brand, so a white-label subject reads
  *"see the agency privacy policy and <Brand>'s privacy documentation at compliance@estalara.com"* —
  an Estalara mailbox asserted to be the **brand's** documentation contact. Three consequences:
  (i) it is a mis-attribution in a legal disclosure; (ii) it discloses the processor's identity in a
  private-label deployment, which `docs/runbooks/BRAND_PROVISIONING.md:106-107` sets up as an
  explicit verify step (*"GET … for an external tenant must NOT emit the Estalara legal identity"*);
  (iii) the renderer docblock's justification is itself false — `lib.ts:86-88` says the address is
  *"changed by ops per-brand if a brand runs its own inbox — same boundary as the DSR sending domain
  in leg 3"*, but leg 3's own docblock says the opposite: *"FIXED infrastructure — the actual sending
  domain is an ops concern and does NOT change per brand"* (`apps/control-plane/src/lib/email/resend.ts:17-22`,
  `SENDER_MAILBOX = 'noreply@contact.estalara.com'` at `:22`). Neither value is ops-changeable
  without a code edit. Latent today (one tenant, memory `project_single_tenant_rebrand_model`), live
  the day the first external brand registers. → **FOLLOW-711**.
- **LG-4 (P1) — the merge coupled two of the three holders of the TOS-version string and left the
  third, which is the only one outside this repo, ungated.** `route.ts:702` writes
  `tosVersion: body.tos_version ?? PLATFORM_REGISTRATION_TOS_VERSION` — the caller's value is
  **accepted unvalidated**, and `HANDOFFS.md:2838` hardcodes `"platform-v1.3-2026-06-21"` into the
  integration instructions. Before #633 this was inert. #633 makes it reachable: it wrote down the
  bump procedure (`lib.ts:108-113` — bump the constant, both sentinels, re-pin the hash) and the gate
  enforces sentinel↔constant (`check-consent-text-sync.mjs:194-201`), so a bump is now a routine
  operation — and **FOLLOW-710 and FOLLOW-711 both require one.** After that bump, a caller still
  pinned to the v1.3 literal writes a row claiming the subject agreed to v1.3 while the server
  serves v1.4 text and (post-FOLLOW-704) defaults the hash to the v1.4 digest: a record whose
  version field and hash field attest different texts. → **FOLLOW-712**.
- **LG-5 (P2) — the ruling created an obligation for the out-of-repo caller that no caller-facing
  document states, and I have to contradict the PR body to say so.** The PR's AC-1 rationale table
  asserts *"`GET /api/v1/consent/platform-registration` already serves this string … so the
  documented GET-then-echo flow is already keyed to it."* **There is no documented GET-then-echo
  flow.** `grep -n "GET /api/v1/consent" backlog/HANDOFFS.md` → **zero hits** (the same grep
  RETRO-224 ran when it filed FOLLOW-685; unchanged since). `HANDOFFS.md:2842` documents the
  opposite — *"omit to use the canonical EN §6.1 SHA-256 hash"* — and
  `EXTERNAL_BRAND_GOLIVE_CHECK-2026-07.md:306` instructs brands to *"always compute and send its own
  `consent_text_hash`"*, i.e. to author their own copy. The whole Art. 7(1) argument that elected the
  renderer is *"the hash attests the exact string the subject read"*; that holds only if the caller
  renders the served bytes verbatim, which nothing asks it to do and nothing checks. → **FOLLOW-713**.

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught (P0/P1/P2)

**None.** Four claims re-verified at source rather than trusted: (1) `lib.ts` is comment-only
(read every changed line); (2) `--print-text` emits the **renderer's** string, not the normalized doc
(`:330` writes `result.canonicalText`, built at `:186-190` from the renderer template) — so no third
artifact was minted, which was FOLLOW-705 AC-2's explicit prohibition; (3) the normalization is
order-correct — N6 (`replaceAll('**','')`) runs after the N5 join (`:130-141`), and since `**`
never spans a line break in the block, the order is immaterial; I checked rather than assumed;
(4) the guards fail loud, not silent — `\r`, tab, `[` and backtick each throw with the reason
(`:150-166`), and an unreadable renderer throws (`:73-93`) instead of comparing against a partial
string.

#### 4c. Test coverage gaps

- **TG-1 (P2) — two of the gate's own error branches have no self-test case.** `extractDocBlock()`
  has a `beginCount !== 1 || endCount !== 1` branch (`:129-137`) and an `endIdx < beginIdx` branch
  (`:139`); the 7 self-test cases cover a **removed BEGIN** sentinel only (`:277-281`). A duplicated
  sentinel pair (the realistic accident when a second consent version is added to the same doc) and
  an inverted pair are unexercised. Cheap: two more entries in the same array. → folded into
  **FOLLOW-714**.
- **TG-2 (P2) — nothing asserts what a NON-Estalara subject reads.** The gate substitutes only
  `ESTALARA_BRAND_NAME` / `ESTALARA_LEGAL_ENTITY` (`:99-113`), and there is no fixture for the
  white-label rendering. That absence is precisely where LG-3 lives: the one string in the template
  that is *not* parameterized is the one no test renders. → folded into **FOLLOW-711**.

#### 4d. Documentation gaps

- **DG-1 (P1, Rule AI — third consecutive merge with this shape) — `HANDOFFS.md:2842` is now false
  on three counts and was not touched.** *"`consent_text_hash` — optional; omit to use the canonical
  EN §6.1 SHA-256 hash."* (a) the default is a placeholder, not a SHA-256 of anything (FOLLOW-704);
  (b) **this merge made "§6.1" the wrong artifact to name** — §6.1 is now explicitly the *published
  rendering*, not the canonical source; (c) it recommends the omission path, which is the one that
  bypasses every gate the chain has built. Rule AI says a change that makes a contract claim false
  must update every document asserting the prior state **in the same PR**; the only document the
  only caller reads was not in the ticket's enumeration. RETRO-226 §4d DG-2 and RETRO-227 §4d DG-4
  are the two prior consecutive sightings — this is now a property of the chain, not of a worker.
  → **FOLLOW-713**.
- **DG-2 (P2, Rule AH) — `dpia.md` §8 step 3 documents the DSR intake as `POST /api/v1/dsr/request`,
  which does not exist** (`find apps -ipath "*v1/dsr*"` → nothing; the real route is
  `POST /api/dsr/initiate`). This is the document that defines the channel the consent text alludes
  to, so it is load-bearing for LG-2 rather than a stray typo. → folded into **FOLLOW-710**.
- **DG-3 (P2, Rule AH shape, freshly introduced) — `.gitleaks.toml`'s rewritten instruction
  presupposes an outcome FOLLOW-704 may not choose.** The new block says *"If the hash is re-pinned
  (FOLLOW-704) or rotated, update the `gitleaks:allow` tag on that line to the new value."*
  FOLLOW-704 AC-1 sanctions two outcomes, and under the first — `export const
  CANONICAL_CONSENT_TEXT_HASH = computeConsentTextHash(renderPlatformConsentText(ESTALARA_IDENTITY))`
  — there is **no 64-char literal**, so the tag must be *removed*, not updated, and the scan re-proved
  green without it. An instruction that one of two sanctioned futures makes unexecutable. →
  folded into **FOLLOW-714**.
- **DG-4 (POSITIVE ×3, worth naming because two of them are firsts for this chain).** (i) The
  unresolved finding was recorded **inside the artifact** (`PRIVACY_NOTICE_TEMPLATE.md:259-269`,
  immediately after the END sentinel) rather than only in the PR description — so it survives the
  PR's half-life, which is exactly how the `[agency DSR contact]` bracket had been doing its job for
  five weeks until this PR deleted it. Deleting an editorial signal and replacing it with a durable
  one is the right trade, executed. (ii) The §6.1.1 recompute instruction is the **first in this
  chain to survive independent re-execution at a different commit** (§2) — the direct answer to
  Rule AH's ninth sighting in RETRO-227. (iii) The revision-history row (`:352`) records the
  deliberate **non-**bump with its reasoning, so the next reader cannot mistake it for an oversight.

### 5. Cascading impact

#### 5a. Current sprint tickets affected

- **FOLLOW-704 (P0, unblocked, held pending Piotr) — the brief's specific question: YES, the
  merged code changes what its AC should say, in five ways.** (1) **AC-1's conditional branch is now
  dead** — *"if FOLLOW-705 rules the DOC bytes canonical … pin to whatever that ruling names and make
  the renderer produce it"* — the ruling went the other way; the target is
  `computeConsentTextHash(renderPlatformConsentText(ESTALARA_IDENTITY))` = `821216cd…`, printable via
  `--print-hash`. (2) **AC-1's "derived, not asserted" option is now the more dangerous of the two,
  and the AC does not say so.** A bare derived constant silently re-points at the new bytes the
  moment the text changes — and two of this retro's tickets *require* a text change — after which
  every row written under `platform-v1.3-2026-06-21` can no longer be validated against it. AC-1 must
  say: version-key the hash (a `tos_version → hash` map), or land FOLLOW-703's snapshot columns
  first, or state in-code that verification requires checking the repo out at the row's

  test** (LG-1) — `route.test.ts` is the artifact class that already failed at this. (4) **AC-6 is
  conditional on AC-1's choice** (DG-3): under the derived option the `gitleaks:allow` tag is removed,

#### 5c. Contracts changed others rely on

- The sentinel line format is now a de-facto contract for any future consent-text tooling: it must
  contain the pinned TOS version, appear exactly once each, and the enclosed block must contain no
  `[`, tab, CR or backtick. Nothing outside the script knows this except §6.1.1.
- The ruling is a contract on FOLLOW-704's input and on FOLLOW-685 AC-3's still-open decision
  (5a), and on any future translation work (FOLLOW-379): a translated consent text must now be
  understood as *its own* canonical byte string with its own hash, since the doc is no longer the
  reference for anything.
- **The out-of-repo caller's obligations changed and it has not been told** (LG-5/DG-1).

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

- **"Canonical = what the subject read."** The ruling is right, and it converts an assumption about
  an actor this repo cannot observe into a legal invariant. The chain now gates
  renderer⇄published-doc — but the hop that the invariant actually rests on, renderer⇄what
  app.estalara.com renders, has no producer contract, no test and no runbook step. The strongest
  available substitute is cheap and unfiled until now: instruct the caller to GET and display the
  served string verbatim, and make that the recorded flow (FOLLOW-713).
- **"Brand-parameterized, therefore defined for every deployment."** True on the axis the ticket
  examined, false on the axis it did not (LG-3). The general form worth carrying: *a surface is only
  as parameterized as its least-parameterized subject-visible string.*
- **"An unfilled `[bracket]` is an editorial defect."** #633 is right that a subject must never see
  one — but the bracket was also the repo's only working detector for "this slot was never filled".
  Reconciling artifacts by deleting the placeholder converts a visible defect into an invisible one
  unless the signal is re-homed, which this PR did (DG-4 i) and which is the practice worth
  generalizing: **when you delete a marker to satisfy a byte-equality, the marker's information must
  land somewhere the equality does not cover.**

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern P-15 (NEW) — "PARAMETERIZED ON THE IDENTITY AXIS, HARDCODED ON THE SUBJECT-VISIBLE
  AXIS": a surface declared per-brand substitutes the fields the ticket named (name, legal entity)
  and leaves the string the end user actually acts on (a contact address, a visible label) as a
  first-party literal — and the per-brand claim is then asserted in a docblock that a sibling
  module's docblock contradicts.** Count 2 = **1 prior retro + this trigger. HELD, NO PROMOTION.**
  Prior: **RETRO-221** §4a LG-3 (*"a white-label brand can override the invisible `aria` string in
  full but is stuck with Estalara's visible label"* → FOLLOW-668) and its LG-2 (white-label
  attribution fails open to "Powered by Estalara" → FOLLOW-671) — same shape, different module.
  Trigger here: §4a LG-3. **Arithmetic stated openly, consistent with the house adjudication**
  (RETRO-145 Rule Q; re-affirmed by RETRO-227 §6): promotion needs the same pattern in **≥2 prior
  retros**; one prior ≠ two. **Pre-authorised: promote unconditionally on a 2nd numbered-retro
  sighting of a per-brand surface whose subject-visible string is a first-party literal.**
- **Pattern P-13 (RETRO-227's "derived constant with no derivation test") — NOT scored as a new
  sighting, deliberately.** §4a LG-1 concerns *the same constant, in the same file, for the same
  reason*; counting a follow-up PR's failure to finish the same instance as a second sighting would
  inflate the count with one defect wearing two dates. Count stays at **1 prior retro (RETRO-227)**,
  pre-authorisation intact. *(This is the discipline RETRO-224 recorded catching itself failing and
  RETRO-227 applied to P-12/P-14; applying it against my own interest here.)*
- **Rule N — sighting, and a positive.** §4a LG-2 is a textbook Rule N violation: a compliance
  disclosure asserting a concrete user-facing behaviour ("withdraw at any time by contacting X")
  with no non-test symbol implementing a subject-reachable X — the same shape as RETRO-018/019's
  banner-string cases that codified the rule, now on the umbrella consent instead of the SDK banner.
  Positive on the same rule: this PR ships the repo's **second Rule N CI gate**, built explicitly in
  the shape of the first (`check-privacy-notice-keys.sh`) — the rule is growing enforcement, not just
  citations.
- **Rule AI — 3rd consecutive merge** (§4d DG-1: RETRO-226 DG-2 → RETRO-227 DG-4 → this). RETRO-227
  predicted exactly this: *"if the next merge repeats it, the finding is no longer 'a worker missed a
  doc' but 'this chain ships doc debt structurally'."* **The prediction fired.** Three merges, one
  document (`HANDOFFS.md`), zero edits, and the pooled debt (FOLLOW-699/709/713) is now larger than
  any single PR that created it. This is a routing problem, not a worker problem: every one of the
  three tickets scoped its doc surfaces by in-repo enumeration, and `HANDOFFS.md` is the surface the
  only *consumer* reads.
- **Rule AH — one satisfaction and two new debts.** Satisfaction: §2 (the recompute instruction
  survives re-execution at a foreign commit) — the direct answer to RETRO-227's ninth sighting.
  New debts: §4d DG-2 (a phantom endpoint in the DPIA's intake procedure) and DG-3 (a
  freshly-written instruction that one sanctioned future makes unexecutable).
- **Rule AJ — satisfied, and worth recording as the first clean instance in this chain.** The one
  failure-detection signal #633 ships (the gate) has its consumer — the CI job — in the same PR,
  plus a `--self-test` that proves the detector detects. RETRO-225 codified AJ; RETRO-226 and
  RETRO-227 each recorded a violation; this is the first merge to comply.
- **Rule AG — recorded factually, not scored, and the contradiction is now one retro older.** #633
  appends 20 lines to `.claude/agents/compliance-engineer/lessons.md`. Single agent in flight
  (QUEUE session-71/72), so no parallel-worktree conflict risk materialised. The rule-vs-practice
  contradiction RETRO-227 surfaced (RETRO-226 scored the *absence* of such an append as a negative;
  Rule AG restricts the artifact) remains unresolved — re-surfaced once for the skill-upgrade run,
  not adjudicated inside a ticket retro.
