## RETRO-229 — FOLLOW-707/712 (#634) + FOLLOW-685/699/713 (#635) — 2026-07-28

### 1. Summary of change

Two PRs, retro'd together because they are two halves of one loop: #634 changed the contract, #635
told the only consumer. That pairing is itself the headline finding (§4, DG-1).

- **PR #634** (merged 2026-07-28T07:13:52Z, squash `6958a3c1`) — "fix(control-plane): brand-correct
  omitted consent hash + validate tos_version [FOLLOW-707]". 3 files, +213/−5: `route.ts`,
  `route.test.ts`, `backlog/HANDOFFS.md`.
- **PR #635** (merged 2026-07-28T07:39:42Z, squash `48ca90c2`) — "docs(compliance): hand off the
  consent GET, method-scope the 409, record GET-then-echo [FOLLOW-685]". 5 files, +184/−19:
  `HANDOFFS.md`, `BRAND_PROVISIONING.md`, `EXTERNAL_BRAND_GOLIVE_CHECK-2026-07.md`,
  `brand-identity.ts` (**comment-only**), `MASTER_DESIGN.md`.
- **Modules touched:** control-plane (one route + one docblock) · backlog · docs/compliance ·
  docs/runbooks · MASTER_DESIGN. No SDK, ingest, decision-api, shared, schema, migration, event or
  env-var change. No new dependency.
- **Key contracts changed:**
  - **NEW refusal, breaking for the out-of-repo caller:** `422 tos_version_superseded` — a
    `tos_version` not equal to `PLATFORM_REGISTRATION_TOS_VERSION` is now refused, response carries
    `current_tos_version`. Deliberately not coerced (FOLLOW-712 AC-2: coercion erases the evidence
    the caller is stale). **Not breaking today** — the caller's hardcoded `platform-v1.3-2026-06-21`
    is exactly what the server serves. Breaking on the *next text bump*, which is DG-1.
  - **CHANGED default (silent, no status change):** omitted `consent_text_hash` on a **provisioned**
    tenant now writes `computeConsentTextHash(renderPlatformConsentText(brandIdentity))` instead of
    `CANONICAL_CONSENT_TEXT_HASH`. Fallback identities unchanged.
  - **RULING recorded (semantic, not code):** GET-then-echo is the canonical registration flow.
    Closes FOLLOW-685 AC-3, which #633 had already pre-decided in substance without saying so
    anywhere a caller reads.
  - `CANONICAL_CONSENT_TEXT_HASH`'s **value: untouched** (still the placeholder — FOLLOW-704 held).

### 2. Verification done in PR

- **Red-first, actually executed** (not asserted): `route.ts` stashed, the two new describes re-run
  → 2 FOLLOW-707 assertions + 1 FOLLOW-712 assertion fail; restored → 56/56 pass. This is the
  standard RETRO-224 §2 complained was skipped; it was not skipped here.
- `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint src/`, prettier: clean on both PRs.
- **CI:** both PRs 63 pass / 2 fail. The only red is `Rule I — wired-or-dead`, and it was
  **checked against the `main` baseline rather than waved through on reputation**: run
  `30335592648` (main @ `e5bf430f`) reports `Rule I FAILED: 192 symbol(s)`; both PRs report the
  identical 192. Zero symbols added by either diff.
- **The load-bearing claim of #635 was verified by reading the code, not by trusting the ticket:**
  does the GET-then-echo flow #635 documents actually survive the POST's own hash gate? Yes, in both
  reachable shapes — provisioned tenant → echoed hash *is* `expectedHash` (`route.ts:523`), no
  mismatch branch; first-party tenant on the fallback identity → `scope === 'first_party'` is exempt
  outright (`route.ts:657-658`). Had this not held, #635 would have documented a flow that fires a
  Sentry alert on every single registration.

### 3. Wiring Audit

- `computeConsentTextHash` / `renderPlatformConsentText`: already imported in `route.ts:66-67`; the
  new default expression is a third consumer of a live pair, not a new export. **Wired.**
- `PLATFORM_REGISTRATION_TOS_VERSION`: one producer (`lib.ts:30`), now three consumers in-route
  (default, validation, 422 body). **Wired.**
- The `422 tos_version_superseded` **code string** has exactly one producer and, in-repo, only test
  consumers — its real consumer is out of repo. That is expected here (it is why #635 exists), but
  it is precisely the shape Rule I cannot see and RETRO-226/227/228 kept re-discovering. See DG-2.
- `#635` added no symbol; `brand-identity.ts`'s diff is comment-only (verified line by line).

### 4. Discovered gaps

- **DG-1 (P1, availability — the one that matters).** FOLLOW-712 converted a *silent, graceful*
  degradation into a *hard, total* one, and nothing sequences the cutover. Before #634, bumping
  `PLATFORM_REGISTRATION_TOS_VERSION` meant the stale caller kept registering people with a wrong
  version string (bad, which is why the ticket existed). After #634, the same bump means **every
  registration on app.estalara.com returns 422 until a different repo redeploys** — a registration
  outage of unbounded length, since the two repos have no shared release train. The refusal is the
  right call compliance-wise (FOLLOW-712 AC-2 is correct: coercion destroys evidence); the *missing*
  piece is a grace mechanism — accept the immediately-previous version for a bounded window while
  alarming, or gate the bump behind a dual-accept flag. **This is not hypothetical:** FOLLOW-704
  (held, P0) re-pins the consent text, FOLLOW-714 argues that re-pin needs a `tos_version` bump, and
  FOLLOW-710/711 need the same bump. The first ticket unblocked by Piotr's ESC-044 ruling is
  therefore also the first one that trips this. → **FOLLOW-715.**
- **DG-2 (P1, structural — third consecutive occurrence, now fourth).** RETRO-226 §4d DG-2 →
  RETRO-227 §4d DG-4 → RETRO-228 §4d DG-1 all filed the same finding: a PR changes the contract of
  an endpoint whose only consumer is out of repo, and no gate notices. #635 fixes the *instances*
  (four surfaces re-synced) and fixes nothing *structural* — the next contract change will drift the
  same way, because the contract lives in English prose in `backlog/HANDOFFS.md` and nothing links
  it to `route.ts`. Four retros is well past the ≥2 threshold CONVENTIONS_PATCH.md sets for
  codifying a rule, and past the point where more prose helps. → **FOLLOW-716** (machine-checkable
  contract artifact + CI gate, modelled on the `consent-text-sync` gate #633 shipped, which is the
  proof this shape of gate works here).
- **DG-3 (P2, honesty about impact).** FOLLOW-707 fixes the omitted-hash default for **provisioned**
  tenants. Prod today has exactly one tenant, Estalara, on the **fallback** identity — so #634's
  hash fix changes the behaviour of **zero** live requests. Every consent record written today still
  carries `CANONICAL_CONSENT_TEXT_HASH`, still a placeholder that is the digest of no text
  (FOLLOW-704/706, held). The PR is correct and prospectively valuable; the compliance exposure it
  was filed under is **not** reduced by it. Worth stating plainly so the held P0 does not look
  smaller than it is. No new ticket — this is FOLLOW-706's existing scope, flagged for ESC-044.
- **DG-4 (P2, self-inflicted, caught).** #635 re-titled §2 of
  `EXTERNAL_BRAND_GOLIVE_CHECK-2026-07.md` from "GAP" and left the file's own summary verdict table
  (`:36`) still reading **GAP** — a section updated, its index not. The same drift class the PR was
  filed to close, committed inside the PR that closes it. Caught in the post-merge read-back, **by
  reading, not by any gate** (which is DG-2 restated). Corrected in PR #636.
- **DG-5 (P3).** No test asserts the FOLLOW-712 refusal happens *before* the brand-identity DB read,
  i.e. that a superseded-version POST costs zero queries. The ordering is correct in the code (step
  4a precedes 7a) but is unpinned, so a future reorder could make a rejected request pay a DB round
  trip. Cheap to pin; not worth its own ticket — folded into FOLLOW-715's AC.

### 5. Cascading impact

- **FOLLOW-704 / 706 / 714 (held, ESC-044):** unchanged in substance, but FOLLOW-704's execution now
  has a new precondition — DG-1. Whoever picks it up must land the grace mechanism first or accept a
  registration outage. Recorded on the stubs.
- **FOLLOW-710 / 711 (held, ESC-044 item 4):** same — both require the text bump.
- **FOLLOW-700 / 708 (queued, alarm registry):** unaffected. #634 deliberately chose *refuse* over
  *accept-and-alarm* partly so it would not need a registry entry, so it does not contradict either
  ticket's shape. Confirmed against both stubs.
- **FOLLOW-701 (needs CEO/DPO):** untouched by both PRs, as instructed. #635 records the current
  state without pre-deciding it.
- **FOLLOW-702 (P2, untested prod branch):** #634 partially *pre-empts* it — the new FOLLOW-707
  tests cover both `FIRST_PARTY_TENANT_ID` SET **and** UNSET-with-one-tenant, which is the exact
  "only branch reachable in prod today is untested" complaint FOLLOW-702 filed. Its scope shrinks;
  re-scope at promotion rather than executing it as written.
- **Out-of-repo (Rafał / app.estalara.com):** real action now required — adopt Step 1 of the
  FOLLOW-374 handoff. Until then the caller keeps omitting `consent_text_hash`, which still works
  and still writes the placeholder. No breakage, no urgency signal sent; someone must actually tell
  him. Flagged for Piotr in the queue head.

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **L-1 (candidate for CONVENTIONS_PATCH, 4th occurrence — promote):** when a PR changes the
  request/response contract of a route whose consumers are outside this repo, the caller-facing
  document is not "documentation", it is *the other half of the change*. Ship both in the same PR or
  the same session — never "docs follow-up next sprint". Four retros in a row have paid for this.
- **L-2:** "refuse rather than coerce" is right for evidentiary fields and is a *breaking change to
  availability* whenever the caller is in another repo. The refusal and its grace window are one
  design, not two tickets. (New — no prior occurrence; not yet promotable.)
- **L-3:** a re-titled section must be diffed against its own file's index/summary table. Cheap
  reflex, caught DG-4 only by accident this time.

### 7. Follow-ups

- **FOLLOW-715** (P1, backend-engineer) — grace window for `tos_version` bumps + pin the
  cost-ordering assertion (DG-1, DG-5). **Blocks FOLLOW-704.**
- **FOLLOW-716** (P1, backend-engineer + devops) — machine-checkable out-of-repo contract artifact +
  CI gate (DG-2, L-1).
- PR **#636** already filed and open for DG-4.

### 8. Cross-references

RETRO-224 (FOLLOW-685's origin) · RETRO-226 §4d DG-2 · RETRO-227 §4d DG-4 · RETRO-228 §4d DG-1
(the DG-2 lineage) · ESC-044 (FOLLOW-704/706/710/711 hold) · Rule AH (verify against `main` at your
own merge commit — applied in §2) · Rule AI (in-file/API docblocks) · Rule I (baseline-compared, not
waved) · FOLLOW-374 (the handoff) · FOLLOW-700/708 (alarm registry, non-colliding) · FOLLOW-702
(scope shrinks)

| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| route⇄doc tuple parity assertion              | `runCheck()` `:310-322`               | CI job `consent-contract-sync` `ci.yml:567-581` | wired (Rule AJ ✅) |
| the detector-of-the-detector (`--self-test`)  | `selfTest()` `:333-410`               | CI step `ci.yml:578`, runs before the check     | wired             |
| per-method machine block                      | `HANDOFFS.md:2880-2890`, `:3002-3014` | `DOC_SENTINELS` `:60-69`                        | wired             |
| **Rule AK item 6's repo-wide obligation**     | `CONVENTIONS_PATCH.md:2571` item 6    | **none**                                        | **HALF_WIRE_P**   |

- **HALF_WIRE_P (P1) — `CONVENTIONS_PATCH.md:2571` Rule AK item 6 declares an obligation for
  "any endpoint whose consumer is confirmed to be outside this repo" and ships exactly one gated
  endpoint, no inventory, and a verification command that cannot detect the gap it was written to
  detect.** The rule's own Verification step 4 is
  `grep -rln "out-of-repo\|no shared release train" backlog/HANDOFFS.md`, annotated *"absence of a
  hit here is a Rule AK gap"*. I ran it: it prints `backlog/HANDOFFS.md`, exit 0 — `grep -l` on a
  single named file that contains the phrase **always** hits, so "absence" is unreachable and the
  check can never fire. Worse, the phrase-match approach cannot find the strongest real candidate:
  `POST /api/crm/outcome` (FOLLOW-172, `HANDOFFS.md:2134-2175`, a PII allow-list contract consumed
  by **tenant CRM systems** — as out-of-repo as it gets, 14 status sites in
  `apps/control-plane/src/app/api/crm/outcome/route.ts`, zero machine block, zero gate) never uses
  either phrase. → **FOLLOW-721.**
- **Recorded, out of this diff, because nothing else will record it (see §5a):**
  `route.ts:396` reads `process.env.PLATFORM_REGISTRATION_TOS_VERSION_PREVIOUS`, shipped by #637
  (FOLLOW-715). It is documented in `docs/runbooks/BRAND_PROVISIONING.md` §Step 3b but is **absent
  from `apps/control-plane/.env.example`** (which does carry its sibling
  `PLATFORM_REGISTRATION_CONSENT_SECRET` at `:54`). That is a textbook CHECK-B env-var HALF_WIRE_P
  — and it has never been wiring-audited because **#637 was merged without a retrospective at
  all**. → **FOLLOW-722.**

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **DG-1 (P1, Rule AE class — the gate is blind to every emission shape except the one it grepped
  for; PROVEN, not theorised).** `extractCalls()` (`:130-154`) searches for the literal string
  `NextResponse.json(` inside two slices of the file, and `extractMethodBody()` (`:166-188`) slices
  `[export async function GET( … export async function POST( … EOF]`. Everything else is invisible
  and **passes silently** — the failure mode Rule AE (`CONVENTIONS_PATCH.md:1956`) names as "the
  guard silently reports success while providing zero enforcement". Two mutations, both run:
  1. a module-level helper `function refuseLocked(): NextResponse` returning
     `NextResponse.json({ code: 'tenant_locked' }, { status: 423 })` placed **above** the GET
     handler (i.e. outside both slices) → gate exits **0, "CONSENT CONTRACT IN SYNC — PASS"**;
  2. `return new NextResponse(JSON.stringify({ code: 'rate_limited' }), { status: 429 })` inside
     the GET handler (a `NextResponse` shape that typechecks against the declared
     `Promise<NextResponse>` return type) → gate exits **0, PASS**.
     `NextResponse.redirect(...)` is a third such shape, untested but structurally identical.
  Today the route is clean — all **22** `NextResponse.json(` call sites in the file sit inside the
  two handlers (`grep -c` → 22; first one is `:214`, GET starts `:208`), so the gate's *current*
  answer is right. It is right by luck of present-day layout, not by construction, and the gate's
  own docblock (`:21-27`) overstates it as "every `NextResponse.json(body, { status: N })` call
  site is extracted … the de-duplicated set … **is** the derived contract". The two things the gate
  *does* fail loud on — a non-literal `status:` (`:142-148`) and unbalanced parens (`:119-124`) —
  show the author was thinking about fail-closed behaviour; the shape enumeration is the axis that
  was missed. → **FOLLOW-717.**
- **DG-2 (P1 — `(status, code)` is not the unit of caller-facing meaning: the gate collapses two
  refusals with opposite remediations into one row).** `route.ts:624-636` and `:723-735` both emit
  `422` with `code: 'consent_text_hash_fabricated'`, and they are **not the same refusal**: `:633`
  (provisioned brand) tells the caller *"echo the hash `GET` returned, or send the SHA-256 of what
  you displayed"*; `:732` (unprovisioned external brand) tells it *"have ops set
  `brand_config.brand_name`"*. `HANDOFFS.md:2991` documents both as remediations "(a)" and "(b)" of
  one row. The gate de-dupes by `tupleKey()` (`:267`), so it sees **one** entry — meaning **if a
  future PR deletes either branch, the tuple set is unchanged and the gate stays green while half
  the documented remediation becomes a lie.** This is not hypothetical: it is exactly the drift
  RETRO-227 §4d DG-4 filed (#632 added the second variant), which is one of the four instances this
  gate was built to prevent. → **FOLLOW-719** (fold into FOLLOW-709 at promotion).
- **DG-3 (P2 — the contract now exists in THREE hand-maintained copies and the gate checks one
  pair).** (i) `route.ts`'s own `Responses:` docblocks — GET `:198-206`, POST `:33-67` — the copy
  RETRO-227 §4d DG-5(i) praised the workers for maintaining, and **the copy an editor actually sees
  when changing the route**; (ii) `HANDOFFS.md`'s human-facing failure tables (`:2863-2868` GET,
  `:2986-2993` POST), which carry the *semantics* ("STOP, do not register", "Proceed. No re-insert
  needed") the machine block deliberately omits; (iii) the new machine blocks. Only (iii) is gated
  against code. A PR that adds a status and updates only (iii) — the minimum CI demands — leaves (i)
  and (ii) stale **with CI green**, i.e. the drift class is not closed, it is displaced one artifact
  sideways. Concretely: #634's `422 tos_version_superseded` would now be caught; #634's
  `current_tos_version` **response-body field** would not, and neither would a rename of any field
  in the GET's 200 body (`HANDOFFS.md:2844-2855`), which is pure prose. → **FOLLOW-718** (docblocks,
  cheap and mechanical) and **FOLLOW-719** (prose table + body shape).
- **DG-4 (the prior-follow-up closure check — FOLLOW-716 does NOT close the RETRO-226→229 class
  end-to-end; it closes one of its three axes).** Rather than accept "four retros' finding is now
  fixed", I replayed each of the four lineage instances against the gate as merged:

  | Lineage instance                          | What actually drifted                                   | Caught by the new gate? |
  | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
  | RETRO-226 §4d DG-2 (FOLLOW-684, #631)     | new `422 consent_text_hash_fabricated` undocumented     | **yes** (new tuple)     |
  | RETRO-227 §4d DG-4 (FOLLOW-697/698, #632) | new retryable `500` … **and** a 2nd 422 *variant*       | **half** — the 500 yes; the 2nd variant reuses the same tuple → invisible (DG-2) |
  | RETRO-228 §4d DG-1 (FOLLOW-705, #633)     | `HANDOFFS.md:2842` prose claim about the hash went false | **no** (not a status/code) |
  | RETRO-229 §4 DG-2 (FOLLOW-707/712, #634)  | `422 tos_version_superseded` **+** `current_tos_version` body field **+** changed omitted-hash default | **partly** — tuple yes, body field and default no |

  So the honest score is **2 of 4 fully, 2 of 4 partially or not at all**. That is real progress and
  a genuine structural improvement over prose — and it is *not* the closure the ticket title
  implies. The gap has moved one hop, exactly as the `inquiry_submit_selector` chain
  (FOLLOW-097 → 114 → 127 → 141) moved: consumer → producer → detector → seed. Recording it now,
  at hop 1, is the entire point of this check. **This retro therefore does NOT declare the
  RETRO-226→229 lineage closed**; it declares the *tuple axis* closed and names the two axes still
  open (DG-2 branch semantics, DG-3 body/prose shape).

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught (P0/P1/P2)

- **CB-1 (P2, latent).** `check-consent-contract-sync.mjs:149` —
  `callText.match(/code:\s*'([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)'/)` has no leading word boundary, so a body field named
  `error_code`, `status_code` or `reason_code` would be **read as the discriminator `code`** and
  silently produce a wrong tuple. No such field exists in this route today
  (`grep -n "code:" route.ts` → 4 hits, all the real discriminator), so this is latent, not live.
  Same line: a `code` whose value is a template literal or double-quoted string yields `null`, i.e.
  "this status carries no code" — a *silent misread*, where every other unparseable input in this
  script fails loud. → folded into **FOLLOW-717**.
- **CB-2 (P3, opposite direction, fail-loud so acceptable).** The extractor is comment-blind: a
  commented-out or JSDoc-quoted `NextResponse.json(… { status: N })` *inside* either handler body
  would be counted as an emittable response and red the gate. Fail-loud, so it cannot hide drift;
  worth one line in the script's docblock rather than a ticket.

#### 4c. Test coverage gaps

- **TG-1 (P1 — the self-test fixtures are anchored on literal source strings that the very changes
  the gate polices will invalidate; PROVEN on BOTH gates in this repo).** Every self-test case
  mutates via `String.replace` on an exact anchor. When the anchor stops matching, `replace` is a
  no-op, the "mutated" source equals the original, the case's `ok === false` assertion fails, and
  CI prints **`=== SELF-TEST FAILED — the gate does not detect drift ===`** — which is *false*, and
  accuses the gate of the one thing that has not happened.
  - **Instance 1 — the new gate.** Sandbox: add `429 rate_limited` to the GET handler **and** to
    the GET machine block (i.e. do the change perfectly, both sides in one PR). Result: real check
    **PASS**, self-test **1/5 FAIL** (`GET contract block missing its own 409 row …`), CI red. The
    case-(c) anchor is a regex over the **entire fenced GET block including both fences**
    (`:376`), so *any* legitimate GET status addition breaks it. Case (b)'s anchor is the POST
    block's full line sequence (`:359`) and breaks on any insertion; case (a)'s anchor is the exact
    text of `route.ts`'s 201 return line (`:343`).
  - **Instance 2 — the precedent gate, `scripts/check-consent-text-sync.mjs`, same defect, and it
    is aimed at a HELD P0.** Sandbox: bump `platform-v1.3-2026-06-21` → `platform-v1.4-2026-08-01`
    consistently in `lib.ts` **and** `PRIVACY_NOTICE_TEMPLATE.md` (i.e. exactly what FOLLOW-704 /
    710 / 711 must do). Result: real check **PASS**, self-test **1/7 FAIL** (`TOS version bumped
    without sentinel update FAILS`), CI red. RETRO-228 §2 scored those 7 cases as the PR's entire
    verification story and did not test them against a future bump; I did, and they do not survive
    it.
  - Both instances are the same shape and both fail **closed**, so nothing unsafe ships — the cost
    is that the first correct contract change after this merge gets a red CI with a misleading
    message, on a ticket (FOLLOW-704) that is already the most contested in the backlog.
    → **FOLLOW-720.**
- **TG-2 (P3).** No vitest test covers either script; the self-test *is* the test. Consistent with
  every other gate in the repo (RETRO-228 §3 established the precedent), recorded not scored.

#### 4d. Documentation gaps

- **DD-1 (P2).** Nothing in `route.ts` tells its next editor that a machine-checked block exists.
  `route.ts` was **not touched by #638 at all**, so the two `Responses:` docblocks (`:33-67`,
  `:198-206`) — the artifact Rule AI names explicitly and the one an editor reads — say nothing
  about `HANDOFFS.md`'s blocks or the `consent-contract-sync` job. The sibling gate did better:
  #633 back-referenced itself from `lib.ts:60-61` and `lib.ts:105`. **Answering the question the
  dispatch brief asked — "is the new obligation obvious enough from the code?" — no.** It is
  discoverable only by (a) reading `HANDOFFS.md`, (b) reading Rule AK, or (c) reddening CI. (c) is
  an acceptable teacher; (a) and (b) are not reachable from the file being edited. → folded into
  **FOLLOW-718.**
- **DD-2 (P2).** Rule AK's Verification step 4 is inert — see §3 HALF_WIRE_P. → **FOLLOW-721.**
- **DD-3 (P3).** `HANDOFFS.md:2873-2878` instructs *"Do not hand-edit this block without also
  changing `route.ts` in the same PR"*, which is the right instruction but omits the one operational
  fact that will bite: **duplicating the block** (the natural move when handing the same contract to
  a second integrator in this append-only file) hard-fails the gate. Verified in sandbox: a second
  copy of the GET block appended to `HANDOFFS.md` → `found 2 / 2 … Without them the GET contract
  block boundary is a guess`, exit 1, under the banner `CONSENT CONTRACT OUT OF SYNC`, which
  misnames the cause. Fail-closed and low-probability; folded into **FOLLOW-718**'s AC as a doc
  line, not its own ticket.

#### 5c. Contracts changed others rely on

- None at runtime. The one contract this PR creates for *agents* is the format of the machine

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

- **New assumption, unstated:** "`route.ts` keeps exactly one GET and one POST, GET first, and all
  responses inline inside those two functions." The gate fails loud on the first two (`:169-174`,
  `:179-184`) and **silently** on the third (§4a DG-1). Any future extraction of a shared
  `respond()` helper — an ordinary refactor in an 865-line route — disarms the gate without a
  single red check.
- **New assumption, unstated:** `backlog/HANDOFFS.md` — an append-only file that PM/retro
  bookkeeping agents commit **directly to `main`** — is now CI-load-bearing. A bookkeeping commit
  that duplicates or reflows a sentinel reds `main` with no PR gate in front of it (§4d DD-3).

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern P-16 (NEW) — "A GATE'S OWN SELF-TEST FIXTURES ARE ANCHORED TO THE LITERALS THE GATE
  POLICES, so the first *correct* change the gate was built for reddens CI with a message accusing
  the gate of being broken."** Count = **1 (this retro).** **HELD, NO PROMOTION.** Arithmetic
  stated openly, per the house adjudication RETRO-145/Rule Q established and RETRO-227/228
  re-affirmed: promotion needs the same pattern in **≥2 PRIOR retros**, and this pattern has **zero**
  prior retro sightings — RETRO-228 §2 scored the sibling gate's 7 cases as verification and did not
  test them against a bump. I found **two instances** (§4c TG-1, both gates) inside one retro;
  per RETRO-228's own discipline, instances ≠ retros and two instances in one retro is still count
  1. **Pre-authorised: promote unconditionally on the 2nd numbered-retro sighting of a
  self-validating gate whose fixtures cannot survive the change it polices.**
- **Rule AE — sighting, with a scope caveat worth one line in the skill-upgrade run.** §4a DG-1 is
  Rule AE's exact pattern ("a fix that closes the one shape a regression happened to use is not
  proof the class is closed … the guard silently reports success while providing zero
  enforcement"), one hop further out: the *emission* shape rather than the *mutation* shape. But
  AE's title binds it to "a security invariant", and a contract-parity gate is not one — so the
  rule as written does not formally reach this gate, and no reviewer citing AE would have caught
  DG-1. Recording as **AE sighting (by analogy), count 1 toward a scope-broadening amendment**
  ("mechanical guard for ANY invariant"), not a new rule.
- **Rule AK — its own first sighting is a violation of its spirit, on the day it was minted.** Item
  6 extends the obligation repo-wide with no inventory and an inert verification command (§3). Not
  scored as a pattern; scored as FOLLOW-721, because a rule whose verification cannot fail is the
  same failure mode as a gate whose assertion cannot fail (Rule Q's subject), applied to prose.
- **Rule AJ — satisfied, second consecutive gate-shipping PR to comply.** The failure-detection
  signal (the gate) has its consumer (the CI job) in the same PR, plus a detector-of-the-detector.
- **L-1 (observation, not a pattern yet).** Mechanising a contract is the right move and it changes
  what "documented" means: after this merge, the *machine-readable* copy is the one that must be
  right, and the *human-readable* copies (docblock, prose table) became the copies most likely to
  be silently wrong — because CI now certifies "in sync" about a subset a reader will read as the
  whole. Any future gate of this shape should either derive the human copy or gate it too.

### 3. Wiring Audit

**CHECK A (dead code) — clean ✅.**

- All five new symbols are module-local (no `export` in either file) and each has ≥1 non-test caller
  inside its own file's `selfTest()`: `mustReplace` → 4 call sites in text-sync + 2 in contract-sync;
  `runCase` → 7 + 5; `insertDocContractLine` → 1 (case b); `removeDocContractLine` → 1 (case c);
  `FixtureStaleError` → constructed at 5 sites, caught at 1 (`runCase`).
- Both scripts remain wired to CI: `ci.yml:547/550` (text-sync) and `:578/581` (contract-sync), both
  hard gates, `--self-test` running **before** the real check in each. Verified in-file.
- `.claude/agents/backend-engineer/lessons.md` — an append-only agent artifact, consumed by the
  skill-upgrade run. Not a code symbol. Suppressed.

**CHECK B (half-wire) — one HALF_WIRE_P (P2).**

| New signal                                   | Producer                                    | Consumer                                                        | Verdict         |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `FixtureStaleError` throw                    | `mustReplace` + 3 sites in the two helpers  | `runCase`'s `catch` (both scripts)                               | wired           |
| `STALE` case status                          | `runCase`                                   | `selfTest()`'s reporting loop → stdout                           | wired (to text) |
| **the FAIL-vs-STALE *distinction***          | `selfTest()` `stale`/`failed` counters      | **none that preserves it**                                       | **HALF_WIRE_P** |

- **HALF_WIRE_P (P2) — the distinction this PR exists to create is destroyed by every consumer
  downstream of the log body.** `process.exit(1)` fires for `failed > 0 || stale > 0`
  (`check-consent-text-sync.mjs:436`, `check-consent-contract-sync.mjs:559`) — **identical exit code
  for "the gate is broken" and "this fixture is stale"** — and the CI step that surfaces it is named
  **"Self-test the gate (proves it detects drift)"** at `ci.yml:546` and
  `ci.yml:577`. So a STALE outcome reaches a PM in `gh pr checks` as a red step whose *name* asserts
  the exact misattribution the PR removed from the log body. The correct diagnosis exists only in
  free text a human must open the job log to read.
  This is not a hypothetical remedy: **the repo already has a convention for exactly this**, in the
  three other self-testing gates — `check-migration-journal.sh:30`, `check-fire-and-forget-sinks.sh:50`
  and `check-modal-app-singleton.sh:61` all document and use **`2 = self-test failure (the guard
  itself is broken)`** as a distinct exit code from `1`. Both `.mjs` consent gates use `1` for
  everything. The producer emits a three-valued outcome into a two-valued channel. → **FOLLOW-724.**

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P1 — `mustReplace` asserts the anchor exists ANYWHERE IN THE FILE, while the gate reads
  only a sentinel-delimited SLICE of that file. A mutation applied outside the slice is an effective
  no-op that `mustReplace` cannot see — so the defect FOLLOW-720 closed is still live in
  `check-consent-text-sync.mjs`, on the exact ticket FOLLOW-720 was written to unblock. PROVEN, in
  a sandbox, against `main` at `47ecb691`.)**

  `check-consent-text-sync.mjs` compares only the bytes between the canonical-consent-text BEGIN and
  END sentinels of `docs/compliance/PRIVACY_NOTICE_TEMPLATE.md` (currently lines 219–257) against the
  renderer. The `bracketDrift` case anchors on the literal `the agency's DSR contact` in `docSrc`.
  **That phrase occurs three times in that file: `:249` (inside the gated block) and `:263` and
  `:352` (outside it)** — `:263` is the standing "Open disclosure-quality finding" blockquote and
  `:352` is the v1.6 changelog row, both added by FOLLOW-705 itself.

  Simulated FOLLOW-710/711 **done perfectly**: rewrote the withdrawal sentence in *both*
  `lib.ts:150` and `PRIVACY_NOTICE_TEMPLATE.md:249`, and bumped `PLATFORM_REGISTRATION_TOS_VERSION`
  consistently across `lib.ts` and both doc sentinels. Result:

  ```
  ===== REAL CHECK =====   PASS  §6.1 normalizes byte-for-byte to the served consent text.
                           === CONSENT TEXT IN SYNC — PASS ===
  ===== SELF-TEST =====    FAIL  [self-test] reintroduced bracket placeholder FAILS
                           === SELF-TEST FAILED (1/7) — the gate does not detect drift ===   EXIT=1
  ```

  **`FAIL`, not `STALE`.** `mustReplace` found the anchor at `:263`, mutated *that* copy — which lies
  outside the compared region — so `runCheck` correctly still returned `ok === true`, the case's
  `ok === false` assertion failed, and CI printed the verbatim misleading banner. FOLLOW-720's own
  §4c TG-1 symptom, reproduced after FOLLOW-720 merged.

  **The gap moved one hop and the ticket declared closure at hop 0.** `insertDocContractLine` /
  `removeDocContractLine` — the *other* half of this same PR — get this right by construction: they
  locate the BEGIN/END sentinel pair and operate strictly between the indices
  (`check-consent-contract-sync.mjs:376-395`, `:406-427`). The author found the correct insight,
  applied it to one script's doc cases, and left the other script's doc cases on the file-wide
  `mustReplace`. Both scripts read a sentinel-delimited slice; the insight was equally load-bearing
  in both.

  **Aggravating, and the reason this is P1 rather than P2:** `PRIVACY_NOTICE_TEMPLATE.md` carries an
  **append-only changelog table that quotes consent-text phrases verbatim** when they change (`:352`
  quotes both of FOLLOW-705's substitutions inside the row text). So performing the very change these
  anchors police *manufactures* the out-of-block duplicate that defeats `mustReplace` for the next
  anchor. The trap regenerates itself. Today `within 30 days` occurs exactly once in the doc and once
  in `lib.ts` (`grep -c` → `1`, `1`), so `wordDrift`/`rendererDrift` are safe **only until the next
  changelog row quotes them**. → **FOLLOW-723.**

- **LG-2 (P2 — the closure claim, scored per ticket rather than per PR).** FOLLOW-720's AC was "make
  BOTH gates' self-test fixtures survive the change they police". Traced end-to-end per axis:

  | Axis (the actual change a held ticket will make)                    | Gate         | Before #639 | After #639                    |
  | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------- | ----------------------------- |
  | Add a status/code to GET or POST, both sides (FOLLOW-707/717/719)   | contract     | 1/5 FAIL    | **5/5 PASS** ✅ (reproduced)   |
  | Bump `PLATFORM_REGISTRATION_TOS_VERSION`, all 3 sites (FOLLOW-710/711) | text       | 1/7 FAIL    | **immune** ✅ (dynamic derive) |
  | Change the consent text's withdrawal sentence (FOLLOW-710/711)      | text         | 1/7 FAIL    | **1/7 FAIL, same banner** ❌   |
  | Reword any gated phrase that a changelog row also quotes            | text         | FAIL        | **FAIL** ❌                    |
  | Reword a gated phrase with no out-of-block copy (`within 30 days`)  | text         | FAIL        | **STALE, correct msg** ✅      |

  **3 of 5 axes closed, 2 open** — and the two open ones are precisely FOLLOW-710/711's, which is
  the ticket pair the fix was dispatched to unblock. Correcting the PM's framing on the evidence
  rather than the ticket text: **FOLLOW-704 was never exposed on this axis at all.** Its AC set
  (FOLLOW_UPS.md `## FOLLOW-704`) changes `CANONICAL_CONSENT_TEXT_HASH`, its docblock, a gitleaks
  tag and tests — **no consent-text byte and no `tos_version` literal** — so none of the seven
  text-sync anchors is touched by it. The ticket that trips them is FOLLOW-710+711 (bundled), whose
  own stub states "the fix changes DISCLOSED MEANING, so it costs a `PLATFORM_REGISTRATION_TOS_VERSION`
  bump, new BEGIN/END sentinel strings…". So: **"unblocks FOLLOW-704/710/711" is right for 704
  (vacuously), right for the version axis of 710/711, and wrong for the text axis of 710/711.**
- **LG-3 (P3 — the misleading banner still prints in the mixed case).** When a run produces both a
  genuine FAIL and a STALE, **both** banners print and `the gate does not detect drift` prints
  **first** (`check-consent-text-sync.mjs:434-451`). Observed in a sandbox one-sided rewording run:
  `FAIL … unmodified repo state PASSES` (genuine) + `STALE … doc retention-period drift` — the reader's
  first line is still the accusation. Cheap ordering fix; folded into FOLLOW-724.

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught (P0/P1/P2)

- **CB-1 (P3, latent, benign today).** `insertDocContractLine:378-379` and
  `removeDocContractLine:408-409` locate the sentinels with `lines.findIndex(...)` and **do not
  replicate the uniqueness count** that `extractDocContract:221-222` enforces
  (`beginCount`/`endCount`). A duplicated sentinel pair would make the helpers splice into the first
  block silently. Benign in practice because `runCheck` re-parses the mutated source and
  `extractDocContract` fails loud on the duplicate — but the helpers' own contract is weaker than the
  parser they feed. Record, do not ticket separately; one line in FOLLOW-723's AC.
- **CB-2 (P3).** `removeDocContractLine(sources.docSrc, 'GET', '409 brand_identity_not_provisioned')`
  is still a literal row anchor. That is inherent to what case (c) tests and it now fails **loud**
  (STALE), so it is correct — but if the GET 409 is ever legitimately removed, the case has no
  documented successor row to re-anchor on, and the STALE message says "update the anchor" without
  saying which property the replacement must have (a coded status in GET whose bare status also
  appears uncoded in POST). One comment line; folded into FOLLOW-723.

#### 4c. Test coverage gaps

- **TG-1 (P2 — the fail-loud machinery this PR shipped has never been observed failing; Rule Q class
  applied to the PR's own contribution).** `FixtureStaleError`'s construction, `runCase`'s `catch`
  branch, the `STALE` reporting arm, the `SELF-TEST FIXTURE STALE (n/N)` banner, and 3 of the 5
  throw sites (the two sentinel-pair guards and the missing-fence guard in the structural helpers)
  are executed by **no self-test case and no CI run**. Every run to date prints `5/5` and `7/7`
  PASS; a typo in the STALE arm would ship undetected, and the whole PR would be inert. Rule Q's
  subject exactly ("a check that cannot fail is not a check"), one level down: *a diagnosis that is
  never rendered is not a diagnosis.* **I proved it works** — sandbox rewording of the unique
  `within 30 days` anchor produced a correctly-worded `STALE`, `EXIT=1` — which is the verification
  the PR could and should have carried, since a self-test file is the one place where a
  deliberately-stale fixture is trivially constructible (mutate a copy of the source in memory, not
  on disk). → **FOLLOW-724.**
- **TG-2 (P3 — un-gated byte-identical duplication across two same-runtime files, reaching neither
  Rule J nor Rule K.1).** `FixtureStaleError` (455 chars), `mustReplace` (165) and `runCase` (277)
  are **byte-identical** in both scripts (verified by AST-slice comparison, not by eye). The PR
  justifies the duplication explicitly and the justification is reasonable on its own terms — but it
  ships with **no parity mechanism**, and this repo has one: `scripts/check-mirror-files.sh` +
  `scripts/mirror-files.json` (Rule J). Rule J's scope is `apps/decision-api/src/lib/` *cross-runtime*
  mirrors, so it does not reach two same-runtime `scripts/*.mjs`; Rule K.1's scope is a "metric or
  business value", so a test-harness helper does not reach it either. Net: a declared-identical pair
  with no gate — the precise pattern Rule J was minted for, in a location neither rule covers. The
  divergence is not theoretical: **FOLLOW-723 will touch the text-sync copy only.** → **FOLLOW-725.**

#### 4d. Documentation gaps

- **DD-1 (P3).** Both CI step names still read "Self-test the gate (proves it detects drift…)"
  (`ci.yml:546`, `:577`) — see §3. Folded into FOLLOW-724.
- **DD-2 (P3).** Neither script's header documents its exit-code vocabulary, unlike all three shell
  gates (`check-migration-journal.sh:28-30` etc.). Folded into FOLLOW-724.

### 5. Cascading impact

**Repo-wide P-16 scan (the PM's step-1 question, answered).** Grepped every gate in `scripts/` for a
self-test (`grep -rln "self-test\|selfTest\|SELF-TEST" scripts/` → 5 hits). The three besides the
consent pair — `check-fire-and-forget-sinks.sh:57-92`, `check-modal-app-singleton.sh:68-111`,
`check-migration-journal.sh:50-160` — **all build fully synthetic fixtures in a `mktemp -d` and
point the gate at the temp tree via an env var / fixture mode. None of them mutates a live repo
source.** They are therefore **structurally immune to P-16**, and no `sed -i` / literal-anchor
mutation exists in any of them (`grep -n "sed -i\|\.replace(" ` → 1 hit, an unrelated `.sql` suffix
strip). Same for the six tests that read real sources via `readFileSync`: only
`chat-intent-cache.test.ts:112-113` uses `.replace`, and its anchors are its own `{tenant_id}` /
`{session_id}` placeholders, not policed literals.

**So P-16 stays scoped to the two consent gates, and the root cause is now named precisely: they are
the only gates in this repo whose self-test fixtures are produced by MUTATING THE LIVE SOURCE
instead of SYNTHESIZING one.** That choice — not the anchor style — is what couples the fixture to
the thing under change; `mustReplace` treats a symptom of it. The synthetic-fixture pattern the
other three gates already use is the structural answer, and it is a *repo precedent*, not a
proposal. Recorded in FOLLOW-723's AC as the alternative to weigh.

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected

- **New assumption, unstated and now falsified:** "a self-test anchor that is present in the source
  file is present in the checked region." True for `check-consent-contract-sync.mjs` (whose two doc
  cases are structurally region-scoped) and **false for `check-consent-text-sync.mjs`** (§4a LG-1).
- **Standing assumption, re-confirmed and now more load-bearing:** these two gates' fixtures are
  coupled to live repo content, so *doc-hygiene edits to files that are not code* — a changelog row,

  for `HANDOFFS.md` (a file bookkeeping agents commit straight to `main`);
  `PRIVACY_NOTICE_TEMPLATE.md` is now in the same category, via `:263` and `:352`.

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern P-16 ("A GATE'S OWN SELF-TEST FIXTURES ARE ANCHORED TO THE LITERALS THE GATE POLICES") —
  count 2 (RETRO-230 prior + this trigger) = **1 PRIOR retro**. HELD, NO PROMOTION.**
  Arithmetic re-verified against the PM's instruction and against house precedent, and it does not
  clear the bar: the charter requires the pattern in **≥2 PRIOR retros**, and RETRO-230 is the only
  prior. Consistent with how RETRO-227 scored P-12 ("count 2 … HELD"), RETRO-227 scored P-14, and
  RETRO-229 scored P-15 ("count 2 … HELD, pre-authorised … on the NEXT sighting" = the 3rd).
  **Reconciliation, stated against my own interest, because it points the other way:** RETRO-230 §6
  wrote *"Pre-authorised: promote unconditionally on the 2nd numbered-retro sighting"* — which is
  **this retro**, and which is **one sighting earlier than the charter bar and one earlier than the
  P-15 wording RETRO-229 set two entries before it.** I am **declining that pre-authorisation** and
  following the charter. Recording the discrepancy rather than quietly resolving it: RETRO-230's
  pre-authorisation clause is drafted a hop early and, if any future retro honours it verbatim, it
  will mint a rule at 1 prior. Correct form is P-15's ("promotion on the next sighting", from
  count 2). **P-16 is now pre-authorised — in the P-15 form — for unconditional promotion on the
  3rd numbered-retro sighting.** Note the sighting here is a *strong* one: the pattern survived its
  own dedicated remediation PR.
- **Pattern P-17 (NEW) — "REGION-BLIND ASSERTION": a check asserts that a literal is PRESENT (or
  ABSENT) across a whole file/repo, while the thing it guards reads only a delimited region of that
  file. The assertion is satisfied — or defeated — by matter outside the region, so it reports on
  something other than what it guards, and it fails in the direction that looks like a real
  finding.** Count = **2 (1 prior retro + this trigger)**: RETRO-230 §3 / §4d DD-2 (Rule AK's
  `grep -rln … backlog/HANDOFFS.md`, whose "absence" predicate is unreachable because the phrase
  lives elsewhere in the same file) + this retro §4a LG-1 (`mustReplace`'s file-wide `.includes()`
  vs the gate's sentinel-delimited slice, **proven**). **HELD, NO PROMOTION** — same arithmetic as
  P-16. Distinct from Rule Q (which is about a check that *cannot* fail; P-17's checks can and do
  fail, just about the wrong bytes) and from Rule AE (which is about enumerating *shapes*, not
  *regions*). **Pre-authorised for promotion on the next sighting (3rd, = 2 priors).**
- **Rule J / Rule K.1 — scope-boundary sighting, count 1, no amendment proposed yet.** §4c TG-2:
  a byte-identical helper triplet duplicated across two same-runtime `scripts/*.mjs` files falls
  outside J (cross-runtime `apps/decision-api/src/lib/`) and outside K.1 ("metric or business
  value"). K.1 has been amended once before for a shape its framing missed (the 2026-06-03 TS-map ↔
  inline-SQL amendment, RETRO-030). This is a second such shape — **gate/tooling code**. Recording as
  count 1 toward a future K.1 scope-broadening amendment, not as a new rule.
- **Rule AJ — satisfied in letter, failed in spirit, and worth one line in the skill-upgrade run.**
  The PR's new failure-detection signal (`STALE`) does have a consumer (the log). But AJ's intent —
  a signal that reaches someone who can act — is defeated when the signal is flattened into an exit
  code shared with its opposite and a step name that asserts the opposite (§3). Not scored as a new
  pattern; scored as FOLLOW-724.
- **L-1 (observation).** Two consecutive PRs in this chain (#638, #639) were verified by their author
  against *the scenario named in the ticket*, and in both cases a **different scenario from the same
  class** was still broken (RETRO-230 §4a DG-1 for #638; §4a LG-1 here for #639). The ticket text is
  becoming the de-facto test plan. The cheap counter-measure, and the one that found both: before
  accepting a fix, run it against **the next ticket in the queue that will exercise it**, not against
  the repro the ticket quotes.

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P1 — THE SAME DEFECT, ON THE `libSrc` AXIS, SURVIVES ITS OWN REMEDIATION PR — AND IS NOW
  COVERED BY AN INLINE COMMENT THAT DECLARES IT SAFE ON A FALSE PREMISE. PROVEN in a sandbox against
  `main` at `1078cfc0`, repo untouched.)**

  `check-consent-text-sync.mjs:296-303` states the justification for leaving the 3 `libSrc` cases on
  the file-wide `mustReplace`:

  > `libSrc`-targeting cases (`renderer-side text drift`, `TOS version bumped`, `unreadable
  > renderer`) still use `mustReplace` above unchanged: `extractRendererTemplate`'s own extraction is
  > itself a whole-`libSrc`-first-match regex (**no narrower region exists to scope to**) …

  **The parenthesis is false.** `extractRendererTemplate` (`:66-95`) *starts* with a whole-file
  first-match regex, but what it **returns and what `runCheck` compares** is `tpl[1]` — the template
  literal inside `renderPlatformConsentText()`, `lib.ts:134-…`. That is a strictly narrower region,
  it is already computed by the gate itself, and it is trivially scopeable — exactly the relationship
  `extractDocBlock` has to the doc, which this same PR *did* scope.

  Audited per site, which is what AC-3 asked for and what the blanket comment did not do:

  | `libSrc` case                | Anchor                                     | Region `runCheck` reads              | Aligned? |
  | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ | -------- |
  | `unreadable renderer`        | `export function renderPlatformConsentText` | the `fn` regex's own first match     | ✅ yes — the anchor *is* the thing the whole-file regex locates |
  | `TOS version bumped`         | the `PLATFORM_REGISTRATION_TOS_VERSION = '…'` assignment, derived dynamically with the gate's own regex | `libSrc.match(/PLATFORM_…/)`, whole-file first match | ✅ yes — same regex, same first match |
  | **`renderer-side text drift`** | **`within 30 days`** — a phrase *inside* the returned template | **`tpl[1]`, the template literal only** | ❌ **NO** |

  **So the collective verdict is right for 2 of 3 sites and wrong for the 1 site it matters at.**

  **Proof.** Sandbox, merged script, one realistic edit: insert a docblock line above the renderer
  quoting the disclosed retention window (`* RETENTION: the erasure window disclosed in the template
  below is "within 30 days";`) at `lib.ts:127`, i.e. **10 lines above** the template literal it
  quotes. Nothing else changed. Result:

  ```
  ===== REAL CHECK =====   === CONSENT TEXT IN SYNC — PASS ===
  ===== SELF-TEST =====    FAIL  [self-test] renderer-side text drift FAILS
                           === SELF-TEST FAILED (1/7) — the gate does not detect drift ===   EXIT=1
  ```

  **`FAIL`, not `STALE`. The verbatim banner FOLLOW-720 and FOLLOW-723 both exist to delete, in the
  file FOLLOW-723 was dispatched to fix, after FOLLOW-723 merged.**

  **Aggravating, and the reason this is P1 and not P2 — the self-regenerating mechanic RETRO-231
  found in the doc has an exact sibling in `lib.ts`, and nobody has named it.** RETRO-231 scored the
  doc case P1 because `PRIVACY_NOTICE_TEMPLATE.md` carries an append-only changelog that quotes
  policed phrases verbatim. `lib.ts` does the same thing in its own docblock: `:113-115` quotes
  `[agency DSR contact]` and `[agency privacy policy]` — the *pre*-FOLLOW-705 forms of two currently
  policed phrases — inside a narrative paragraph, and `:121-126` **instructs the next editor to
  update that very docblock when the text changes** ("When the text changes: edit both, bump … and
  re-pin … — all in the same PR"). So the file's own instructions steer the next text-change author
  into writing prose *above the template* about the phrases *inside* it. Stated at the honesty level
  the evidence supports: the *mechanism* is proven live (above); the *specific* trip on
  FOLLOW-710/711 is **not** proven, because `within 30 days` is still unique in `lib.ts` today
  (`grep -c` → 1) and 710/711 rewrites the DSR sentence, not the retention window.
  **What tips it to P1 is not probability — it is that a wrong "audited, safe" verdict now sits in
  the file and will stop the next auditor.** An unexamined call site invites examination; one
  labelled *audited and safe* does not. → **FOLLOW-726.**

- **LG-2 (P1 — contract-sync case (a): the audit verdict names a trigger NARROWER than the real one,
  and the real one is live TODAY under an ordinary refactor. PROVEN. This is the PM's direct
  question, answered with evidence: YES, it warrants its own ticket.)**

  `check-consent-contract-sync.mjs:486-496` records the verdict "SAFE TODAY, NOT STRUCTURALLY" and
  names the trigger:

  > If a future change ever produces **a second literal match of this anchor across GET/POST**, this
  > case must be re-scoped to `extractMethodBody(routeSrc, 'POST')` …

  The count is right (`grep -c` → 1 today) and the remedy is right. **The trigger condition is
  wrong — too narrow in the one direction that matters.** `mustReplace` mutates the **first match in
  the whole file**, and POST's real copy is at `route.ts:853`. So the case is defeated by a second
  literal match **anywhere above line 853** — which includes the entire GET handler (`:208-318`) and,
  critically, **all module-level code**, the region RETRO-230 §4a DG-1 already proved `extractCalls`
  is structurally blind to. "Across GET/POST" does not name that region at all.

  **Proof.** Sandbox, merged script, one ordinary refactor — extract the 201 builder into a
  module-level helper placed above `GET` (5 lines, no behaviour change, the exact shape RETRO-230
  §4a DG-1 mutation 1 used):

  ```
  ===== REAL CHECK =====   === CONSENT CONTRACT IN SYNC — PASS ===
  ===== SELF-TEST =====    FAIL  [self-test] route-side undocumented addition (POST 201 + new code) FAILS
                           === SELF-TEST FAILED (1/5) — the gate does not detect drift ===   EXIT=1
  ```

  **Two independent defects compound here and neither is visible from the other's ticket:** the real
  check silently PASSES (RETRO-230 DG-1, owned by FOLLOW-717) *and* the self-test misleadingly FAILS
  (this). A reader sees a red self-test and a green contract check and will reasonably conclude the
  gate broke, when in fact the gate went blind and the fixture went stale, simultaneously, from one
  five-line refactor.

  **And the FOLLOW-717 interaction is the opposite of what the comment predicts.** The comment says
  *"if 717 **narrows** the extraction region, case (a)'s anchor must be re-scoped"*. FOLLOW-717's
  stub does the reverse — it **broadens** `extractCalls` to see helper-extracted and
  `new NextResponse(...)` emissions. After 717 lands, the module-level copy becomes visible to the
  real check, so `runCheck` fails, so case (a) goes **green again — while silently testing
  module-level attribution instead of the POST-body addition its name asserts.** FOLLOW-717 therefore
  *masks* this rather than triggering it, which is the worst of the three outcomes. → **FOLLOW-727.**

- **LG-3 (P3, latent — the displacement's NEXT hop, named in advance rather than after it bites).**
  `mustReplaceInDocBlock`'s docblock claims it is scoped to "the bytes strictly between the BEGIN and
  END sentinel lines … **which is exactly what `extractDocBlock`/`runCheck` compare**". One hop
  loose: `runCheck:229` compares `normalizeDocBlock(block)`, not `block`. Normalization (`:148-178`,
  §6.1.1 N3–N6) discards leading/trailing whitespace, intra-paragraph line breaks, blank-line runs
  and every `**`. A fixture mutation landing *inside the block* but *only in normalized-away bytes*
  is an effective no-op the helper cannot see — the identical FAIL-not-STALE shape, one region
  deeper. Symmetrically, `mustReplaceBeginSentinelLine` scopes to the whole BEGIN line while
  `runCheck:213` reads only `beginLine.includes(tosVersion)` from it. **Latent, not live:** all three
  current doc anchors are prose inside a paragraph, and the sentinel case removes the sentinel
  outright. Recording it now is the point — this chain has displaced one hop per PR for four PRs.
  → folded into **FOLLOW-728.**

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught (P0/P1/P2)

- **CB-1 (P3, benign, worth one line).** `locateDocSentinelLines:325-329` throws `FixtureStaleError`
  when the sentinel pair is not unique, while `extractDocBlock:129-138` throws a plain `Error` for
  the identical condition (which `runCheck` catches into `errors`, i.e. a legitimate check failure).
  The split is **correct** — a fixture helper's inability to locate its region is fixture staleness,
  not drift — but it means the same repo state is reported as `STALE` by one code path and as a real
  `FAIL` by the other in the same run, with no comment saying that divergence is deliberate. One
  comment line; folded into **FOLLOW-728**.
- **CB-2 (P3, cosmetic).** `mustReplaceInDocBlock:352-354` — if the sentinel block were empty
  (`endIdx === beginIdx + 1`), `''.replace(...).split('\n')` yields `['']` and the reconstruction
  inserts a blank line. Unreachable in practice (the `!block.includes(anchor)` guard throws first on
  an empty block), so recorded, not ticketed.
- **No P0/P1 code bug.** The reconstruction arithmetic in `mustReplaceInDocBlock`
  (`lines.slice(0, beginIdx+1) + mutated + lines.slice(endIdx)`) is off-by-one-correct against
  `extractDocBlock`'s `lines.slice(beginIdx+1, endIdx)`; verified by re-derivation and by the 7/7
  green run.

  the checked region" is now **true** for text-sync's `docSrc` cases and contract-sync's `docSrc`
  cases, and **false** for text-sync's `renderer-side text drift` (§4a LG-1) and contract-sync's case
  (a) (§4a LG-2).
- **New assumption, unstated, introduced by this PR:** "the region a fixture must be scoped to is the
  region the gate *extracts*." The truthful statement is "the region the gate *compares*" — which for
  the doc is `normalizeDocBlock(block)`, a subset of the extracted block (§4a LG-3), and for the
  renderer is `tpl[1]`, a subset of `libSrc` (§4a LG-1). The PR's own comment conflates extraction
  with comparison, and that conflation is the single root of both LG-1 and LG-3.
- **Standing assumption, re-confirmed and now proven on a second file:** these gates' fixtures are
  coupled to live repo content, so *narrative prose in a non-code file* changes CI's verdict on the
  gate's own health. RETRO-230 said it for `HANDOFFS.md`; RETRO-231 for
  `PRIVACY_NOTICE_TEMPLATE.md`; **this retro adds `lib.ts`'s own docblock** (§4a LG-1) — i.e. the
  category now includes a *source file's comments*, which no reviewer treats as CI-load-bearing.

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern P-17 ("REGION-BLIND ASSERTION") — count 3, = 2 PRIOR RETROS. THRESHOLD MET. → PROMOTED
  as Rule AL.** Arithmetic, stated openly and re-derived rather than inherited: priors are
  **RETRO-230 §3 / §4d DD-2** (Rule AK's Verification step 4, `grep -rln … backlog/HANDOFFS.md`,
  whose "absence" predicate is unreachable because the phrase lives elsewhere in the same file) and
  **RETRO-231 §4a LG-1** (`mustReplace`'s file-wide `.includes()` vs the gate's sentinel-delimited
  slice, proven). That is **two prior numbered retros**, which is the charter bar. This retro is the
  third sighting and contributes **two further proven instances** (§4a LG-1 `libSrc`, §4a LG-2
  `route.ts`) plus one named in advance (§4a LG-3, normalization). RETRO-231 pre-authorised promotion
  "on the next sighting (3rd, = 2 priors)" **in the corrected P-15 form**, and I am honouring it
  **after re-deriving the count independently**, not because it was pre-authorised — RETRO-231's own
  lesson is that a predecessor's pre-authorisation is not an authorisation. Checked before minting:
  distinct from **Rule Q** (a check that *cannot* fail; P-17's checks fail readily, just about the
  wrong bytes), from **Rule AE** (enumerating *shapes*, not *regions*), and from **Rule AD**
  (structural shapes of a literal). No existing rule states the region invariant.
- **Pattern P-16 ("A GATE'S OWN SELF-TEST FIXTURES ARE ANCHORED TO THE LITERALS THE GATE POLICES") —
  count 3, = 2 PRIOR RETROS. THRESHOLD MET. → PROMOTED as Rule AM.** Priors: **RETRO-230 §4c TG-1**
  (both gates, proven) and **RETRO-231 §4a LG-1 / §5** (survived remediation once; §5's repo-wide
  scan established that the three shell gates are structurally immune because they synthesize
  fixtures). This retro is the third sighting and it is the strongest one available: **the pattern
  has now survived TWO consecutive dedicated remediation PRs** (#639, #640), and §2's own proof shows
  that even the *fully successful* fix leaves the next legitimate consent-text change reddening CI —
  correctly worded, but red. The root coupling RETRO-231 §5 named (fixtures produced by **mutating
  the live source** rather than **synthesizing one**) was explicitly offered to FOLLOW-723 as the
  structural alternative in AC-1 and was **not taken**; the PR chose region-scoping and said so. That
  is a defensible engineering call for a 3h ticket and it is *precisely* why the invariant belongs in
  a rule rather than in a ticket: the next gate author will make the same call by default.
  Checked before minting: **Rule Q** requires a gate to prove its assertion ran — it says nothing
  about where the *fixture* comes from; **Rule AJ** is about a signal's consumer; **Rule AK item 5**
  requires a red-first proof at merge time, which is orthogonal to whether the fixture survives the
  next legitimate change. AM is the fixture-provenance rule none of them states.
- **Rule J / Rule K.1 scope-boundary — sighting count 2 (RETRO-231 §4c TG-2 + this §5a), still NO
  amendment proposed.** The byte-identical triplet did *not* diverge (§5a) and the duplication grew
  asymmetric. Recorded as count 2 toward a future K.1 scope-broadening amendment for **gate/tooling
  code**; the amendment itself belongs to FOLLOW-725's decision, not to a retro.
- **L-1 (observation, and the sharpest thing in this retro).** **An audit that produces a "safe"
  verdict is itself an assertion, and it inherits every failure mode of the code it audits.**
  FOLLOW-723's AC-3 asked for an audit; the audit was performed conscientiously, its counts were all
  correct (`grep -c` → 1 at both flagged sites — I re-ran both), and **two of its verdicts are
  nonetheless wrong**, because each reasoned about *the count of matches* rather than *the region the
  consumer reads*. That is P-17 applied to the audit rather than to the code. Generalising: **when a
  ticket's AC is "audit X and record the verdict", the retro's job is to re-derive the verdicts, not
  to check that they were written.** Both P-1-class findings in this retro came from exactly that.
- **L-2 (observation).** Three consecutive PRs in this chain (#638, #639, #640) were verified by
  their author against the scenario the ticket names, and in all three a **different scenario from
  the same class** was still broken. RETRO-231 §6 L-1 named the counter-measure (run it against the
  next queued ticket). This retro adds the second half: **also run it against the sites the PR
  declared safe without changing.** Unchanged code carrying a new "checked" comment is the least
  scrutinised artifact a PR can ship.

### 7. Follow-ups

- **FOLLOW-726** (P1, backend-engineer, 3h) — region-scope `check-consent-text-sync.mjs`'s `libSrc`

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P2) — the localhost failure mode this ticket exists to expose is SILENT, and the recorded
  AC5 diagnosis attributes it to the wrong dependency.** `apps/intent-engine/src/nlp.py:318-332`:
  `extract_intent` is documented "Never raises" and catches `Exception` → `print(...)` →
  `_neutral_payload(...)` (`nlp.py:202-218`: all 12 dims `None`, `confidence=0.0`,
  `archetype_hint="neutral"`). The only uncaught dependency is
  `redis_writer._get_redis()`'s `os.environ["UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL"]` (`redis_writer.py:35`).
  Reproduced against the merged shim, not reasoned about:

  ```
  # no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, no UPSTASH_* :
  extract_intent error model=claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 source=realtime: 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'
  RAISED: KeyError KeyError('UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL')      ← this is the 500, NOT Anthropic

  # UPSTASH_* valid, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY still absent :
  HTTP: 202 {"status":"accepted"}
  KEY WRITTEN: shadow:t:s:chat_intent
  archetype_hint: neutral | confidence: 0.0 | all dims null: True
  ```

  Consequence, and it lands squarely on Piotr's standing priority: **the operator who provisions
  Upstash first (the harder credential) and Anthropic second gets a green 202, a present shadow key,
  and zero archetype movement** — which reads exactly like "chat doesn't affect the archetype", the
  highest-cost false-bug trail in this loop. This is a **Rule K.2** instance ("swallows an error and
  substitutes plausible-looking default data … a neutral response"; `CONVENTIONS_PATCH.md:509-513`)
  and it is additionally un-Sentried despite `sentry-sdk>=2.0` being a declared dependency
  (`pyproject.toml:15`) — the signal is a bare `print`.
  **Pre-existing in `nlp.py`, NOT introduced by this PR** — but this PR is the one that makes it the
  first thing a human meets on localhost, and the PR/QUEUE/FOLLOW_UPS record of AC5 ("a real POST
  500s on the missing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`") is falsified by the trace above. → **FOLLOW-730**.
  Blast radius CHECKED and bounded: `flattenIntentDimensions`
  (`apps/control-plane/src/lib/chat-intent-cache.ts:176-191`) skips nulls → `{}`, and
  `adapt.ts:869-880` gates on `Object.keys(dims).length > 0`, so a neutral write does **not** poison

  (`adapt.ts:877,888`). The damage is diagnostic, not correctness.

- **LG-2 (P3) — the sync-vs-spawn divergence is documented as a MECHANISM but not as a
  CONSEQUENCE.** `local_dev.py:32-42` and `README.md:73-74` both state the shim writes synchronously
  while prod spawns. Neither states what that costs: prod has a real write/read race (the SDK's next
  `/api/adapt` may hit `readShadowChatIntent` before the Modal container finishes), so
  "the first chat message's intent isn't visible until a later adapt call" is a **prod-only class
  that structurally cannot reproduce on the shim**. Verified benign for correctness (an absent key
  yields `dims={}` → skip → gate not burned), so this is a fidelity/expectation gap, not a bug.
  Latency: no breach — §C.3's `<500ms` budget is "message send → intent vector update"
  (`MASTER_DESIGN.md:1653`) which the shim meets more directly than prod, and the ingest ACK budget
  is unaffected because `dispatchChatNlp` runs inside `ctx.waitUntil()`
  (`chat-nlp-dispatch.ts:5-7`). Folded into **FOLLOW-733**.

- **LG-3 (P2, structural — the step-7 finding) — the wire closed one hop and the gap moved
  downstream, and 2 of the 3 remaining hops fail invisibly.** Traced the full chain
  producer→consumer→render for localhost at merge commit `6f12174`:

  Hop 5 is the specific trap the PM flagged: `docs/runbooks/upstash-redis-env-parity.md:36-40`

### 5. Cascading impact

#### 5a. Current sprint tickets affected

**None.** `backlog/QUEUE.md:119` records **0 tickets IN_PROGRESS** at merge (FOLLOW-729 was the only
one and is DONE). The held set on ESC-044 (FOLLOW-704, 706, 710, 711, 701, 714) is consent-domain
and untouched by a Python-only intent-engine diff — re-verified, not inherited. No READY ticket's
assumptions are invalidated: nothing in the queue asserts "intent-engine cannot run locally".

#### 5b. Future sprint tickets affected

- **`apps/llm-gateway` has TWO endpoints with the byte-identical structural problem**, and the brief's
  premise needed narrowing:
  `grep -rn "fastapi_endpoint" --include=*.py apps/` returns exactly three production endpoints —
  `apps/intent-engine/src/main.py:108` (closed by this PR),

  they do not share this problem. The cascade is 2 endpoints in 1 app, not 3 apps.
- Consequence for Piotr's "100% end-to-end on localhost" goal: **FOLLOW-729 closed 1 of 3** Modal HTTP
  endpoints. `description_requested_endpoint` is the AI-description generator — as central to the

  Modal app. Copied as-is twice more it multiplies TG-2/TG-3: three ungated `_valid_bearer` copies
  plus three ungated validation blocks, in a repo whose Rule J exists specifically because that
  compounds. A generalize-or-accept decision is cheap NOW and expensive after the second copy. →
  **FOLLOW-734**.

#### 5c. Contracts changed others rely on

- `POST {MODAL_CHAT_NLP_URL}` now has **two** independent server implementations against **one**
  producer, with no shared fixture (TG-1). The next editor of `chat-nlp-dispatch.ts`'s body literal

#### 5d. Architectural assumptions affected — **PM ACTION RECOMMENDED, severity HIGH**

- **The credentials gap is the last hop of a CEO-stated priority and is tracked only in prose.**
  FOLLOW-729's own AC5 pre-authorised the remedy — *"escalate the credentials gap separately if

  the verdict MUST split the code axis from the operator axis with a fail-loud proof step —

### 6. New lesson candidates

- **Pattern "SAME-RUNTIME DECLARED-IDENTICAL DUPLICATE IN THE Rule J / Rule K.1 GAP" — count 2
  (1 PRIOR retro). THRESHOLD NOT MET → NOT PROMOTED.** RETRO-231 §6 recorded this as a
  "Rule J / Rule K.1 scope-boundary sighting, count 1, no amendment proposed yet" for the three
  byte-identical helpers across two `scripts/*.mjs` gates (→ FOLLOW-725). This retro is the second
  sighting and a genuinely different shape: **Python, intra-app, and PARTIAL** — a whole function
  (`_valid_bearer`) plus an inline 24-line block inside a larger function, not a whole-file mirror.
  The house counting convention (RETRO-232 §6: "count 3, = 2 PRIOR RETROS. THRESHOLD MET") puts this
  at 1 prior retro, one short. Explicitly holding. What the third sighting should carry, so the
  eventual amendment is not under-scoped: **(a)** a comparison strategy that is language-agnostic
  (the current `check-mirror-files.sh` cannot express Python — `strip_comments()` at `:33-40` strips
  `/* */`+`//`, the fallback greps `^(export )?(async )?function`), and **(b)** a strategy for a
  REGION of a file rather than a whole file, since neither RETRO-231's nor this instance is a
  file-level mirror. §5b says the third sighting is likely to arrive as the llm-gateway copy of
  `local_dev.py` — if so it is the same instance multiplied, and I will need to decide whether N
  copies of one PR's decision count once or N times. Recording that question now so the next retro
  does not have to re-derive it.
- **Rule K.2 — instance sighting, no promotion needed (already codified).** LG-1 is a textbook K.2
  fabricate-instead-of-fail: neutral payload substituted for a failed extraction, `print` instead of
  Sentry, and — the K.2 clause that bites hardest here — **no provenance marker on the wire**, so
  neither the shadow key nor the 202 distinguishes "the buyer said nothing archetype-bearing" from
  "the model call died". K.2's own amendment history (`:552-564`) is three retros of exactly this
  sub-shape: the degraded signal emitted with no schema slot. Here it is not even emitted.
  FOLLOW-730 is written against K.2 rather than proposing anything new.
- **Rule AF — the count moved again: 179 → 183 → 191 → 192.** Rule I is at 192 on this PR and
  `failure` on `main`, so this merge complied with AF's actual requirement (compare the known-red set
  to `main`'s baseline, find it UNCHANGED) — the PM did that and I re-derived it independently
  (§2). But AF was promoted at RETRO-205 on evidence of exactly this drift, and the number has
  incremented once more since. The specific erosion this retro can attest to: **I could not use
  "CI green" as a signal at all** — I had to fetch the job log, read `Violations found : 192`, and
  fetch `main`'s check-runs to establish that 192 was not 191+1-from-this-PR. That is three API
  calls of ceremony per merge to recover a boolean, and it is the mechanism by which "some red is
  normal" becomes load-bearing. No new rule (AF covers it); recording the count so the next retro
  has the series. Not filing a stub — FOLLOW-591/602 already exist for the remediation.
- **Process/meta — the recovery-discipline hypothesis is FALSIFIED; no documentation gap.** The PM
  flagged the terminal-close recovery (worker output surviving as uncommitted changes in the MAIN
  working tree) as a possible third variant undocumented outside operator memory. It is documented:
  `docs/AGENT_WORKFLOW.md:171-181` describes this exact variant — *"before ever running
  `git checkout -b`* — the edits sat uncommitted directly in the `main` working tree"* — and
  `:193-212` is a mandatory **"Recovered-work re-verification"** procedure whose step 1 is *"if it's
  sitting uncommitted on `main`, move it"* and whose step 3 requires the recovering party to run its
  own verification pass because *"a worker that crashed produced zero verification"*. The PM
  followed both. **No stub filed** — writing one would have been a manufactured finding, and the
  more useful record is that this convention has now been exercised and held.
- **Process/meta — ticket design foreclosed the best option, and the retro nearly inherited the
  worker's framing.** FOLLOW-729 AC1 offered a binary: *import `main.py`'s logic, or duplicate it
  with a keep-in-step comment*. The worker verified the first is impossible and took the second, and
  its reasoning is correct (§2, re-derived here). But the binary omits option (c): **extract the
  auth+validation contract into a sibling module (`src/http_contract.py`) that BOTH import** — which
  has nothing to do with Modal decorators and is feasible, since `main.py` already relies on sibling
  modules resolving inside the Modal container (`main.py:76-77` imports `nlp`/`redis_writer` at call
  time). Option (c) was foreclosed not by Modal but by **AC4** ("no change to `main.py`"). Lesson for
  ticket authors, and for me: *when a ticket offers "reuse X or duplicate X", the third option —
  extract X — is usually invisible because the ticket named X as the thing to reuse.* The
  duplication here is therefore a scoping artifact, not a technical necessity, and FOLLOW-732 says so
  explicitly so the next editor does not inherit "we had to".

### 4. Discovered gaps

#### 4a. Logic gaps

- **LG-1 (P2) — `schemas.py:20-21`'s claim "One value per code path in `nlp.extract_intent` that can
  produce a payload — nothing here is inferred or decorative" is FALSE.** Three distinct producer
  paths all emit `data_source="model"`: the primary parse (`nlp.py:441`), the successful Sonnet retry
  (`nlp.py:543`, a _different model_), and the two failed-retry arms (`nlp.py:552`, `nlp.py:575`)
  which return a Haiku read carrying a `retry_failed:` marker. That is a **Rule Y** citation defect in
  a comment that exists specifically to make provenance auditable, and it is why HW-1's `retry_failed`
  case fell out of every consumer's filter. → FOLLOW-740.
- **LG-2 (P3) — the `data_source` default fails in the GREEN direction.** `schemas.py:118`
  (`data_source: ChatIntentDataSource = "model"`) means any _future_ construction of
  `ChatIntentDetectedPayload` that forgets the stamp is silently labelled "a real model read" — the
  exact fail-green this ticket exists to remove. The PR's stated mitigation (required keyword-only arg
  on `_neutral_payload`) guards only that one helper; direct construction sites bypass it (2 today,
  `nlp.py:237` and `nlp.py:430`, both explicit — so this is latent, not live). The default is
  nonetheless _correct_ for legacy-JSON compatibility, so the fix is a construction-site guard, not a
  different default. → FOLLOW-740.
- **LG-3 (P3, latent) — the batch tier can clobber a fresher realtime read, and ADR-0020 names that a
  non-goal.** `jobs/batch_enrich.py` writes the SAME shadow key with `source="batch"` on a 6h cron; a
  non-empty batch write is an unconditional `SET` under both current behaviour and ADR-0020's spec
  (D7 explicitly parks `detected_at`-monotonic ordering). Correctly out of scope and correctly named
  as a non-goal; recorded because it stops being latent the moment FOLLOW-101 implements
  `read_recent_chat_sessions`. No stub — ADR-0020 D7 owns the decision.

#### 4b. Code bugs not caught (P0/P1/P2)

- **CB-1 (P1) — the compliance exposure closed in review round 2 has a second, still-open channel,
  and the doc control asserted to cover it does not exist.** Round 2 correctly set
  `include_local_variables=False` (`nlp.py:322-336`) so Sentry stops serialising frames holding
  `messages`/`raw_text`. But `capture_exception(exc)` still transmits the **exception value string**,
  and this PR's own C-07 edit concedes it: _"the exception message, **which could echo prompt text**,
  goes to the log line and the Sentry event"_ (`docs/compliance/C-07-chat-retention-scope.md:222`).
  Meanwhile `docs/compliance/ropa.md:444` asserts Sentry receives _"Stack traces, request context
  (scrubbed of PII before transmission per Sentry SDK `beforeSend` hook with PII patterns regex;
  verification: **CI check on scrubber config** + annual audit)"_, and `dpia.md:157` / `dpia.md:224`
  repeat it ("scrubbed of PII via SDK `beforeSend` hook; **CI-verified**").
  **`grep -rn "beforeSend\|before_send" --include=*.ts --include=*.py --include=*.mjs --include=*.cjs --include=*.yml . | grep -v node_modules`
  returns ZERO hits repo-wide** — across all four Sentry init sites (`nlp.py:337`,
  `consume_embed_seed_requests.py:195,395`, `schema_validation.py:354`,
  `apps/control-plane/sentry.server.config.ts:18`). The scrubber does not exist and neither does its
  CI check. This is pre-existing doc-vs-code drift, but PR #642 makes it **newly load-bearing**: it
  adds a fourth producer under that assertion, on the one data path whose binding constraint is _"no
  free text, no message content"_. Rule N + Rule AI (ropa.md WAS edited in this PR — the retention row
  — but line 444 was not). → FOLLOW-739 (docs/truth) + FOLLOW-738 (the control itself).
- **CB-2 (P2) — Rule S sibling-completeness: the round-2 compliance hardening was applied to 1 of 4

- **DG-1 (P2) — ADR-0020 §D6 lists three visibility channels for a suppressed degraded write; two of
